children.text: Tantrasāra, Prathamam āhnikam
children.translated_text: <s>Tantrasāra</s>, First Chapter (<s>Āhnika</s>)

children.text: vimalakalāśrayābhinavasṛṣṭimahā jananī bharitatanuś ca pañcamukhaguptarucir janakaḥ /
children.translated_text: The Mother of the great creation, who is the abode of the pure <s>kalā</s> (creative power), newly emanated, and the Father, whose body is full, whose splendor is concealed within the five mouths—

children.text: tadubhayayāmalasphuritabhāvavisargamayaṃ hṛdayam anuttarāmṛtakulaṃ mama saṃsphuratāt // AbhTs_1.1
children.translated_text: may that Heart, which consists of the <s>visarga</s> (creative emission) flashing forth from the union (<s>yāmala</s>) of those two, which is the family of the unsurpassed nectar (<s>anuttarāmṛtakula</s>), pulsate within me. [AbhTs 1.1]

children.text: vitatas tantrāloko vigāhituṃ naiva śakyate sarvaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The extensive <s>Tantrāloka</s> cannot be fathomed by all;

children.text: ṛjuvacanaviracitam idaṃ tu tantrasāraṃ tataḥ śṛṇuta // AbhTs_1.2
children.translated_text: therefore hear this <s>Tantrasāra</s>, composed in straightforward language. [AbhTs 1.2]

children.text: śrīśambhunāthabhāskaracaraṇanipātaprabhāpagatasaṃkocam /
children.translated_text: The lotus of <s>Abhinavagupta</s>'s heart, whose contraction has been removed by the radiance falling from the feet of the illustrious <s>Śambhunātha</s> and <s>Bhāskara</s>—

children.text: abhinavaguptahṛdambujam etad vicinuta maheśapūjanahetoḥ // AbhTs_1.3
children.translated_text: examine this [work] for the sake of worshipping <s>Maheśa</s> (the Great Lord). [AbhTs 1.3]

body.text:
iha jñānaṃ mokṣakāraṇaṃ bandhanimittasya ajñānasya virodhakatvāt dvividhaṃ ca ajñānaṃ buddhigataṃ pauruṣaṃ ca tatra buddhigatam aniścayasvabhāvaṃ viparītaniścayātmakaṃ ca /
pauruṣaṃ tu vikalpasvabhāvaṃ saṃkucitaprathātmakaṃ tad eva ca mūlakāraṇaṃ saṃsārasya iti vakṣyāmo malanirṇaye /
tatra pauruṣam ajñānaṃ dīkṣādinā nivartetāpi kiṃ tu dīkṣāpi buddhigate anadhyavasāyātmake ajñāne sati na sambhavati heyopādeyaniścayapūrvakatvāt tattvaśuddhiśivayojanārūpāyā dīkṣāyā iti /
tatra adhyavasāyātmakaṃ buddhiniṣṭham eva jñānaṃ pradhānam tad eva ca abhyasyamānaṃ pauruṣam api ajñānaṃ nihanti vikalpasaṃvidabhyāsasya avikalpāntatāparyavasānāt /
vikalpāsaṃkucitasaṃvitprakāśarūpo hy ātmā śivasvabhāva iti sarvathā samastavastuniṣṭhaṃ samyaṅniścayātmakaṃ jñānam upādeyam /
tac ca śāstrapūrvakam /
śāstraṃ ca parameśvarabhāṣitam eva pramāṇam /
aparaśāstroktānām arthānāṃ tatra vaiviktyena abhyupagamāt tadarthātiriktayuktisiddhanirūpaṇāc ca tena aparāgamoktaṃ jñānaṃ tāvata eva bandhāt vimocakam na sarvasmāt sarvasmāt tu vimocakaṃ parameśvaraśāstraṃ pañcasrotomayaṃ daśāṣṭādaśavasvaṣṭabhedabhinnam /
tato 'pi sarvasmāt sāraṃ ṣaḍardhaśāstrāṇi /
tebhyo 'pi mālinīvijayam /
tadantargataś cārthaḥ saṃkalayyāśakyo nirūpayitum /

children.text: na ca anirūpitavastutattvasya muktatvaṃ mocakatvaṃ vā śuddhasya jñānasyaiva tathārūpatvāt iti /
children.translated_text: And one whose understanding of the true nature of reality has not been ascertained cannot be liberated, nor can he be a liberator—for only pure knowledge has such a nature.

children.text: svabhyastajñānamūlatvāt parapuruṣārthasya tatsiddhaye idam ārabhyate /
children.translated_text: Since the highest human goal has as its root the knowledge that has been practiced by oneself, this [work] is undertaken for its attainment.

children.text: ajñānaṃ kila bandhahetur uditaḥ śāstre malaṃ tat smṛtaṃ pūrṇajñānakalodaye tad akhilaṃ nirmūlatāṃ gacchati /
children.translated_text: Ignorance is indeed declared in scripture to be the cause of bondage; it is called <s>mala</s> (impurity). Upon the arising of the full <s>kalā</s> (power) of knowledge, all of it goes to a state of rootlessness.

children.text: dhvastāśeṣamalātmasaṃvidudaye mokṣaś ca tenāmunā śāstreṇa prakaṭīkaromi nikhilaṃ yaj jñeyatattvaṃ bhavet // AbhTs_1.4
children.translated_text: Upon the arising of awareness whose nature is the Self, with all <s>mala</s> destroyed, there is liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). Therefore, by means of this scripture, I shall make manifest everything that is the true nature of what is to be known. [AbhTs 1.4]

children.text:
tatra iha svabhāva eva paramopādeyaḥ sa ca sarvabhāvānāṃ prakāśarūpa eva aprakāśasya svabhāvatānupapatteḥ sa ca nānekaḥ prakāśasya taditarasvabhāvānupraveśāyoge svabhāvabhedābhāvāt deśakālāv api ca asya na bhedakau tayor api tatprakāśasvabhāvatvāt iti eka eva prakāśaḥ sa eva ca saṃvit arthaprakāśarūpā hi saṃvit iti sarveṣām atra avivāda eva /
sa ca prakāśo na paratantraḥ prakāśyataiva hi pāratantryam prakāśyatā ca prakāśāntarāpekṣitaiva na ca prakāśāntaraṃ kiṃcit asti iti svatantra ekaḥ prakāśaḥ svātantryād eva ca deśakālākārāvacchedavirahāt vyāpako nityaḥ sarvākāranirākārasvabhāvaḥ tasya ca svātantryam ānandaśaktiḥ taccamatkāra icchāśaktiḥ prakāśarūpatā cicchaktiḥ āmarśātmakatā jñānaśaktiḥ sarvākārayogitvaṃ kriyāśaktiḥ ity evaṃ mukhyābhiḥ śaktibhiḥ yukto 'pi vastuta icchājñānakriyāśaktiyuktaḥ anavacchinnaḥ prakāśo nijānandaviśrāntaḥ śivarūpaḥ sa eva svātantryāt ātmānaṃ saṃkucitam avabhāsayan aṇur iti ucyate /
children.translated_text: Now, herein, it is one's own essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) that is supremely to be adopted. And that [essential nature] of all things is nothing but the form of luminous awareness (<s>prakāśa</s>), since what is non-luminous cannot possibly be one's essential nature. And it is not many, because, in the impossibility of luminous awareness entering into what is other than itself, there is no differentiation of its essential nature. Nor do space and time differentiate it, since those too have luminous awareness as their essential nature. Thus there is only one luminous awareness. And that is consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>), for consciousness is indeed the form of illuminating objects—about this there is no dispute at all. And that luminous awareness is not dependent on another, for dependence consists precisely in being illuminated [by another]; and being illuminated requires another light; but there is no other light whatsoever. Therefore, one luminous awareness is autonomous (<s>svatantra</s>). And precisely because of its autonomy, being free from limitation by space, time, and form, it is all-pervading, eternal, of the nature of all forms and formlessness. Its autonomy is the power of bliss (<s>ānandaśakti</s>); its wonder is the power of will (<s>icchāśakti</s>); its luminous nature is the power of consciousness (<s>cicchakti</s>); its nature as reflective awareness (<s>āmarśa</s>) is the power of knowledge (<s>jñānaśakti</s>); its capacity to assume all forms is the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>). Thus, though endowed with these primary powers, in reality it is endowed with the powers of will, knowledge, and action—unlimited luminous awareness, resting in its own bliss, having the nature of <s>Śiva</s>. That very [awareness], through its autonomy, manifesting itself as contracted, is called <s>aṇu</s> (the limited individual self).

children.text: punar api ca svātmānaṃ svatantratayā prakāśayati yena anavacchinnaprakāśaśivarūpatayaiva prakāśate /
children.translated_text: And again, it illuminates its own Self autonomously, whereby it shines as having the very nature of <s>Śiva</s>, whose luminous awareness is unlimited.

children.text: tatrāpi svātantryavaśāt anupāyam eva svātmānaṃ prakāśayati sopāyaṃ vā sopāyatve 'pi icchā vā jñānaṃ vā kriyā vā abhyupāya iti traividhyaṃ śāmbhavaśāktāṇavabhedena samāveśasya tatra caturvidham api etad rūpaṃ krameṇa atra upadiśyate /
children.translated_text: Therein too, by the force of its autonomy, it illuminates its own Self either without any means (<s>anupāya</s>) or with means (<s>sopāya</s>). And when with means, the means is either will (<s>icchā</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), or action (<s>kriyā</s>)—thus there is a threefold [distinction of] <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption), corresponding to <s>Śāmbhava</s>, <s>Śākta</s>, and <s>Āṇava</s>. Even this fourfold form [including anupāya] is taught here in sequence.

children.text: ātmā prakāśavapur eṣa śivaḥ svatantraḥ svātantryanarmarabhasena nijaṃ svarūpam /
children.translated_text: This Self, whose body is luminous awareness, is <s>Śiva</s>, autonomous; through the play of his autonomy, his own nature—

children.text: saṃchādya yat punar api prathayeta pūrṇaṃ tac ca kramākramavaśād athavā tribhedāt // AbhTs_1.5
children.translated_text: having concealed [it], when he again manifests it fully, that [occurs] either through sequence and non-sequence, or through the threefold [division]. [AbhTs 1.5]

body.translated_text: Here, knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is the cause of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>), because it is the counteragent of ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>), which is the cause of bondage. And ignorance is twofold: that which pertains to the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) and that which pertains to the self (<s>puruṣa</s>). Of these, intellectual ignorance has the nature of indeterminacy and of erroneous determination. The personal (self-related) ignorance, however, has the nature of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) and the nature of contracted manifestation—and this alone is the root cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), as we shall explain in the section on the determination of <s>mala</s> (impurity). Therein, the personal ignorance may be removed through <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) and the like; but <s>dīkṣā</s> itself is not possible when there exists intellectual ignorance in the form of non-determination, since <s>dīkṣā</s>—which takes the form of purification of the <s>tattva</s>s (principles) and union with <s>Śiva</s>—is preceded by the determination of what is to be rejected and what is to be adopted. Therefore, the primary [type of] knowledge is that which is intellectual in nature and has the form of determination. And this very [knowledge], when practiced, also destroys the personal ignorance, because the practice of conceptual awareness (<s>vikalpa-saṃvid</s>) culminates in the non-conceptual (<s>avikalpa</s>). For the Self, whose nature is the light of awareness (<s>saṃvit-prakāśa</s>) unconstricted by conceptual construction, has the nature of <s>Śiva</s>. Therefore, in every respect, the knowledge to be adopted is that which has the form of correct determination regarding all things. And this is preceded by scripture (<s>śāstra</s>). And the authoritative scripture is only that which is spoken by the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>). Since the meanings stated in other scriptures are accepted there with variation, and since [our scripture] also establishes through reasoning truths beyond the scope of those other scriptures—therefore, the knowledge proclaimed by other <s>āgama</s>s liberates only from that much bondage, not from all; but the scripture of the Supreme Lord, which consists of the five streams, divided into ten, eighteen, and sixty-four divisions, liberates from all [bondage]. And among all of those, the essence is the six-and-a-half scriptures (<s>ṣaḍardhaśāstra</s>). And of those, the <s>Mālinīvijaya</s> [is supreme]. The meaning contained within it cannot be examined in a collected form.

children.text: atha anupāyam eva tāvat vyākhyāsyāmaḥ // AbhTs_2.1
children.translated_text: Now, first we shall explain <s>anupāya</s> (the means-less means). [AbhTs 2.1]

children.text: yadā khalu dṛḍhaśaktipātāviddhaḥ svayam eva itthaṃ vivecayati sakṛd eva guruvacanam avadhārya tadā punar upāyavirahito nityoditaḥ asya samāveśaḥ // AbhTs_2.2
children.translated_text: When indeed one who has been pierced by an intense descent of power (<s>śaktipāta</s>) discerns thus by himself, having grasped the guru's word just once—then, devoid of any means, his absorption (<s>samāveśa</s>) is eternally arisen. [AbhTs 2.2]

children.text: atra ca tarka eva yogāṅgam iti kathaṃ vivecayati iti cet ucyate yo 'yaṃ parameśvaraḥ svaprakāśarūpaḥ svātmā tatra kim upāyena kriyate na svarūpalābho nityatvāt na jñaptiḥ svayaṃprakāśamānatvāt nāvaraṇavigamaḥ āvaraṇasya kasyacid api asaṃbhavāt na tadanupraveśaḥ anupraveṣṭuḥ vyatiriktasya abhāvāt // AbhTs_2.3
children.translated_text: Here, reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) itself is the limb of yoga. How does he discern? It is said: This Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), who has the form of self-luminous awareness, is one's own Self. What is accomplished there by any means? Not the attainment of one's own nature, because it is eternal. Not making it known, because it is self-luminous. Not the removal of a covering, because no covering whatsoever is possible. Not entry into it, because there is nothing separate that could enter. [AbhTs 2.3]

children.text: kaś cātra upāyaḥ tasyāpi vyatiriktasya anupapatteḥ tasmāt samastam idam ekaṃ cinmātratattvaṃ kālena akalitaṃ deśena aparicchinnam upādhibhir amlānam ākṛtibhir aniyantritaṃ śabdair asaṃdiṣṭaṃ pramāṇair aprapañcitaṃ kālādeḥ pramāṇaparyantasya svecchayaiva svarūpalābhanimittaṃ ca svatantram ānandaghanaṃ tattvaṃ tad eva ca aham tatraiva antar mayi viśvaṃ pratibimbitam evaṃ dṛḍhaṃ viviñcānasya śaśvad eva pārameśvaraḥ samāveśo nirupāyaka eva tasya ca na mantrapūjādhyānacaryādiniyantraṇā kācit // AbhTs_2.4
children.translated_text: And what means could there be here? For a means too cannot possibly be separate from it. Therefore, all of this is one single reality whose nature is pure consciousness (<s>cinmātra</s>)—uncalculated by time, unlimited by space, untarnished by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>), unconfined by forms, undesignated by words, unelaborated by means of knowledge—and [all things] from time to the means of knowledge exist because of its own will, for the sake of the realization of its own nature. [This reality is] autonomous, a dense mass of bliss (<s>ānandaghana</s>). And that is I myself. Within me the universe is reflected. For one who discerns thus firmly, the absorption into the Supreme Lord is forever, entirely without means. And for that [absorption], there is no restriction whatsoever of <s>mantra</s>, worship (<s>pūjā</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), observance (<s>caryā</s>), or the like. [AbhTs 2.4]

children.text: yad etat prakāśarūpaṃ śivatattvam uktam tatra akhaṇḍamaṇḍale yadā praveṣṭuṃ na śaknoti tadā svātantryaśaktim eva adhikāṃ paśyan nirvikalpam eva bhairavasamāveśam anubhavati ayaṃ ca asya upadeśaḥ sarvam idaṃ bhāvajātaṃ bodhagagane pratibimbamātraṃ pratibimbalakṣaṇopetatvāt idaṃ hi pratibimbasya lakṣaṇaṃ yat bhedena bhāsitam aśaktam anyavyāmiśratvenaiva bhāti tat pratibimbam mukharūpam iva darpaṇe rasa iva dantodake gandha iva ghrāṇa mithunasparśa iva ānandendriye śūlakuntādisparśo vā antaḥsparśanendriye pratiśrutkeva vyomni // AbhTs_3.1
children.translated_text: That which has been called the <s>Śiva</s>-principle, whose form is luminous awareness—when one is unable to enter that undivided sphere, then, seeing the power of autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>) as predominant, one experiences the absorption into <s>Bhairava</s> that is itself non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpa</s>). And this is the instruction for it: this entire world of entities is a mere reflection in the sky of awareness (<s>bodhagagana</s>), because it possesses the characteristic of a reflection. For this is the characteristic of a reflection: that which appears as separate, unable [to exist independently], shines only as intermixed with another—that is a reflection. Like a face in a mirror; like taste in dental water; like smell in the organ of smell; like the touch of union in the organ of bliss; or like the touch of a spear, lance, etc., in the inner organ of touch; or like an echo in space. [AbhTs 3.1]

children.text: na hi sa raso mukhyaḥ tatkāryavyādhiśamanādyadṛṣṭeḥ // AbhTs_3.2
children.translated_text: For that taste is not primary, since the effects [of the primary substance] such as curing illness are not seen [in the reflection]. [AbhTs 3.2]

children.text: nāpi gandhasparśau mukhyau guṇinaḥ tatra abhāve tayor ayogāt kāryaparamparānārambhāt ca // AbhTs_3.3
children.translated_text: Nor are the [reflected] smell and touch primary, for in the absence of the substance possessing qualities, they are impossible, and because there is no commencement of a chain of effects. [AbhTs 3.3]

children.text: na ca tau na staḥ dehoddhūlanavisargādidarśanāt // AbhTs_3.4
children.translated_text: Nor do they not exist, as is seen from the dusting of the body, emission, and the like. [AbhTs 3.4]

children.text: śabdo 'pi na mukhyaḥ ko 'pi vakti iti āgacchantyā iva pratiśrutkāyāḥ śravaṇāt // AbhTs_3.5
children.translated_text: Sound too is not primary, as one hears from an echo, as if someone says 'Come!' [AbhTs 3.5]

children.text: evaṃ yathā etat pratibimbitaṃ bhāti tathaiva viśvaṃ parameśvaraprakāśe // AbhTs_3.6
children.translated_text: Thus, just as these [reflections] appear as reflected, so too the universe [appears] in the luminous awareness of the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>). [AbhTs 3.6]

children.text: nanu atra bimbaṃ kiṃ syāt mābhūt kiṃcit // AbhTs_3.7
children.translated_text: But what would be the original (<s>bimba</s>) here? Let there be nothing [as an original]. [AbhTs 3.7]

children.text: nanu kim akāraṇakaṃ tat hanta tarhi hetupraśnaḥ tat kiṃ bimbavācoyuktyā hetuś ca parameśvaraśaktir eva svātantryāparaparyāyā bhaviṣyati viśvapratibimbadhāritvāc ca viśvātmakatvaṃ bhagavataḥ saṃvinmayaṃ hi viśvaṃ caitanyasya vyaktisthānam iti tad eva hi viśvam atra pratīpam iti pratibimbadhāritvam asya tac ca tāvat viśvātmakatvaṃ parameśvarasya svarūpaṃ na anāmṛṣṭaṃ bhavati citsvabhāvasya svarūpānāmarśanānupapatteḥ // AbhTs_3.8
children.translated_text: But is it then without a cause? Well then, the question of cause [is this]: the cause, by the reasoning of the term 'original' (<s>bimba</s>), will be none other than the power of the Supreme Lord, synonymous with autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>). And because it bears the reflection of the universe, the Lord's nature as the totality of the universe [follows]. For the universe consists of consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>); it is the locus of manifestation of consciousness. Therefore, this same universe in its inverted form—this constitutes [the Lord's] bearing of reflection. And this nature as the totality of the universe, which is the essential nature of the Supreme Lord, is not un-cognized, since it is impossible for one whose nature is consciousness not to cognize one's own nature. [AbhTs 3.8]

children.text: svarūpānāmarśane hi vastuto jaḍataiva syāt āmarśaś ca ayaṃ na sāketikaḥ api tu citsvabhāvatāmātranāntarīyakaḥ paranādagarbha uktaḥ sa ca yāvān viśvavyavasthāpakaḥ parameśvarasya śaktikalāpaḥ tāvantam āmṛśati // AbhTs_3.9
children.translated_text: For if one's own nature were not cognized, there would in reality be mere insentience. And this cognition (<s>āmarśa</s>) is not conventional; rather, it is inseparable from the very nature of consciousness, and is said to contain the supreme resonance (<s>paranāda</s>). And this [cognition] cognizes as much as is the entire cluster of powers of the Supreme Lord that establishes the universe. [AbhTs 3.9]

children.text: tatra mukhyās tāvat tisraḥ parameśvarasya śaktayaḥ anuttarecchonmeṣa iti tad eva parāmarśatrayam a i u iti etasmād eva tritayāt sarvaḥ śaktiprapañcaḥ caryate anuttara eva hi viśrāntir ānandaḥ icchāyām eva viśrāntiḥ īśanam unmeṣa eva hi viśrāntir ūrmiḥ yaḥ kriyāśakteḥ prārambhaḥ tad eva parāmarśatrayam ā ī ū iti // AbhTs_3.10
children.translated_text: Among those, the primary powers of the Supreme Lord are three: <s>Anuttara</s> (the Unsurpassed), <s>Icchā</s> (Will), and <s>Unmeṣa</s> (Opening/Emergence). These are the three reflective cognitions (<s>parāmarśa</s>): a, i, u. From this very triad, the entire elaboration of powers proceeds. In <s>Anuttara</s> itself, the repose is bliss (<s>Ānanda</s>); in Will, the repose is sovereignty (<s>Īśana</s>); in Emergence, the repose is the wave (<s>Ūrmi</s>)—which is the commencement of the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>). These are the three reflective cognitions: ā, ī, ū. [AbhTs 3.10]

children.text: atra ca prācyaṃ parāmarśatrayaṃ prakāśabhāgasāratvāt sūryātmakaṃ caramaṃ parāmarśatrayaṃ viśrāntisvabhāvāhlādaprādhānyāt somātmakam iyati yāvat karmāṃśasya anupraveśo nāsti // AbhTs_3.11
children.translated_text: Here, the former triad of reflective cognitions, being predominantly the essence of the luminous aspect (<s>prakāśa</s>), has the nature of the Sun (<s>Sūrya</s>). The latter triad of reflective cognitions, being predominantly of the nature of repose and delight, has the nature of the Moon (<s>Soma</s>). Up to this point, there is no entry of the action aspect (<s>karmāṃśa</s>). [AbhTs 3.11]

children.text: yadā tu icchāyām īśane ca karma anupraviśati yat tat iṣyamāṇam īśyamāṇam iti ca ucyate tadā asya dvau bhedau prakāśamātreṇa raśrutiḥ viśrāntyā laśrutiḥ ralayoḥ prakāśastambhasvabhāvatvāt iṣyamāṇaṃ ca na bāhyavat sphuṭam sphuṭarūpatve tad eva nirmāṇaṃ syāt na icchā īśanaṃ vā ataḥ asphuṭatvāt eva śrutimātraṃ ralayoḥ na vyañjanavat sthitiḥ // AbhTs_3.12
children.translated_text: But when action enters into Will and Sovereignty—that which is spoken of as 'the object of willing' and 'the object of ruling'—then there are two varieties of it: as pure luminosity (<s>prakāśamātra</s>), the sound 'ra'; with repose, the sound 'la.' Since 'ra' and 'la' have the nature of the stilling of luminosity; and the object of willing is not manifest like an external thing, for if it were fully manifest, it would be [actual] creation (<s>nirmāṇa</s>), not will or sovereignty. Therefore, due to its non-manifestness, 'ra' and 'la' are merely sounds, not consonants with stable existence. [AbhTs 3.12]

children.text: tad etad varṇacatuṣṭayam ubhayacchāyādhāritvāt napuṃsakam ṛ ṝ ḷ ḹ iti // AbhTs_3.13
children.translated_text: This group of four phonemes, because it bears the shade of both [luminosity and repose], is neuter: ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, ḹ. [AbhTs 3.13]

children.text: anuttarānandayoḥ icchādiṣu yadā prasaraḥ tadā varṇadvayam e oṃ iti // AbhTs_3.14
children.translated_text: When <s>Anuttara</s> and <s>Ānanda</s> extend into Will and the rest, then two phonemes [arise]: e, o. [AbhTs 3.14]

children.text: tatrāpi punar anuttarānandasaṃghaṭṭāt varṇadvayam ai au iti // AbhTs_3.15
children.translated_text: And there again, from the conjunction of <s>Anuttara</s> and <s>Ānanda</s>, two phonemes [arise]: ai, au. [AbhTs 3.15]

children.text: sā iyaṃ kriyāśaktiḥ tad eva ca varṇacatuṣṭayam e ai o au iti // AbhTs_3.16
children.translated_text: This is the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>); and these four phonemes are: e, ai, o, au. [AbhTs 3.16]

children.text: tataḥ punaḥ kriyāśaktyante sarvaṃ kāryabhūtaṃ yāvat anuttare pravekṣyati tāvad eva pūrvaṃ saṃvedanasāratayā prakāśamātratvena bindutayā āste am iti // AbhTs_3.17
children.translated_text: Then again, at the end of the power of action, everything that has become effect, before it enters into <s>Anuttara</s>, first abides as the essence of pure awareness, as mere luminosity, as the point (<s>bindu</s>): 'am.' [AbhTs 3.17]

children.text: tatas tatraiva anuttarasya visargo jāyate aḥ iti // AbhTs_3.18
children.translated_text: Then, in that very [Anuttara], the <s>visarga</s> (creative emission) of <s>Anuttara</s> is born: 'aḥ.' [AbhTs 3.18]

children.text: evaṃ ṣoḍaśakaṃ parāmarśānāṃ bījasvarūpam ucyate // AbhTs_3.19
children.translated_text: Thus, the group of sixteen reflective cognitions is said to be the seed-nature (<s>bīja</s>). [AbhTs 3.19]

children.text: tadutthaṃ vyañjanātmakaṃ yonirūpam // AbhTs_3.20
children.translated_text: That which arises from them, having the nature of consonants (<s>vyañjana</s>), is the womb-form (<s>yoni</s>). [AbhTs 3.20]

children.text: tatra anuttarāt kavargaḥ śraddhāyāḥ icchāyāḥ cavargaḥ sakarmikāyā icchāyā dvau ṭavargas tavargaś ca unmeṣāt pavargaḥ śaktipañcakayogāt pañcakatvam // AbhTs_3.21
children.translated_text: Among them: from <s>Anuttara</s> [comes] the ka-group; from <s>Śraddhā</s> (Faith), i.e., <s>Icchā</s> (Will), the ca-group; from the Will that has an object, the two groups ṭa and ta; from <s>Unmeṣa</s> (Emergence), the pa-group. Their five-fold nature is due to the conjunction of the five powers. [AbhTs 3.21]

children.text: icchāyā eva trividhāyā ya ra lāḥ unmeṣāt vakāraḥ icchāyā eva trividhāyāḥ śa ṣa sāḥ visargāt hakāraḥ yonisaṃyogajaḥ kṣakāraḥ // AbhTs_3.22
children.translated_text: From Will itself in its threefold [aspect come] ya, ra, la; from Emergence, the phoneme va; from Will itself in its threefold [aspect come] śa, ṣa, sa; from <s>visarga</s>, the phoneme ha; born from the union of seed and womb, the phoneme kṣa. [AbhTs 3.22]

children.text: ity eva eṣa bhagavān anuttara eva kuleśvararūpaḥ // AbhTs_3.23
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, this Blessed Lord, in his very <s>Anuttara</s> form, is <s>Kuleśvara</s> (the Lord of the Family). [AbhTs 3.23]

children.text: tasya ca ekaiva kaulikī visargaśaktiḥ yayā ānandarūpāt prabhṛti iyatā bahiḥsṛṣṭiparyantena praspandataḥ vargādiparāmarśā eva bahis tattvarūpatāṃ prāptāḥ // AbhTs_3.24
children.translated_text: And his single <s>Kaulikī</s> power is the power of <s>visarga</s> (emission). By this [power], starting from the form of <s>Ānanda</s> (Bliss) and extending outward to the limit of external creation, the reflective cognitions beginning with the phoneme groups have attained the status of external <s>tattva</s>s (principles). [AbhTs 3.24]

children.text: sa ca eṣa visargas tridhā āṇavaḥ cittaviśrāntirūpaḥ śāktaḥ cittasaṃbodhalakṣaṇaḥ śāṃbhavaḥ cittapralayarūpaḥ iti // AbhTs_3.25
children.translated_text: And this <s>visarga</s> (emission) is threefold: <s>Āṇava</s> (individual), having the form of repose of mind; <s>Śākta</s> (power-related), characterized by the awakening of mind; and <s>Śāmbhava</s> (pertaining to Śiva), having the form of dissolution of mind. [AbhTs 3.25]

children.text: evaṃ visarga eva viśvajanane bhagavataḥ śaktiḥ // AbhTs_3.26
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>visarga</s> (emission) alone is the power of the Lord in the creation of the universe. [AbhTs 3.26]

children.text: ity evam iyato yadā nirvibhāgatayā eva parāmarśaḥ tadā eka eva bhagavān bījayonitayā bhāgaśaḥ parāmarśe śaktimān śaktiś ca // AbhTs_3.27
children.translated_text: Thus, of this [Lord] in this extent, when the reflective cognition (<s>parāmarśa</s>) is in an undivided manner, the Lord is one alone. [But] when reflected upon in parts as seed (<s>bīja</s>) and womb (<s>yoni</s>), [he is] the power-possessor (<s>śaktimān</s>) and the power (<s>śakti</s>). [AbhTs 3.27]

children.text: pṛthak aṣṭakaparāmarśe cakreśvarasāhityena navavargaḥ ekaikaparāmarśaprādhānye pañcāśadātmakatā // AbhTs_3.28
children.translated_text: When reflected upon separately as eight groups, together with the lord of the <s>cakra</s> (circle), [there are] nine classes. When the predominance of each individual reflective cognition [is considered], there is the fifty-fold nature. [AbhTs 3.28]

children.text: tatrāpi sambhavadbhāgabhedaparāmarśane ekāśītirūpatvam // AbhTs_3.29
children.translated_text: And even therein, when the possible subdivisions are reflected upon, there is the eighty-one-fold nature. [AbhTs 3.29]

children.text: vastutas tu ṣaṭ eva parāmarśāḥ prasaraṇapratisaṃcaraṇayogena dvādaśa bhavantaḥ parameśvarasya viśvaśaktipūrṇatvaṃ puṣṇanti // AbhTs_3.30
children.translated_text: But in reality, there are only six reflective cognitions, which, through the conjunction of emanation (<s>prasaraṇa</s>) and withdrawal (<s>pratisaṃcaraṇa</s>), become twelve, nourishing the Supreme Lord's fullness of all universal powers. [AbhTs 3.30]

children.text: tā eva etāḥ parāmarśarūpatvāt śaktayo bhagavatyaḥ śrīkālikā iti niruktāḥ // AbhTs_3.31
children.translated_text: These very powers, because they have the nature of reflective cognition, are called the Blessed Goddesses (<s>Bhagavatyaḥ</s>), known as <s>Śrī Kālikā</s>. [AbhTs 3.31]

children.text: ete ca śaktirūpā eva śuddhāḥ parāmarśāḥ śuddhavidyāyāṃ parāpararūpatvena māyonmeṣamātrasaṃkocāt vidyāvidyeśvararūpatāṃ bhajante // AbhTs_3.32
children.translated_text: And these pure reflective cognitions (<s>parāmarśa</s>), which are of the nature of powers, in <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (Pure Knowledge), through the slight contraction of the first stirring of <s>Māyā</s>, assume the nature of supreme-and-non-supreme (<s>parāpara</s>), taking on the form of <s>Vidyā</s>, <s>Avidyā</s>, and <s>Īśvara</s>. [AbhTs 3.32]

children.text: māyāyāṃ punaḥ sphaṭībhūtabhedavibhāgā māyīyavarṇatāṃ bhajante ye paśyantīmadhyamāvaikharīṣu vyāvahārikatvam āsādya bahīrūpatattvasvabhāvatāpattiparyantāḥ te ca māyīyā api śarīrakalpatvena yadā dṛśyante yadā ca teṣām uktanayair etaiḥ jīvitasthānīyaiḥ śuddhaiḥ parāmarśaiḥ pratyujjīvanaṃ kriyate tadā te savīryā bhavanti te ca tādṛśā bhogamokṣapradāḥ ity evaṃ sakalaparāmarśaviśrāntimātrarūpaṃ pratibimbitasamastatattvabhūtabhuvanabhedam ātmānaṃ paśyato nirvikalpatayā śāṃbhavena samāveśena jīvanmuktatā // AbhTs_3.33
children.translated_text: In <s>Māyā</s> again, with their differentiation and division crystallized, they assume the nature of <s>Māyīya</s> (māyā-born) phonemes. These, attaining conventional usage in <s>Paśyantī</s>, <s>Madhyamā</s>, and <s>Vaikharī</s> [levels of speech], extend down to the point of becoming the nature of external <s>tattva</s>s (principles). And these <s>Māyīya</s> [phonemes], when seen as being like a body, and when they are revivified by the pure reflective cognitions described above—which stand in the place of life—then they become empowered. And in such a state, they bestow both enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). Thus, for one who sees the Self as having the mere form of repose in the totality of reflective cognitions, with the reflected division of all <s>tattva</s>s (principles), worlds, and beings, there is <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living) through the <s>Śāmbhava</s> absorption that is non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpa</s>). [AbhTs 3.33]

children.text: atrāpi pūrvavat na mantrādiyantraṇā kācid iti // AbhTs_3.34
children.translated_text: Here too, as before, there is no restriction whatsoever of <s>mantra</s> and the like. [AbhTs 3.34]

children.text: tatra yadā vikalpaṃ krameṇa saṃskurute samanantaroktasvarūpapraveśāya tadā bhāvanākramasya sattarkasadāgamasadgurūpadeśapūrvakasya asti upayogaḥ // AbhTs_4.1
children.translated_text: When one gradually refines conceptual thought (<s>vikalpa</s>) for the purpose of entering the essential nature just described, then the progressive practice of contemplation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), preceded by sound reasoning (<s>sattarka</s>), valid scripture (<s>sadāgama</s>), and the instruction of a true guru (<s>sadguru</s>), is useful. [AbhTs 4.1]

children.text: tathā hi vikalpabalāt eva jantavo baddham ātmānam abhimanyante sa abhimānaḥ saṃsārapratibandhahetuḥ ataḥ pratidvandvirūpo vikalpa uditaḥ saṃsārahetuṃ vikalpaṃ dalayati iti abhyudayahetuḥ // AbhTs_4.2
children.translated_text: For it is indeed through the force of conceptual thought alone that beings consider the Self to be bound. That false identification (<s>abhimāna</s>) is the cause of obstruction in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therefore, a counter-opposing conceptual thought, once arisen, shatters the conceptual thought that causes <s>saṃsāra</s>—thus it is the cause of spiritual advancement. [AbhTs 4.2]

children.text: sa ca evaṃrūpaḥ samastebhyaḥ paricchinnasvabhāvebhyaḥ śivāntebhyaḥ tattvebhyo yat uttīrṇam aparicchinnasaṃvinmātrarūpaṃ tad eva ca paramārthaḥ tat vastuvyavasthāsthānaṃ tat viśvasya ojaḥ tena prāṇiti viśvam tad eva ca aham ato viśvottīrṇo viśvātmā ca aham iti // AbhTs_4.3
children.translated_text: And it has this form: that which transcends all principles (<s>tattva</s>s), from those of limited nature up to <s>Śiva</s>, whose form is unlimited pure consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>) alone—that is the ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>); that is the ground of the establishment of all things; that is the vital essence (<s>ojas</s>) of the universe; by that the universe lives. And that is I myself. Therefore, I transcend the universe and am also the Self of the universe. [AbhTs 4.3]

children.text: sa ca ayaṃ māyāndhānāṃ na utpadyate sattarkādīnām abhāvāt // AbhTs_4.4
children.translated_text: And this [realization] does not arise for those blinded by <s>Māyā</s>, due to the absence of sound reasoning and the rest. [AbhTs 4.4]

children.text: vaiṣṇavādyā hi tāvanmātra eva āgame rāgatattvena niyamitā iti na ūrdhvadarśane 'pi tadunmukhatāṃ bhajante tataḥ sattarkasadāgamasadgurūpadeśadveṣiṇa eva // AbhTs_4.5
children.translated_text: For <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>s and others, being bound by the <s>rāga-tattva</s> (principle of attachment) in their own scripture to just that extent, do not turn toward the higher vision. Therefore, they are hostile to sound reasoning, valid scripture, and the instruction of a true guru. [AbhTs 4.5]

children.text: yathoktaṃ pārameśvare vaiṣṇavādyāḥ samastās te vidyārāgeṇa rañjitāḥ // AbhTs_4.6
children.translated_text: As it is said in the <s>Pārameśvara</s> [scripture]: 'All those <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>s and others are colored by attachment to [their limited] knowledge (<s>vidyārāga</s>).' [AbhTs 4.6]

children.text: na vindanti paraṃ tattvaṃ sarvajñajñānavarjitāḥ iti // AbhTs_4.7
children.translated_text: 'Devoid of the knowledge of the Omniscient One, they do not find the supreme <s>tattva</s> (reality).' [AbhTs 4.7]

children.text: tasmāt śāṃbhavadṛḍḥaśaktipātāviddhā eva sadāgamādikrameṇa vikalpaṃ saṃskṛtya paraṃ svarūpaṃ praviśanti // AbhTs_4.8
children.translated_text: Therefore, only those pierced by the firm descent of <s>Śāmbhava</s> power (<s>śaktipāta</s>) enter the supreme essential nature by gradually refining conceptual thought through the sequence of valid scripture and the rest. [AbhTs 4.8]

children.text: nanu itthaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ vikalpyarūpaṃ syāt maivam vikalpasya dvaitādhivāsabhaṅgamātre caritārthatvāt paraṃ tattvaṃ tu sarvatra sarvarūpatayā svaprakāśam eva iti na tatra vikalpaḥ kasyaicit upakriyāyai khaṇḍanāyai vā // AbhTs_4.9
children.translated_text: Objection: In this way, the supreme <s>tattva</s> would become an object of conceptualization. Not so—for conceptual thought has fulfilled its purpose merely in the breaking of the habitual impression of duality (<s>dvaitādhivāsa</s>). The supreme <s>tattva</s>, however, shines everywhere as all forms through its own luminous awareness. [AbhTs 4.9]

children.text: tatra atidṛḍhaśaktipātāviddhasya svayam eva sāṃsiddhikatayā sattarka udeti yo 'sau devībhiḥ dīkṣita iti ucyate // AbhTs_4.10
children.translated_text: Therein, for one pierced by an exceedingly firm descent of power, sound reasoning arises spontaneously as an innate accomplishment—such a one is said to be 'initiated by the Goddesses.' [AbhTs 4.10]

children.text: anyasya āgamakrameṇa ityādi savistaraṃ śaktipātaprakāśane vakṣyāmaḥ // AbhTs_4.11
children.translated_text: For another, [it arises] through the sequence of scripture, etc.—this we shall explain in detail in the chapter on the manifestation of <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of power). [AbhTs 4.11]

children.text: kiṃ tu guror āgamanirūpaṇe vyāpāraḥ āgamasya ca niḥśaṅkasajātīyatatprabandhaprasavanibandhanasamucitavikalpodaye vyāpāraḥ tathāvidhavikalpaprabandha eva sattarka iti uktaḥ sa eva ca bhāvanā bhaṇyate asphuṭatvāt bhūtam api artham abhūtam iva sphuṭatvāpādanena bhāvyate yayā iti // AbhTs_4.12
children.translated_text: However, the role of the guru lies in the ascertainment of scripture; and the role of scripture lies in the arising of appropriate conceptual thought whose foundation is the production of a continuous stream of cognates free from doubt. And such a stream of conceptual thought—

children.text: na ca atra sattarkāt śuddhavidyāprakāśarūpāt ṛte anyat yogāṅgaṃ sākṣāt upāyaḥ tapaḥprabhṛteḥ niyamavargasya ahiṃsādeś ca yamaprakārasya pūrakādeḥ prāṇāyāmavargasya vedyamātraniṣṭhatvena ka iva saṃvidi vyāpāraḥ // AbhTs_4.13
children.translated_text: is the direct means here, apart from which—sound reasoning, which has the form of the illumination of <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (Pure Knowledge)—there is no other limb of yoga that is a direct means. For the class of <s>niyama</s>s (observances) beginning with austerity (<s>tapas</s>), the class of <s>yama</s>s (restraints) such as non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) in the form of inhalation (<s>pūraka</s>) and the like—

children.text: pratyāhāro 'pi karaṇabhūmim eva sātiśayāṃ kuryāt dhyānadhāraṇāsamādhayo 'pi yathottaram abhyāsakrameṇa nirvartyamānā dhyeyavastutādātmyaṃ dhyātuḥ vitareyuḥ // AbhTs_4.14
children.translated_text: <s>Pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of senses) would only enhance the ground of the sense organs. <s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), and <s>samādhi</s> (absorption), being progressively accomplished through a sequence of practice, [produce] identification of the meditator with the object meditated upon—

children.text: abhyāsaś ca pare tattve śivātmani svasvabhāve na saṃbhavaty eva // AbhTs_4.15
children.translated_text: But practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) in the supreme <s>tattva</s>, which is the nature of <s>Śiva</s>, one's own essential nature, is simply not possible. [AbhTs 4.15]

children.text: saṃvidrūḍhasya prāṇabuddhidehaniṣṭhīkaraṇarūpo hi abhyāsaḥ bhārodvahanaśāstrārthabodhanṛttābhyāsavat saṃvidrūpe tu na kiṃcit ādātavyaṃ na apasaraṇīyam iti katham abhyāsaḥ // AbhTs_4.16
children.translated_text: For practice pertains to that which is established in <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), and body, as attained through consciousness—like the practice of carrying burdens, understanding the meaning of texts, or dancing. But in the form of consciousness, there is nothing to be acquired nor anything to be removed—

children.text: kiṃ tarkeṇāpi iti cet uktam atra dvaitādhivāsanirāsaprakāra eva ayaṃ na tu anyat kiṃcid iti // AbhTs_4.17
children.translated_text: 'But what about reasoning (<s>tarka</s>)?'—it has been stated: this [reasoning] is merely the method of removing the habitual impression of duality (<s>dvaitādhivāsa</s>), nothing else. [AbhTs 4.17]

children.text: laukike 'pi vā abhyāse cidātmatvena sarvarūpasya tasya tasya dehādeḥ abhimatarūpatāprakaṭīkaraṇaṃ taditararūpanyagbhāvanaṃ ca iti eṣa eva abhyāsārthaḥ // AbhTs_4.18
children.translated_text: Even in worldly practice, the meaning of practice is: the manifestation of the desired form of this or that—body, etc.—as being of the nature of consciousness, and the suppression of its other forms—

children.text: paratattve tu na kiṃcit apāsyam iti uktam // AbhTs_4.19
children.translated_text: But in the supreme <s>tattva</s>, there is nothing to be removed, as has been said. [AbhTs 4.19]

children.text: dvaitādhivāso 'pi nāma na kaścana pṛthak vastubhūtaḥ api tu svarūpākhyātimātraṃ tat ato dvaitāpāsanaṃ vikalpena kriyata ity ukteḥ // AbhTs_4.20
children.translated_text: And the so-called 'habitual impression of duality' (<s>dvaitādhivāsa</s>) is not something that exists as a separate entity; rather, it is merely the non-recognition (<s>akhyāti</s>) of one's own essential nature. Therefore, the statement that duality is removed by conceptual thought [is valid]. [AbhTs 4.20]

children.text: ayaṃ paramārthaḥ svarūpaṃ prakāśamānam akhyātirūpatvaṃ svayaṃ svātantryāt gṛhītaṃ krameṇa projjhya vikāsonmukham atha vikasat atha vikasitam ity anena krameṇa prakāśate tathā prakāśanam api parameśvarasya svarūpam eva tasmāt na atra yogāṅgāni sākṣāt upāyaḥ // AbhTs_4.21
children.translated_text: This is the supreme truth: one's own essential nature, which is self-luminous, having of its own accord, through its autonomy, assumed the form of non-recognition—gradually casting that off, becomes inclined toward unfolding, then unfolding, then fully unfolded—by this—

children.text: tarkaṃ tu anugṛhṇīyur api sattarka eva sākṣāt tatra upāyaḥ sa eva ca śuddhavidyā sa ca bahuprakāratayā saṃskṛto bhavati tadyathā yāgo homo japo vrataṃ yoga iti tatra bhāvānāṃ sarveṣāṃ parameśvara eva sthitiḥ nānyat vyatiriktam asti iti vikalparūḍhisiddhaye parameśvara eva sarvabhāvārpaṇaṃ yāgaḥ sa ca hṛdyatvāt ye saṃvidanupraveśaṃ svayam eva bhajante teṣāṃ suśakaṃ parameśvare arpaṇam ity abhiprāyeṇa hṛdyānāṃ kusumatarpaṇagandhādīnāṃ bahir upayoga uktaḥ // AbhTs_4.22
children.translated_text: reasoning supports [this process]; but sound reasoning alone is the direct means there. And that is <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (Pure Knowledge). And that is refined in many ways, such as: worship (<s>yāga</s>), fire-offering (<s>homa</s>), recitation (<s>japa</s>), vow (<s>vrata</s>)—

children.text: sarve bhāvāḥ parameśvaratejomayā iti rūḍhavikalpaprāptyai parameśasaṃvidanalatejasi samastabhāvagrāsarasikatābhimate tattejomātrāvaśeṣatvasahasamastabhāvavilāpanaṃ homaḥ // AbhTs_4.23
children.translated_text: 'All entities are made of the radiance of the Supreme Lord'—for the attainment of this firmly established conceptual thought, [one meditates that] in the fire of the awareness of the Supreme Lord, which is held to relish the devouring of all entities like grains of sand, all entities are consumed, with only that radiance remaining, together with the blossoming of all entities—

children.text: tathā ubhayātmakaparāmarśodayārthaṃ bāhyābhyantarādiprameyarūpabhinnabhāvānapekṣayaiva evaṃvidhaṃ tat paraṃ tattvaṃ svasvabhāvabhūtam iti antaḥ parāmarśanaṃ japaḥ // AbhTs_4.24
children.translated_text: Likewise, for the arising of reflective cognition (<s>parāmarśa</s>) of both aspects [immanent and transcendent], without depending on external or internal objects of varied forms—[recognizing that] such supreme <s>tattva</s>, which is one's own essential nature, exists as the inner reflective cognition—

children.text: sarvatra sarvadā nirupāyaparameśvarābhimānalābhāya parameśvarasamatābhimānena dehasyāpi ghaṭāder api avalokanaṃ vratam // AbhTs_4.25
children.translated_text: For the attainment everywhere and at all times of the identity with the Supreme Lord who is without any means, the vow (<s>vrata</s>) consists in viewing even the body, a pot, and everything else with the attitude of equality with the Supreme Lord. [AbhTs 4.25]

children.text: yathoktaṃ śrīnandiśikhāyām sarvasāmyaṃ paraṃ vratam iti // AbhTs_4.26
children.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Śrī Nandiśikhā</s>: 'Equality with all is the supreme vow.' [AbhTs 4.26]

children.text: itthaṃ vicitraiḥ śuddhavidyāṃśarūpaiḥ vikalpaiḥ yat anapekṣitavikalpaṃ svābhāvikaṃ paramārthatattvaṃ prakāśate tasyaiva sanātanatathāvidhaprakāśamātratārūḍhaye tatsvarūpānusaṃdhānātmā vikalpaviśeṣo yogaḥ // AbhTs_4.27
children.translated_text: Thus, through varied conceptual thoughts that are of the nature of aspects of <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (Pure Knowledge), when the supreme reality shines forth—which is natural, independent of conceptual thought—[the absorption into] its own eternal luminous nature of just such a kind—

children.text: tatra parameśvaraḥ pūrṇasaṃvitsvabhāvaḥ pūrṇataiva asya śaktiḥ kulaṃ sāmarthyam ūrmiḥ hṛdayaṃ sāraṃ spandaḥ vibhūtiḥ trīśikā kālī karṣaṇī caṇḍī vāṇī bhogo dṛk nityā ityādibhiḥ āgamabhāṣābhiḥ tattadanvarthapravṛttābhiḥ abhidhīyate tena tena rūpeṇa dhyāyināṃ hṛdi āstām iti // AbhTs_4.28
children.translated_text: Therein, the Supreme Lord's essential nature is complete awareness (<s>pūrṇasaṃvit</s>). His completeness itself is his power, [called] <s>kula</s> (family), <s>sāmarthya</s> (capacity), <s>ūrmi</s> (wave), <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart), <s>sāra</s> (essence), <s>spanda</s> (vibration), <s>vibhūti</s> (glory), <s>trīśikā</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Karṣaṇī</s>, <s>Caṇḍī</s>, <s>Vāṇī</s>, <s>Bhūtirāja</s>—

children.text: sā ca samagraśaktitādarśanena pūrṇatāsaṃvit prakāśate // AbhTs_4.29
children.translated_text: And that awareness of completeness (<s>pūrṇatāsaṃvit</s>) shines forth through seeing the totality of powers. [AbhTs 4.29]

children.text: śaktayaś ca asya asaṃkhyeyāḥ // AbhTs_4.30
children.translated_text: And his powers are innumerable. [AbhTs 4.30]

children.text: kiṃ bahunā yat viśvaṃ tā asya śaktayaḥ tāḥ katham upadeṣṭuṃ śakyāḥ iti // AbhTs_4.31
children.translated_text: What more [need be said]? The universe itself is his powers. How can they be taught? [AbhTs 4.31]

children.text: tisṛṣu tāvat viśvaṃ samāpyate yayā idaṃ śivādidharaṇyantam avikalpyasaṃvinmātrarūpatayā bibharti ca paśyati ca bhāsayati ca parameśvaraḥ sā asya śrīparaśaktiḥ // AbhTs_4.32
children.translated_text: The universe is encompassed in three [powers]: that by which the Supreme Lord sustains, perceives, and illuminates all this—from <s>Śiva</s> down to the earth—as having the form of mere undifferentiated consciousness (<s>avikalpyasaṃvinmātra</s>), that is his <s>Śrī Parā Śakti</s> (Supreme Power)—

children.text: yayā ca darpaṇahastyādivat bhedābhedābhyāṃ sā asya śrīparāparaśaktiḥ // AbhTs_4.33
children.translated_text: That by which [he sees] through both difference and non-difference, like a mirror and an elephant [reflected in it], that is his <s>Śrī Parāparā Śakti</s> (Supreme-and-Non-supreme Power). [AbhTs 4.33]

children.text: yayā parasparaviviktātmanā bhedenaiva sā asya śrīmadaparaśaktiḥ // AbhTs_4.34
children.translated_text: That by which [he sees] through difference alone, with mutually distinct natures, that is his <s>Śrī Aparā Śakti</s> (Non-supreme Power). [AbhTs 4.34]

children.text: etat trividhaṃ yayā dhāraṇam ātmany eva kroḍīkāreṇa anusandhānātmanā grasate sā asya bhagavatī śrīparaiva śrīmanmātṛsadbhāvakālakarṣiṇyādiśabdāntaraniruktā // AbhTs_4.35
children.translated_text: This threefold sustaining, which [the Lord] consumes through integration (<s>kroḍīkāra</s>) within himself, in the form of [continuous] awareness (<s>anusandhāna</s>), that is the Blessed <s>Śrī Parā</s> herself, designated by the terms <s>Śrīmanmātṛsadbhāva</s>, <s>Kālakarṣiṇī</s>, etc.—

children.text: tā etāḥ catasraḥ śaktayaḥ svātantryāt pratyekaṃ tridhaiva vartante // AbhTs_4.36
children.translated_text: These four powers, through [the Lord's] autonomy, each exist in a threefold manner. [AbhTs 4.36]

children.text: sṛṣṭau sthitau saṃhāre ca iti dvādaśa bhavanti // AbhTs_4.37
children.translated_text: In creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>), maintenance (<s>sthiti</s>), and dissolution (<s>saṃhāra</s>)—thus they become twelve. [AbhTs 4.37]

children.text: tathā hi saṃvit pūrvam antar eva bhāvaṃ kalayati tato bahir api sphuṭatayā kalayati tatraiva raktimayatāṃ gṛhītvā tataḥ tam eva bhāvam antar upasaṃjihīrṣayā kalayati tataś ca tadupasaṃhāravighnabhūtāṃ śaṅkāṃ nirmiṇoti ca grasate ca grastaśaṅkāṃśaṃ bhāvabhāgam ātmani upasaṃhāreṇa kalayati tata upasaṃhartṛtvaṃ mamedaṃ rūpam ity api svabhāvam eva kalayati tata upasaṃhartṛsvabhāvakalane kasyacid bhāvasya vāsanātmanā avasthitiṃ kasyacit tu saṃvinmātrāvaśeṣatāṃ kalayati tataḥ svarūpakalanānāntarīyakatvenaiva karaṇacakraṃ kalayati tataḥ karaṇeśvaram api kalayati tataḥ kalpitaṃ māyīyaṃ pramātṛrūpam api kalayati saṅkocatyāgonmukhavikāsagrahaṇarasikam api pramātāraṃ kalayati ato vikasitam api rūpaṃ kalayati iti etā dvādaśa bhagavatyaḥ saṃvidaḥ pramātṝn ekaṃ vāpi uddiśya yugapat krameṇa dviśaḥ triśa ityādisthityāpi udayabhāginyaḥ cakravad āvartamānā bahir api māsakalārāśyādikrameṇa antato vā ghaṭapaṭādikrameṇāpi bhāsamānāḥ cakreśvarasya svātantryaṃ puṣṇatyaḥ śrīkālīśabdavācyāḥ // AbhTs_4.38
children.translated_text: Thus, consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>) first internally activates (<s>kalayati</s>) an object; then externally too manifests it clearly; then, having assumed a state of attachment toward it; then draws that very object back within—

children.text: kalanaṃ ca gatiḥ kṣepo jñānaṃ gaṇanaṃ bhogīkaraṇaṃ śabdanaṃ svātmalayīkaraṇaṃ ca // AbhTs_4.39
children.translated_text: And 'activation' (<s>kalana</s>) means: movement, projection, cognition, enumeration, enjoyment, sounding, and absorption into one's own Self. [AbhTs 4.39]

children.text: yad āhuḥ śrībhūtirājaguravaḥ kṣepāj jñānāc ca kālī kalanavaśatayātha iti // AbhTs_4.40
children.translated_text: As the gurus <s>Śrī Bhūtirāja</s> have said: '<s>Kālī</s> [is so called] from projection (<s>kṣepa</s>) and knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), by the force of activation (<s>kalana</s>)...' [AbhTs 4.40]

children.text: eṣa ca arthaḥ tatra tatra madviracite vivaraṇe prakaraṇastotrādau vitatya vīkṣyaḥ // AbhTs_4.41
children.translated_text: And this meaning is to be examined at length in the commentary, topical treatise (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), hymn (<s>stotra</s>), and other works composed by me in various places. [AbhTs 4.41]

children.text: na atirahasyam ekatra khyāpyaṃ na ca sarvathā gopyam iti hi asmadguravaḥ // AbhTs_4.42
children.translated_text: 'What is exceedingly secret should not be proclaimed in one place; nor should it be entirely concealed'—thus [say] our gurus. [AbhTs 4.42]

children.text: tad evam yad uktaṃ yāgahomādi tat evaṃvidhe maheśvara eva mantavyam // AbhTs_4.43
children.translated_text: Thus, what has been described as worship (<s>yāga</s>), fire-offering (<s>homa</s>), and so on, should be understood as being of this nature, [rooted] in the Great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>) himself. [AbhTs 4.43]

children.text: sarve hi heyam eva upādeyabhūmirūpaṃ viṣṇutaḥ prabhṛti śivāntaṃ paramaśivatayā paśyanti tac ca mithyādarśanam avaśyatyājyam anuttarayogibhir iti tadartham eva vidyādhipateḥ anubhavastotre mahān saṃrambhaḥ evaṃvidhe yāgādau yogānte ca pañcake pratyekaṃ bahuprakāraṃ nirūḍhiḥ yathā yathā bhavati tathaiva ācaret na tu bhakṣyābhakṣyaśuddhyaśuddhyādivivecanayā vastudharmojjhitayā kalpanāmātrasārayā svātmā khedanīya iti uktaṃ śrīpūrvādau na hi śuddhiḥ vastuno rūpaṃ nīlatvavat anyatra tasyaiva aśuddhicodanāt dānasyeva dīkṣitatve codanātaḥ tasya tat tatra aśuddham iti cet codanāntare 'pi tulyaṃ codanāntaram asat tadbādhitatvāt iti cet na śivacodanāyā eva bādhakatvaṃ yuktisiddhaṃ sarvajñānottarādyanantāgamasiddhaṃ ca iti vakṣyāmaḥ // AbhTs_4.44
children.translated_text: For all [lower systems] regard what is to be rejected and what is to be adopted—from <s>Viṣṇu</s> upward to <s>Śiva</s>—as the supreme <s>Śiva</s>. But that is a false view, which must necessarily be abandoned by yogins of the Unsurpassed (<s>Anuttara</s>). Therefore—

children.text: tasmāt vaidikāt prabhṛti pārameśvarasiddhāntatantrakulocchuṣmādiśāstrokto 'pi yo niyamo vidhiḥ vā niṣedho vā so 'tra yāvad akiṃcitkara eva iti siddham // AbhTs_4.45
children.translated_text: Therefore, whatever rule, injunction, or prohibition is stated in any scripture—whether Vedic or from the <s>Pārameśvara Siddhānta</s>, <s>Tantra</s>, <s>Kula</s>, <s>Ucchuṣma</s>, or other scriptures—here it is entirely without effect. This is established. [AbhTs 4.45]

children.text: tathaiva ca uktaṃ śrīpūrvādau vitatya tantrālokāt anveṣyam // AbhTs_4.46
children.translated_text: And likewise it has been stated extensively in the <s>Śrī Pūrvādi</s> [scripture]—to be sought in the <s>Tantrāloka</s>. [AbhTs 4.46]

children.text: tatra yadā vikalpaḥ svayam eva saṃskāram ātmani upāyāntaranirapekṣatayaiva kartuṃ prabhavati tadā asau pāśavavyāpārāt pracyutaḥ śuddhavidyānugraheṇa parameśaśaktirūpatām āpanna upāyatayā avalambyamānaḥ śāktaṃ jñānam āvirbhāvayati // AbhTs_5.1
children.translated_text: Therein, when <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) is able by itself to create an impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) in the self, independent of any other means, then, having fallen away from the activity of the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), by the grace of <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (Pure Knowledge), having attained the nature of the power of the Supreme Lord, being relied upon as a means, it manifests <s>śākta jñāna</s> (knowledge pertaining to <s>Śakti</s>). [AbhTs 5.1]

children.text: tad etac ca nirṇītam anantara eva āhnike // AbhTs_5.2
children.translated_text: And this has been determined in the immediately preceding chapter. [AbhTs 5.2]

children.text: yadā tu upāyāntaram asau svasaṃskārārthaṃ vikalpo 'pekṣate tadā buddhiprāṇadehaghaṭādikān parimitarūpān upāyatvena gṛhṇan aṇutvaṃ prāpta āṇavaṃ jñānam āvirbhāvayati tatra buddhiḥ dhyānātmikā prāṇaḥ sthūlaḥ sūkṣmaś ca ādya uccāraṇātmā uccāraṇaṃ ca nāma pañca prāṇādyā vṛttayaḥ sūkṣmas tu varṇaśabdavācyo vakṣyate dehaḥ saṃniveśaviśeṣātmā karaṇaśabdavācyaḥ ghaṭādayo bāhyāḥ kumbhasthaṇḍilaliṅgapūjādyupāyatayā kīrtayiṣyamāṇāḥ // AbhTs_5.3
children.translated_text: But when that <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) requires another means for the purpose of its own impression, then, grasping limited forms such as intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), breath (<s>prāṇa</s>), body (<s>deha</s>), pot, etc. as means, having attained the state of limitation (<s>aṇutva</s>), it manifests <s>āṇava jñāna</s> (knowledge pertaining to the limited individual). Therein, the intellect is of the nature of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>); the breath is gross and subtle — the former is of the nature of utterance (<s>uccāraṇa</s>), and utterance means the five functions beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>; the subtle, to be described, is denoted by the word <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme); the body, whose nature is a particular configuration, is denoted by the word <s>karaṇa</s> (instrument/mudrā); and external [means] such as the pot etc. will be described as means in the form of worship of the water-vessel (<s>kumbha</s>), altar (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>), <s>liṅga</s>, etc. [AbhTs 5.3]

children.text: tatra dhyānaṃ tāvat iha ucitam upadekṣyāmaḥ yat etat svaprakāśaṃ sarvatattvāntarbhūtaṃ paraṃ tattvam uktaṃ tad eva nijahṛdayabodhe dhyātvā tatra pramātṛpramāṇaprameyarūpasya vahnyarkasomatritayasya saṃghaṭṭaṃ dhyāyet yāvat asau mahābhairavāgniḥ dhyānavātasamiddhākāraḥ sampadyate tasya prāktanaśaktijvālādvādaśakaparivṛtasya cakrātmanaḥ cakṣurādīnām anyatamasuṣiradvāreṇa niḥsṛtasya bāhye grāhyātmani viśrāntaṃ cintayet tena ca viśrāntena prathamaṃ tadbāhyaṃ somarūpatayā sṛṣṭikrameṇa prapūritaṃ tataḥ arkarūpatayā sthityā avabhāsitaṃ tato 'pi saṃhāravahnirūpatayā vilāpitaṃ tataḥ anuttarātmatām āpāditaṃ dhyāyet // AbhTs_5.4
children.translated_text: Herein we shall first teach meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) as is appropriate. That supreme reality (<s>tattva</s>), which has been described as self-luminous and inherent in all principles — one should meditate upon that very [reality] in the awareness of one's own heart. There one should meditate on the collision of the triad of fire (<s>vahni</s>), sun (<s>arka</s>), and moon (<s>soma</s>), which have the forms of the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>), means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), and object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>), until that great fire of <s>Bhairava</s>, blazing forth kindled by the wind of meditation, is accomplished. One should contemplate that [fire], which is of the nature of the <s>cakra</s> (wheel), surrounded by the twelve flames of primordial power, as having issued forth through any one of the aperture-doors of the eye and other [senses] and as coming to rest in the external objective reality (<s>grāhya</s>). And one should meditate that through this resting, first the external [reality] is filled through the process of creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>) in the form of the moon; then it is illuminated through maintenance (<s>sthiti</s>) in the form of the sun; then further it is dissolved through the fire of withdrawal (<s>saṃhāra</s>); and then it is brought to the state of the unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>). [AbhTs 5.4]

children.text: evaṃ tac cakraṃ samastabāhyavastvabhedaparipūrṇaṃ sampadyate // AbhTs_5.5
children.translated_text: Thus that <s>cakra</s> (wheel) becomes filled with the totality of all external objects without distinction. [AbhTs 5.5]

children.text: tato vāsanāśeṣān api bhāvān tena cakreṇa itthaṃ kṛtān dhyāyet // AbhTs_5.6
children.translated_text: Then one should meditate upon even the remaining impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of entities as being thus transformed by that <s>cakra</s>. [AbhTs 5.6]

children.text: evam asya anavarataṃ dhyāyinaḥ svasaṃvinmātraparamārthān sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhāraprabandhān sṛṣṭyādisvātantryaparamārthatvaṃ ca svasaṃvido niścinvataḥ sadya eva bhairavībhāvaḥ // AbhTs_5.7
children.translated_text: Thus, for one who meditates unceasingly, determining the continuous processes of creation, maintenance, and dissolution as having their ultimate reality in nothing but one's own awareness, and determining the ultimate truth of the autonomy of creation etc. as belonging to one's own awareness — the state of <s>Bhairava</s> arises immediately. [AbhTs 5.7]

children.text: abhyāsāt tu sarvepsitasiddhyādayo 'pi // AbhTs_5.8
children.translated_text: And through practice, the accomplishment of all desired <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural attainments) and the like also [arise]. [AbhTs 5.8]

children.text: svaprakāśaṃ samastātmatattvaṃ mātrādikaṃ trayam // AbhTs_5.9
children.translated_text: The self-luminous reality of all selves, the triad beginning with <s>mātrā</s> (the knower),

children.text: antaḥkṛtya sthitaṃ dhyāyed dhṛdayānandadhāmani // AbhTs_5.10
children.translated_text: Having internalized [all], one should meditate upon it as resting in the abode of heart-bliss. [AbhTs 5.10]

children.text: tad dvādaśamahāśaktiraśmicakreśvaraṃ vibhum // AbhTs_5.11
children.translated_text: That all-pervading lord of the wheel of rays of twelve great powers,

children.text: vyomabhir niḥsarad bāhye dhyāyet sṛṣṭyādibhāvakam // AbhTs_5.12
children.translated_text: Issuing forth through the apertures to the external, one should meditate upon it as the agent of creation and the rest. [AbhTs 5.12]

children.text: tad grastasarvabāhyāntarbhāvamaṇḍalam ātmani // AbhTs_5.13
children.translated_text: Having devoured the entire <s>maṇḍala</s> (circle) of external and internal entities, [resting] in the Self,

children.text: viśrāmyan bhāvayed yogī syād evam ātmanaḥ prathā // AbhTs_5.14
children.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s> should contemplate it as resting; thus there is the expansion of the Self. [AbhTs 5.14]

children.text: iti saṃgrahaślokāḥ // AbhTs_5.15
children.translated_text: Thus [end] the summary verses. [AbhTs 5.15]

children.text: iti dhyānam // AbhTs_5.16
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the section on] meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>). [AbhTs 5.16]

children.text: tatra prāṇam uccicārayiṣuḥ pūrvaṃ hṛdaya eva śūnye viśrāmyati tato bāhye prāṇodayāt tato 'pi bāhyaṃ prati apānacandrāpūraṇena sarvātmatāṃ paśyati tataḥ anyanirākāṅkṣo bhavati tataḥ samānodayāt saṃghaṭṭaviśrāntim anubhavati tata udānavahnyudaye mātṛmeyādikalanāṃ grasate // AbhTs_5.17
children.translated_text: Therein, one who is about to utter the <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) first rests in the void of the heart itself. Then, from the external arising of <s>prāṇa</s>, and then further, through the filling of the moon of <s>apāna</s> toward the external, one sees the all-pervading nature. Then one becomes free from desire for anything else. Then, from the arising of <s>samāna</s>, one experiences the repose in collision. Then, in the rising of the fire of <s>udāna</s>, one devours the divisions of knower, known, and so forth. [AbhTs 5.17]

children.text: tadgrāsakavahnipraśame vyānodaye sarvāvacchedavandhyaḥ sphurati // AbhTs_5.18
children.translated_text: Upon the subsiding of that devouring fire, in the arising of <s>vyāna</s>, [awareness] flashes forth, free from all limitation. [AbhTs 5.18]

children.text: evaṃ śūnyāt prabhṛti vyānāntaṃ yā etā viśrāntayaḥ tā eva nijānando nirānandaḥ parānando brahmānando mahānandaḥ cidānanda iti ṣaṭ ānandabhūmaya upadiṣṭāḥ yāsām ekaḥ anusaṃdhātā udayāstamayavihīnaḥ antarviśrāntiparamārtharūpo jagadānandaḥ // AbhTs_5.19
children.translated_text: Thus, the resting points from the void up to <s>vyāna</s> — these are the six planes of bliss taught as: <s>nijānanda</s> (innate bliss), <s>nirānanda</s> (bliss of voidness), <s>parānanda</s> (supreme bliss), <s>brahmānanda</s> (bliss of <s>Brahman</s>), <s>mahānanda</s> (great bliss), and <s>cidānanda</s> (bliss of consciousness). The one who unifies them all, devoid of arising and setting, having the true nature of inner repose, is <s>jagadānanda</s> (universal bliss). [AbhTs 5.19]

children.text: tat etāsu uccārabhūmiṣu pratyekaṃ dvyādiśaḥ sarvaśo vā viśrāmya anyat taddehaprāṇādivyatiriktaṃ viśrāntitattvam āsādayati // AbhTs_5.20
children.translated_text: Therein, at each of these planes of breath-utterance, resting in two and so on or in all, one attains that resting reality which is distinct from one's body, breath, and the like. [AbhTs 5.20]

children.text: tad eva sṛṣṭisaṃhārabījoccāraṇarahasyam anusaṃdadhat vikalpaṃ saṃskuryāt āsu ca viśrāntiṣu pratyekaṃ pañca avasthā bhavanti praveśatāratamyāt // AbhTs_5.21
children.translated_text: That very [practitioner], unifying the secret of the utterance of the seed of creation and dissolution, should purify <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction). And at each of these resting points, there are five states due to the gradation of depth of entry. [AbhTs 5.21]

children.text: tatra prāg ānandaḥ pūrṇatāṃśasparśāt tata udbhavaḥ kṣaṇaṃ niḥśarīratāyāṃ rūḍheḥ tataḥ kampaḥ svabalākrāntau dehatādātmyaśaithilyāt tato nidrā bahirmukhatvavilayāt // AbhTs_5.22
children.translated_text: Therein, first is <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), from the touch of a portion of fullness; then <s>udbhava</s> (arising), from being established for a moment in bodilessness; then <s>kampa</s> (trembling), from the loosening of identity with the body when overcome by one's own power; then <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), from the dissolution of outward-directed attention. [AbhTs 5.22]

children.text: ittham anātmani ātmabhāve līne svātmanaḥ sarvamayatvāt ātmani anātmabhāvo vilīyate iti ato ghūrṇiḥ mahāvyāptyudayāt // AbhTs_5.23
children.translated_text: Thus, when the non-self nature is dissolved in the self-nature, since the Self is of the nature of everything, the non-self nature dissolves in the Self. Therefore, <s>ghūrṇi</s> (reeling/absorption) [arises] from the dawn of great all-pervasiveness. [AbhTs 5.23]

children.text: tā etā jāgradādibhūmayaḥ turyātītāntāḥ // AbhTs_5.24
children.translated_text: These are the planes of waking etc., ending with <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth). [AbhTs 5.24]

children.text: etāś ca bhūmayaḥ trikoṇakandahṛttālūrdhvakuṇḍalinīcakrapraveśe bhavanti // AbhTs_5.25
children.translated_text: And these planes arise in the entry into the <s>cakras</s> (centers) of the triangle (<s>trikoṇa</s>), bulb (<s>kanda</s>), heart (<s>hṛt</s>), palate (<s>tālu</s>), upper (<s>ūrdhva</s>), and <s>kuṇḍalinī</s>. [AbhTs 5.25]

children.text: evam uccāraviśrāntau yat paraṃ spandanaṃ galitāśeṣavedyaṃ yac ca unmiṣad vedyaṃ yac ca unmiṣitavedyaṃ tad eva liṅgatrayam iti vakṣyāmaḥ svāvasare // AbhTs_5.26
children.translated_text: Thus, in the repose of utterance, that supreme vibration (<s>spanda</s>) devoid of all objectivity, and that in which objectivity dawns, and that in which objectivity has dawned — these are the three <s>liṅgas</s> (signs), as we shall explain in their proper place. [AbhTs 5.26]

children.text: paraṃ cātra liṅgaṃ yoginīhṛdayam // AbhTs_5.27
children.translated_text: And the supreme <s>liṅga</s> here is the heart of the <s>Yoginī</s>. [AbhTs 5.27]

children.text: tatra mukhyā spandanarūpatā saṃkocavikāsātmatayā yāmalarūpatodayena visargakalāviśrāntilābhāt ity alam // AbhTs_5.28
children.translated_text: Therein, the primary nature of vibration (<s>spandana</s>), through the arising of the paired form (<s>yāmala</s>) consisting of contraction and expansion, [is attained] by obtaining repose in the <s>kalā</s> (phase) of emission (<s>visarga</s>) — enough said. [AbhTs 5.28]

children.text: aprakāśaḥ atra anupraveśaḥ // AbhTs_5.29
children.translated_text: The entry here is not [publicly] revealed. [AbhTs 5.29]

children.text: pūrvaṃ svabodhe tadanu prameye viśramya meyaṃ paripūrayeta // AbhTs_5.30
children.translated_text: First resting in one's own awareness, then in the object of knowledge, one should fill the object of knowledge. [AbhTs 5.30]

children.text: pūrṇe 'tra viśrāmyati mātṛmeyavibhāgam āśv eva sa saṃhareta // AbhTs_5.31
children.translated_text: When [the object is] filled, [awareness] rests therein; swiftly one should withdraw the division of knower and known. [AbhTs 5.31]

children.text: vyāptyātha viśrāmyati tā imāḥ syuḥ śūnyena sākaṃ ṣaḍupāyabhūmyaḥ // AbhTs_5.32
children.translated_text: Then resting in all-pervasiveness — these, together with the void, are the six planes of the means. [AbhTs 5.32]

children.text: prāṇādayo vyānanapaścimās tallīnaś ca jāgrat prabhṛti prapañcaḥ // AbhTs_5.33
children.translated_text: The <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest up to <s>vyāna</s> — in these the manifest world is dissolved, beginning from waking. [AbhTs 5.33]

children.text: abhyāsaniṣṭho 'tra tu sṛṣṭisaṃhṛdvimarśadhāmany acireṇa rohet // AbhTs_5.34
children.translated_text: One who is devoted to practice herein will quickly ascend to the abode of the reflective awareness of creation and dissolution. [AbhTs 5.34]

children.text: iti āntaraślokāḥ // AbhTs_5.35
children.translated_text: Thus [end] the internal verses. [AbhTs 5.35]

children.text: iti uccāraṇam // AbhTs_5.36
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the section on] utterance (<s>uccāraṇa</s>). [AbhTs 5.36]

children.text: asmin eva uccāre sphuran avyaktānukṛtiprāyo dhvaniḥ varṇaḥ tasya sṛṣṭisaṃhārabīje mukhyaṃ rūpaṃ tadabhyāsāt parasaṃvittilābhaḥ tathāhi kādau mānte sācke anacke vā antaruccārite smṛte vā samaviśiṣṭaḥ saṃvitspandasparśaḥ samayānapekṣitvāt paripūrṇaḥ samayopekṣiṇo 'pi śabdāḥ tadarthabhāvakā manorājyādivat anuttarasaṃvitsparśāt ekīkṛtahṛtkaṇṭhoṣṭho dvādaśāntadvayaṃ hṛdayaṃ ca ekīkuryāt iti varṇarahasyam // AbhTs_5.37
children.translated_text: Within this very utterance, the sound (<s>dhvani</s>), which is predominantly an indistinct imitation shining forth, is a <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme). Its primary form is in the seed of creation and dissolution. Through its practice, one attains supreme awareness (<s>parasaṃvit</s>). For indeed, when 'ka' and others, or 'ma' at the end, 'sa-cke,' 'ana-cke,' or others are internally uttered or recollected, the touch of the vibration of awareness is equal and undifferentiated, because it is independent of convention. Even conventional sounds manifest their meanings through the touch of supreme awareness, like day-dreaming and the like. One should unify the heart, throat, and lips with the touch of supreme awareness, and should unify the two <s>dvādaśāntas</s> (twelve-finger spaces) and the heart — this is the secret of the phonemes. [AbhTs 5.37]

children.text: antaḥsparśadvimarśānantarasamudbhūtaṃ sitapītādyāntaraṃ varṇam udbhāvyamānaṃ saṃvidam anubhāvayati iti kecit // AbhTs_5.38
children.translated_text: Some say that the internal color — white, yellow, etc. — arising immediately after the reflective awareness of the internal touch, when manifested, produces the experience of awareness. [AbhTs 5.38]

children.text: vācyaviraheṇa saṃvitspandād indvarkagatinirodhābhyām // AbhTs_5.39
children.translated_text: Through the vibration of awareness without the expressed [object], by stopping the movements of moon and sun — [AbhTs 5.39]

children.text: yasya tu samasaṃpraveśāt pūrṇāṃ cidbījapiṇḍavarṇavidhau // AbhTs_5.40
children.translated_text: For one whose equal entry into the fullness of the consciousness-seed-mass-phoneme arrangement [is accomplished]. [AbhTs 5.40]

children.text: iti āntaraślokaḥ // AbhTs_5.41
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the internal verse. [AbhTs 5.41]

children.text: iti varṇavidhiḥ // AbhTs_5.42
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the phoneme method (<s>varṇavidhi</s>). [AbhTs 5.42]

children.text: karaṇaṃ tu mudrāprakāśane vakṣyāmaḥ // AbhTs_5.43
children.translated_text: The instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) we shall explain in the chapter on the revelation of <s>mudrā</s>. [AbhTs 5.43]

children.text: sa eva sthānaprakalpanaśabdena uktaḥ tatra tridhā sthānaṃ prāṇavāyuḥ śarīraṃ bāhyaṃ ca tatra prāṇe tāvat vidhiḥ sarvaḥ asau vakṣyamāṇaḥ adhvā prāṇasthaḥ kalyate tasya kramākramakalanaiva kālaḥ sa ca parameśvara eva antarbhāti tadbhāsanaṃ ca devasya kālī nāma śaktiḥ bhedena tu tadābhāsanaṃ kramākramayoḥ prāṇavṛttiḥ // AbhTs_6.1
children.translated_text: That very [topic] is denoted by the word <s>sthānaprakalpana</s> (establishment of locus). Therein, the locus is threefold: the breath (<s>prāṇa</s>), the body (<s>śarīra</s>), and the external. Therein, first, the entire method regarding the breath will be described. The path (<s>adhvan</s>) established in the breath is calculated; its sequential and non-sequential calculation is time (<s>kāla</s>). And that is none other than the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) shining within. And his manifestation is the power (<s>śakti</s>) of the Lord called <s>Kālī</s>. But its manifestation with differentiation, in sequence and non-sequence, is the function of the breath. [AbhTs 6.1]

children.text: saṃvid eva hi prameyebhyo vibhaktaṃ rūpaṃ gṛhṇāti ata eva ca avacchedayogāt vedyatāṃ yāntī nabhaḥ tataḥ svātantryāt meye svīkārautsukyena nipatantī kriyāśaktipradhānā prāṇanārūpā jīvasvabhāvā pañcabhī rūpaiḥ dehaṃ yataḥ pūrayati tato 'sau cetana iva bhāti // AbhTs_6.2
children.translated_text: For awareness (<s>saṃvit</s>) indeed assumes a form separate from objects of knowledge. And because of being subject to limitation, it assumes the nature of the knowable — [becoming like] space. Then, through its autonomy, falling toward the object of knowledge with eagerness to appropriate it, [awareness], predominantly the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>), assumes the form of vitality (<s>prāṇana</s>), the nature of the life-force (<s>jīva</s>), and fills the body with five forms — therefore [the body] appears as if conscious. [AbhTs 6.2]

children.text: tatra kriyā śaktau kālādhvā prācyabhāge uttare tu mūrtivaicitryarūpo deśādhvā tatra varṇamantrapadādhvanaḥ kālādhvani sthitiḥ parasūkṣmasthūlarūpatvāt // AbhTs_6.3
children.translated_text: Therein, in the power of action, the path of time (<s>kālādhvan</s>) is on the eastern side; on the northern side is the path of space (<s>deśādhvan</s>), having the form of diversity of embodiment. Therein, the paths of phoneme (<s>varṇa</s>), <s>mantra</s>, and word (<s>pada</s>) are situated in the path of time, because of being of supreme, subtle, and gross nature. [AbhTs 6.3]

children.text: deśādhvasthitis tu tattvapurakalātmanā iti bhaviṣyati svāvasare // AbhTs_6.4
children.translated_text: But the situation in the path of space, by way of <s>tattva</s> (principle), <s>pura</s> (world), and <s>kalā</s> (phase) — this will be [explained] in its proper place. [AbhTs 6.4]

children.text: tatra yady api dehe sabāhyābhyantaram otaprotarūpaḥ prāṇaḥ tathāpi prasphuṭasaṃvedyaprayatnaḥ asau hṛdayāt prabhṛti iti tata eva ayaṃ nirūpaṇīyaḥ // AbhTs_6.5
children.translated_text: Therein, although the breath is woven through the body both internally and externally, nevertheless, its effort is clearly perceptible from the heart onward — therefore it should be examined from there. [AbhTs 6.5]

children.text: tatra prabhuśaktiḥ ātmaśaktiḥ yatna iti tritayaṃ prāṇeraṇe hetuḥ guṇamukhyabhāvāt // AbhTs_6.6
children.translated_text: Therein, the Lord's power, the Self's power, and effort — this triad is the cause of the movement of the breath, due to their relationship as secondary and primary. [AbhTs 6.6]

children.text: tatra hṛdayāt dvādaśāntāntaṃ svāṅgulaiḥ sarvasya ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulaḥ prāṇacāraḥ nirgame praveśe ca svocitabalayatnadehatvāt sarvasya // AbhTs_6.7
children.translated_text: Therein, the course of the breath from the heart to the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (twelve-finger space above the head) is thirty-six finger-breadths by one's own fingers for everyone, in both exhalation and inhalation, because of the appropriate power, effort, and body of each person. [AbhTs 6.7]

children.text: tatra ghaṭikā tithiḥ māso varṣaṃ ca varṣasamūhātmā iti samastaḥ kālaḥ parisamāpyate /
children.translated_text: Therein, a <s>ghaṭikā</s> (time unit), a <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), a month, a year, and a collection of years — thus all time is completed.

children.text: tatra sapañcāṃśe aṅgule caṣaka iti sthityā ghaṭikodayaḥ ghaṭikā hi ṣaṣṭyā caṣakaiḥ tasmāt dvāsaptatyaṅgulā bhavati // AbhTs_6.8
children.translated_text: Therein, at one-and-one-fifth finger-breadths, one <s>caṣaka</s> unit arises; a <s>ghaṭikā</s> consists of sixty <s>caṣakas</s>; therefore it amounts to seventy-two finger-breadths [of breath]. [AbhTs 6.8]

children.text: atha tithyudayaḥ // AbhTs_6.9
children.translated_text: Now, the arising of a <s>tithi</s> (lunar day). [AbhTs 6.9]

children.text: sapādam aṅguladvayaṃ tuṭiḥ ucyate tāsu catasṛṣu praharaḥ tuṭyardhaṃ tuṭyardhaṃ tatra saṃdhyā evaṃ nirgame dinaṃ praveśe rātriḥ iti tithyudayaḥ // AbhTs_6.10
children.translated_text: Two-and-a-quarter finger-breadths is called a <s>tuṭi</s>. In four <s>tuṭis</s>, one <s>prahara</s> (watch). Half a <s>tuṭi</s>, half a <s>tuṭi</s> — there is the twilight (<s>saṃdhyā</s>). Thus in exhalation is the day, in inhalation is the night — this is the arising of a <s>tithi</s>. [AbhTs 6.10]

children.text: atha māsodayaḥ // AbhTs_6.11
children.translated_text: Now, the arising of a month. [AbhTs 6.11]

children.text: tatra dinaṃ kṛṣṇapakṣaḥ rātriḥ śuklaḥ tatra pūrvaṃ tuṭyardham antyaṃ ca tuṭyardhaṃ viśrāntiḥ akālakalitāḥ madhyās tu pañcadaśa tuṭaya eva tithayaḥ tatra prakāśo viśrāntiś ca iti ete eva dinaniśe // AbhTs_6.12
children.translated_text: Therein, the day is the dark fortnight (<s>kṛṣṇapakṣa</s>); the night is the bright fortnight (<s>śuklapakṣa</s>). The first half-<s>tuṭi</s> and the last half-<s>tuṭi</s> are resting points, uncalculated by time. But the fifteen <s>tuṭis</s> in between are the <s>tithis</s> (lunar days). Therein, light and rest — these are the day and night. [AbhTs 6.12]

children.text: tatra vedyamayatāprakāśo dinaṃ vedyasya vicārayitari layo rātriḥ te ca prakāśaviśrāntī cirāciravaicitryāt anantabhede tatsāmye tu viṣuvat // AbhTs_6.13
children.translated_text: Therein, the manifestation of objectivity is the day; the dissolution of the object in the observer is the night. And those phases of light and rest, because of the variety of long and short duration, are infinitely differentiated; but when they are equal, that is the equinox (<s>viṣuvat</s>). [AbhTs 6.13]

children.text: tatra kṛṣṇapakṣe prāṇārke apānacandra āpyāyikām ekām ekāṃ kalām arpayati yāvat pañcadaśyāṃ tuṭau dvādaśāntasamīpe kṣīṇapṛthagbhūtakalāprasaraḥ candramāḥ prāṇārka eva līyate // AbhTs_6.14
children.translated_text: Therein, during the dark fortnight, the moon of <s>apāna</s> offers one <s>kalā</s> (phase) at a time, its nourishing power, to the sun of <s>prāṇa</s>, until on the fifteenth <s>tuṭi</s>, near the <s>dvādaśānta</s>, the moon, its stream of separate <s>kalās</s> diminished, dissolves into the sun of <s>prāṇa</s> itself. [AbhTs 6.14]

children.text: tadanantaraṃ yat tuṭyardhaṃ sa pakṣasaṃdhiḥ // AbhTs_6.15
children.translated_text: Immediately after that, the half-<s>tuṭi</s> is the junction of the fortnights (<s>pakṣasaṃdhi</s>). [AbhTs 6.15]

children.text: tasya ca tuṭyardhasya prācyam ardham āmāvasyaṃ dvitīyaṃ prātipadam // AbhTs_6.16
children.translated_text: And of that half-<s>tuṭi</s>, the first half is the new-moon (<s>āmāvāsya</s>), the second is the first day of the bright fortnight (<s>prātipadā</s>). [AbhTs 6.16]

children.text: tatra prātipade tasmin bhāge sa āmāvasyo bhāgo yadā kāsaprayatnāvadhānādikṛtāt tithicchedāt viśati tadā tatra grahaṇam tatra ca vedyarūpasomasahabhūto māyāpramātṛrāhuḥ svabhāvatayā vilāpanāśaktaḥ kevalam ācchādanamātrasamarthaḥ sūryagataṃ cāndram amṛtaṃ pibati iti // AbhTs_6.17
children.translated_text: Therein, in that <s>prātipadā</s> portion, when the new-moon portion enters through the interruption of the <s>tithi</s> caused by attention to the effort of practice and the like, then there is an eclipse (<s>grahaṇa</s>). And there, <s>Rāhu</s>, the <s>māyā</s>-subject, together with the moon-form of objectivity, is by nature unable to dissolve, capable only of covering — he drinks the lunar nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) that belongs to the sun. [AbhTs 6.17]

children.text: pramātṛpramāṇaprameyatritayāvibhāgakāritvāt sa puṇyaḥ kālaḥ pāralaukikaphalapradaḥ // AbhTs_6.18
children.translated_text: Because it creates non-differentiation of the triad of knower, means of knowledge, and object of knowledge, that is an auspicious time, bestowing otherworldly fruits. [AbhTs 6.18]

children.text: tataḥ praviśati prāṇe cidarka ekaikayā kalayā apānacandram āpūrayati yāvat pañcadaśī tuṭiḥ pūrṇimā tadanantaraṃ pakṣasaṃdhiḥ grahaṇaṃ ca iti prāgvat etat tu aihikaphalapradam iti māsodayaḥ // AbhTs_6.19
children.translated_text: Then, entering the breath, the sun of consciousness fills the moon of <s>apāna</s> with one <s>kalā</s> at a time, until the fifteenth <s>tuṭi</s> is the full moon (<s>pūrṇimā</s>). Immediately after, the junction of the fortnights and the eclipse — as before. But this bestows worldly fruits. Thus [ends] the arising of a month. [AbhTs 6.19]

children.text: atha varṣodayaḥ // AbhTs_6.20
children.translated_text: Now, the arising of a year. [AbhTs 6.20]

children.text: tatra kṛṣṇapakṣa eva uttarāyaṇaṃ ṣaṭsu ṣaṭsu aṅguleṣu saṃkrāntiḥ makarāt mithunāntām // AbhTs_6.21
children.translated_text: Therein, the dark fortnight itself is the northern course (<s>uttarāyaṇa</s>); at every six finger-breadths there is a transit (<s>saṃkrānti</s>), from <s>Makara</s> (Capricorn) to the end of <s>Mithuna</s> (Gemini). [AbhTs 6.21]

children.text: tatra pratyaṅgulaṃ pañca tithayaḥ tatrāpi dinarātrivibhāgaḥ evaṃ praveśe dakṣiṇāyanaṃ garbhatvam udbhavecchā udbubhūṣutā udbhaviṣyatvam udbhavārambhaḥ udbhavattā janmādivikāraṣaṭkaṃ ca iti kramāt makarādiṣu iti // AbhTs_6.22
children.translated_text: Therein, five <s>tithis</s> per finger-breadth. Therein too there is the division of day and night. Similarly, in inhalation is the southern course (<s>dakṣiṇāyana</s>). Embryonic state, desire for manifestation, being about to manifest, beginning of manifestation, state of having manifested, and the six modifications beginning with birth — these arise successively in the signs beginning with <s>Makara</s>. [AbhTs 6.22]

children.text: tathaiva upāsā atra phalaṃ samucitaṃ karoti // AbhTs_6.23
children.translated_text: Similarly, worship here produces appropriate fruit. [AbhTs 6.23]

children.text: atra ca dakṣādyāḥ pitāmahāntā rudrāḥ śaktayaś ca dvādaśādhipataya iti varṣodayaḥ // AbhTs_6.24
children.translated_text: And here, <s>Dakṣa</s> and others beginning from him up to Grandfather (<s>Pitāmaha</s>), the <s>Rudras</s> and <s>Śaktis</s> — these are the twelve presiding deities. Thus [ends] the arising of a year. [AbhTs 6.24]

children.text: pratyaṅgulaṃ ṣaṣṭiḥ tithaya iti krameṇa saṃkrāntau varṣam ity anena krameṇa praveśanirgamayoḥ dvādaśābdodayaḥ pratyaṅgulaṃ tithīnāṃ śatatrayaṃ sapañcāṃśe 'ṅgule varṣaṃ yatra prāk caṣakam uktam iti gaṇanayā saṃkrāntau pañca varṣāṇi iti anayā paripāṭyā ekasmin prāṇanirgamapraveśakāle ṣaṣṭyabdodayaḥ atra ekaviṃśatisahasrāṇi ṣaṭ śatāni iti tithīnāṃ saṃkhyā // AbhTs_6.25
children.translated_text: Sixty <s>tithis</s> per finger-breadth; thus by succession, at each transit is a year. By this method, in both inhalation and exhalation, there arises a twelve-year cycle. Three hundred <s>tithis</s> per finger-breadth; at one-and-one-fifth finger-breadths is a year — where previously a <s>caṣaka</s> was mentioned. By this calculation, at each transit is five years. By this system, in one cycle of breath exhalation and inhalation, there arises a sixty-year cycle. Herein, the count of <s>tithis</s> is twenty-one thousand six hundred. [AbhTs 6.25]

children.text: tāvatī eva ahorātre prāṇasaṃkhyā iti na ṣaṣṭyabdodayāt adhikaṃ parīkṣyate ānantyāt // AbhTs_6.26
