children.translated_text: That very same is the count of breaths in a day and night. Therefore nothing beyond the sixty-year cycle is examined, because of infinity. [AbhTs 6.26]

children.text: tatra mānuṣaṃ varṣaṃ devānāṃ tithiḥ anena krameṇa divyāni dvādaśavarṣasahasrāṇi caturyugam // AbhTs_6.27
children.translated_text: Therein, a human year is a day (<s>tithi</s>) of the gods; by this reckoning, twelve thousand divine years constitute a <s>caturyuga</s> (cycle of four ages). [AbhTs 6.27]

children.text: catvāri trīṇi dve ekam iti kṛtāt prabhṛti tāvadbhiḥ śataiḥ aṣṭau saṃdhyāḥ // AbhTs_6.28
children.translated_text: Four, three, two, and one — beginning from the <s>Kṛta</s> [age], with that many hundreds, [make up] the eight junctures (<s>saṃdhyā</s>). [AbhTs 6.28]

children.text: caturyugānām ekasaptatyā manvantaram manvantaraiḥ caturdaśabhiḥ brāhmaṃ dinaṃ brahmadinānte kālāgnidagdhe lokatraye anyatra ca lokatraye dhūmaprasvāpite sarve janā vegavad agnipreritā janaloke pralayākalībhūya tiṣṭhanti // AbhTs_6.29
children.translated_text: Seventy-one <s>caturyugas</s> constitute a <s>manvantara</s>; with fourteen <s>manvantaras</s>, one day of <s>Brahmā</s>. At the end of <s>Brahmā</s>'s day, when the three worlds are burned by the fire of time (<s>kālāgni</s>) and the other three worlds are put to sleep by smoke, all beings, propelled swiftly by fire, remain in <s>Janaloka</s>, having become as if absorbed in dissolution. [AbhTs 6.29]

children.text: prabuddhās tu kūṣmāṇḍahāṭakeśādyā maholoke krīḍanti // AbhTs_6.30
children.translated_text: But those who are awakened — <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s>, <s>Hāṭakeśa</s>, and others — sport in <s>Maholoka</s>. [AbhTs 6.30]

children.text: tato niśāsamāptau brāhmī sṛṣṭiḥ // AbhTs_6.31
children.translated_text: Then, upon the completion of night, the <s>Brāhmī</s> creation [begins]. [AbhTs 6.31]

children.text: anena mānena varṣaśataṃ brahmāyuḥ // AbhTs_6.32
children.translated_text: By this measure, one hundred years is the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>. [AbhTs 6.32]

children.text: tat viṣṇoḥ dinaṃ tāvatī ca rātriḥ tasyāpi śatam āyuḥ // AbhTs_6.33
children.translated_text: That [lifespan of Brahmā] is one day of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and an equal period is his night; his lifespan too is one hundred [such years]. [AbhTs 6.33]

children.text: tat dinaṃ tadūrdhve rudralokaprabho rudrasya tāvatī rātriḥ prāgvat varṣaṃ tacchatam api ca avadhiḥ // AbhTs_6.34
children.translated_text: That [lifespan of Viṣṇu] is one day of <s>Rudra</s>, the lord of <s>Rudraloka</s>, situated above; an equal period is his night; as before, one year [is calculated similarly], and one hundred [such years] is the limit. [AbhTs 6.34]

children.text: tatra rudrasya tadavasitau śivatvagatiḥ rudrasya uktādhikārāvadhiḥ brahmāṇḍadhārakāṇāṃ tat dinaṃ śatarudrāṇāṃ niśā tāvatī teṣām api ca śatam āyuḥ // AbhTs_6.35
children.translated_text: There, at the conclusion of <s>Rudra</s>'s [lifespan], he attains the state of <s>Śiva</s>; this is the stated limit of <s>Rudra</s>'s authority. That [lifespan] is one day of the hundred <s>Rudras</s> who uphold the cosmic eggs (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>); an equal period is their night; their lifespan too is one hundred [such years]. [AbhTs 6.35]

children.text: śatarudrakṣaye brahmāṇḍavināśaḥ // AbhTs_6.36
children.translated_text: Upon the exhaustion of the hundred <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>brahmāṇḍa</s> (cosmic egg) is destroyed. [AbhTs 6.36]

children.text: evaṃ jalatattvāt avyaktāntam etad eva krameṇa rudrāṇām āyuḥ // AbhTs_6.37
children.translated_text: Thus, from the water-principle (<s>jala-tattva</s>) up to the <s>Avyakta</s> (Unmanifest), in the same manner sequentially is the lifespan of the [respective] <s>Rudras</s>. [AbhTs 6.37]

children.text: pūrvasyāyur uttarasya dinam iti // AbhTs_6.38
children.translated_text: The lifespan of the former is the day of the latter. [AbhTs 6.38]

children.text: tataś ca brahmā rudrāś ca abādyadhikāriṇaḥ avyakte tiṣṭhanti iti // AbhTs_6.39
children.translated_text: And thereupon, <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, and the presiding authorities from [earth] upward abide in the <s>Avyakta</s> (Unmanifest). [AbhTs 6.39]

children.text: śrīkaṇṭhanāthaś ca tadā saṃhartā // AbhTs_6.40
children.translated_text: And Lord <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> is then the destroyer. [AbhTs 6.40]

children.text: eṣo 'vāntarapralayaḥ tatkṣaye sṛṣṭiḥ // AbhTs_6.41
children.translated_text: This is the intermediate dissolution (<s>avāntara-pralaya</s>); upon its exhaustion, creation [begins again]. [AbhTs 6.41]

children.text: tatra śāstrāntaram uktā api sṛjyante // AbhTs_6.42
children.translated_text: There, even those mentioned in other scriptures are [re-]created. [AbhTs 6.42]

children.text: yat tu śrīkaṇṭhanāthasya svam āyuḥ tat kañcukavāsināṃ rudrāṇāṃ dinaṃ tāvatī rajanī teṣāṃ yad āyuḥ tat gahaneśadinaṃ tāvatī eva kṣapā tasyāṃ ca samastam eva māyāyāṃ vilīyate // AbhTs_6.43
children.translated_text: But the own lifespan of Lord <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> is one day of the <s>Rudras</s> dwelling in the coverings (<s>kañcuka</s>); an equal period is their night. Their lifespan is one day of <s>Gahaneśa</s>; an equal period is his night. And during that [night], everything dissolves entirely into <s>Māyā</s>. [AbhTs 6.43]

children.text: punaḥ gahaneśaḥ sṛjati // AbhTs_6.44
children.translated_text: Again <s>Gahaneśa</s> creates. [AbhTs 6.44]

children.text: evaṃ yaḥ avyaktakālaḥ taṃ daśabhiḥ parārdhaiḥ guṇayitvā māyādinaṃ kathayet tāvatī rātriḥ // AbhTs_6.45
children.translated_text: Thus, the time of the <s>Avyakta</s>, multiplied by ten <s>parārdhas</s>, gives the day of <s>Māyā</s>; an equal period is the night. [AbhTs 6.45]

children.text: sa eva pralayaḥ // AbhTs_6.46
children.translated_text: That itself is the dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>). [AbhTs 6.46]

children.text: māyākālaḥ parārdhaśatena guṇita aiśvaratattve dinam // AbhTs_6.47
children.translated_text: The time of <s>Māyā</s>, multiplied by one hundred <s>parārdhas</s>, is one day in the <s>Īśvara-tattva</s> (Lord-principle). [AbhTs 6.47]

children.text: atra prāṇo jagat sṛjati tāvatī rātriḥ yatra prāṇapraśamaḥ prāṇe ca brahmabiladhāmni śānte 'pi yā saṃvit tatrāpy asti kramaḥ // AbhTs_6.48
children.translated_text: Here, <s>prāṇa</s> (the vital breath) creates the world; an equal period is the night, in which <s>prāṇa</s> subsides. And even when <s>prāṇa</s>, the abode of the aperture of <s>Brahman</s>, has become quiescent, the awareness (<s>saṃvit</s>) that exists there — even there, there is succession. [AbhTs 6.48]

children.text: aiśvare kāle parārdhaśataguṇite yā saṃkhyā tat sādāśivaṃ dinaṃ tāvatī niśā sa eva mahāpralayaḥ // AbhTs_6.49
children.translated_text: The number obtained by multiplying the time of <s>Īśvara</s> by one hundred <s>parārdhas</s> — that is one day of <s>Sadāśiva</s>; an equal period is the night. That itself is the great dissolution (<s>mahāpralaya</s>). [AbhTs 6.49]

children.text: sadāśivaḥ svakālaparikṣaye bindvardhacandranirodhikā ākramya nāde līyate nādaḥ śaktitattve tat vyāpinyāṃ sā ca anāśrite // AbhTs_6.50
children.translated_text: <s>Sadāśiva</s>, upon the exhaustion of his own time, ascending through <s>bindu</s> (point), <s>ardhacandra</s> (half-moon), and <s>nirodhikā</s> (obstruction), dissolves in <s>nāda</s> (resonance); <s>nāda</s> dissolves in the <s>Śakti-tattva</s>; that in <s>Vyāpinī</s> (the All-pervading); and she in <s>Anāśrita</s> (the Supportless). [AbhTs 6.50]

children.text: śaktikālena parārdhakoṭiguṇitena anāśritadinam // AbhTs_6.51
children.translated_text: The time of <s>Śakti</s>, multiplied by a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) of <s>parārdhas</s>, gives one day of <s>Anāśrita</s>. [AbhTs 6.51]

children.text: anāśritaḥ sāmanase pade yat tat sāmanasyaṃ sāmyaṃ tat brahma // AbhTs_6.52
children.translated_text: <s>Anāśrita</s> [dissolves] in the state of mental equilibrium (<s>sāmanasya</s>); that equilibrium, that balance — that is <s>Brahman</s>. [AbhTs 6.52]

children.text: asmāt sāmanasyāt akalyāt kālāt nimeṣonmeṣamātratayā proktāśeṣakālaprasarapravilayacakrabhramodayaḥ // AbhTs_6.53
children.translated_text: From this equilibrium (<s>sāmanasya</s>), from this undivided time, through the mere closing and opening of the eyes [of consciousness], the arising of the whirling wheel of the extension and dissolution of all the previously stated [cycles of] time [takes place]. [AbhTs 6.53]

children.text: ekaṃ daśa śataṃ sahasram ayutaṃ lakṣaṃ niyutaṃ koṭiḥ arbudaṃ vṛndaṃ kharvaṃ nikharvaṃ padmaṃ śaṅkuḥ samudram antyaṃ madhyam parārdham iti krameṇa daśaguṇitāni aṣṭādaśa iti gaṇitavidhiḥ // AbhTs_6.54
children.translated_text: One, ten, hundred, thousand, <s>ayuta</s>, <s>lakṣa</s>, <s>niyuta</s>, <s>koṭi</s>, <s>arbuda</s>, <s>vṛnda</s>, <s>kharva</s>, <s>nikharva</s>, <s>padma</s>, <s>śaṅku</s>, <s>samudra</s>, <s>antya</s>, <s>madhya</s>, <s>parārdha</s> — thus eighteen [denominations], each multiplied tenfold in sequence — this is the method of calculation. [AbhTs 6.54]

children.text: evam asaṃkhyāḥ sṛṣṭipralayāḥ ekasmin mahāsṛṣṭirūpe prāṇe so 'pi saṃvidi sā upādhau sa cinmātre cinmātrasyaiva ayaṃ spando yad ayaṃ kālodayo nāma // AbhTs_6.55
children.translated_text: Thus, innumerable creations and dissolutions [occur] within a single <s>prāṇa</s> that has the form of the great creation; that [prāṇa] too [resides] in awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>); that in the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>); that in pure consciousness (<s>cinmātra</s>). The vibration (<s>spanda</s>) of pure consciousness alone is what is called the arising of time (<s>kālodaya</s>). [AbhTs 6.55]

children.text: tata eva svapnasaṃkalpādau vaicitryam asya na virodhāvaham // AbhTs_6.56
children.translated_text: Therefore, the variety [of time] in dream, imagination, and so forth does not produce any contradiction. [AbhTs 6.56]

children.text: evaṃ yathā prāṇe kālodayaḥ tathā apāne 'pi hṛdayāt mūlapīṭhaparyantam // AbhTs_6.57
children.translated_text: Just as the arising of time occurs in the <s>prāṇa</s>, so too in the <s>apāna</s>, from the heart down to the root-seat (<s>mūlapīṭha</s>). [AbhTs 6.57]

children.text: yathā ca hṛtkaṇṭhatālulalāṭarandhradvādaśānteṣu brahmaviṣṇurudreśasadāśivānāśritākhyaṃ kāraṇaṣaṭkam tathaiva apāne 'pi hṛtkandānandasaṃkocavikāsadvādaśānteṣu bālyayauvanavārddhakanidhanapunarbhavamuktyadhipataya ete // AbhTs_6.58
children.translated_text: And just as in the heart, throat, palate, forehead, aperture, and <s>dvādaśānta</s> (twelve-finger space above) are the six causes named <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, and <s>Anāśrita</s>, so too in the <s>apāna</s>, in the heart, bulb, bliss, contraction, expansion, and <s>dvādaśānta</s> [below], these are the lords of childhood, youth, old age, death, rebirth, and liberation. [AbhTs 6.58]

children.text: atha samāne kālodayaḥ // AbhTs_6.59
children.translated_text: Now, the arising of time in the <s>samāna</s> [breath]. [AbhTs 6.59]

children.text: samāno hārdīṣu daśāsu nāḍīṣu saṃcaran samaste dehe sāmyena rasādīn vāhayati /
children.translated_text: The <s>samāna</s>, circulating in the ten <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) connected to the heart, carries the essences (<s>rasa</s>) and so forth equally throughout the entire body.

children.text: tatra digaṣṭake saṃcaran taddikpaticeṣṭām iva pramātuḥ anukārayati // AbhTs_6.60
children.translated_text: Therein, circulating in the eight directions, it causes the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>) to imitate, as it were, the activity of the guardian of that direction. [AbhTs 6.60]

children.text: ūrdhvādhas tu saṃcaran tisṛṣu nāḍīṣu gatāgataṃ karoti // AbhTs_6.61
children.translated_text: But circulating upward and downward, it moves back and forth in the three <s>nāḍīs</s>. [AbhTs 6.61]

children.text: tatra viṣuvaddine bāhye prabhātakāle sapādāṃ ghaṭikāṃ madhyamārge vahati // AbhTs_6.62
children.translated_text: There, on the equinox day, externally, at dawn, it flows in the middle path for one and a quarter <s>ghaṭikā</s> (24 minutes). [AbhTs 6.62]

children.text: tato navaśatāni prāṇavikṣepāṇām iti gaṇanayā bahiḥ sārdhaghaṭikādvayaṃ vāme dakṣiṇe vāme dakṣiṇe vāme iti pañca saṃkrāntayaḥ // AbhTs_6.63
children.translated_text: Then, by the count of nine hundred breath-exhalations, externally for two and a half <s>ghaṭikās</s>, [it flows] in the left, right, left, right, left — thus five transitions (<s>saṃkrānti</s>). [AbhTs 6.63]

children.text: tataḥ saṃkrāntipañcake vṛtte pādonāsu caturdaśasu ghaṭikāsu atikrāntāsu dakṣiṇaṃ śāradaṃ viṣuvanmadhyāhne nava prāṇaśatāni // AbhTs_6.64
children.translated_text: Then, when the fivefold transition-cycle is completed, in the fourteen <s>ghaṭikās</s> minus a quarter that have elapsed, at the autumnal equinox at midday in the right [channel] — nine hundred breaths. [AbhTs 6.64]

children.text: tato 'pi dakṣiṇe vāme dakṣiṇe vāme dakṣiṇe iti saṃkrāntipañcakaṃ pratyekaṃ navaśatāni ity evaṃ rātrāv api iti // AbhTs_6.65
children.translated_text: And then again, right, left, right, left, right — a fivefold transition-cycle, nine hundred each; likewise also during the night. [AbhTs 6.65]

children.text: evaṃ viṣuvaddivase tadrātrau ca dvādaśa dvādaśa saṃkrāntayaḥ // AbhTs_6.66
children.translated_text: Thus, on the equinox day and its night, twelve and twelve transitions [occur]. [AbhTs 6.66]

children.text: tato dinavṛddhikṣayeṣu saṃkrāntivṛddhikṣayaḥ // AbhTs_6.67
children.translated_text: Then, with the increase and decrease of the day, there is increase and decrease of the transitions. [AbhTs 6.67]

children.text: evam ekasmin samānamaruti varṣadvayaṃ śvāsapraśvāsayogābhāvāt // AbhTs_6.68
children.translated_text: Thus, in one <s>samāna</s> breath, two years [elapse], because of the absence of the conjunction of inhalation and exhalation. [AbhTs 6.68]

children.text: atrāpi dvādaśābdodayādi pūrvavat // AbhTs_6.69
children.translated_text: Here too, the arising of a twelve-year [cycle] and so forth is as before. [AbhTs 6.69]

children.text: udāne tu dvādaśāntāvadhiś cāraḥ spandamātrātmanaḥ kālasya // AbhTs_6.70
children.translated_text: But in the <s>udāna</s>, the movement of time, whose nature is mere vibration (<s>spandamātra</s>), extends up to the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (twelve-finger space). [AbhTs 6.70]

children.text: atrāpi pūrvavat vidhiḥ // AbhTs_6.71
children.translated_text: Here too, the procedure is as before. [AbhTs 6.71]

children.text: vyāne tu vyāpakatvāt akrame 'pi sūkṣmocchalattāyogena kālodayaḥ // AbhTs_6.72
children.translated_text: But in the <s>vyāna</s>, because of its all-pervasiveness, even in the absence of succession, the arising of time occurs through the connection with subtle pulsation. [AbhTs 6.72]

children.text: atha varṇodayaḥ // AbhTs_6.73
children.translated_text: Now, the arising of phonemes (<s>varṇodaya</s>). [AbhTs 6.73]

children.text: tatra ardhaprahare ardhaprahare vargodayo viṣuvati samaḥ varṇasya varṇasya dve śate ṣoḍaśādhike prāṇānām bahiḥ ṣaṭtriṃśat caṣakāṇi iti udayaḥ ayam ayatnajo varṇodayaḥ // AbhTs_6.74
children.translated_text: There, in each half-<s>prahara</s> (approximately 1.5 hours), on the equinox, the arising of a phoneme-group occurs equally: for each phoneme, two hundred and sixteen breaths; externally, thirty-six <s>caṣakas</s> — this is the spontaneous arising of phonemes (<s>varṇodaya</s>). [AbhTs 6.74]

children.text: yatnajas tu mantrodayaḥ araghaṭṭaghaṭīyantravāhanavat ekānusaṃdhibalāt citraṃ mantrodayaṃ divāniśam anusaṃdadhat mantradevatayā saha tādātmyam eti // AbhTs_6.75
children.translated_text: But the effortful [arising] is the arising of <s>mantra</s>: like the mechanism of a water-wheel (<s>araghaṭṭa</s>), by the force of continuous single-pointed focus, contemplating the wondrous arising of <s>mantra</s> day and night, one attains identity with the <s>mantra</s>-deity. [AbhTs 6.75]

children.text: tatra sadodite prāṇacārasaṃkhyayaiva udayasaṃkhyā vyākhyātā taddviguṇite tadardham ityādi krameṇa aṣṭottaraśate cakre dviśata udayaḥ iti krameṇa sthūlasūkṣme cārasvarūpe viśrāntasya prāṇacāre kṣīṇe kālagrāse vṛtte sampūrṇām ekam evedaṃ saṃvedanaṃ citraśaktinirbharaṃ bhāsate // AbhTs_6.76
children.translated_text: There, in the ever-arisen [mantra], the count of arisings is explained by the very count of the breath-cycle; when doubled, half of that, and so on — in the wheel of one hundred and eight, with two hundred arisings — thus sequentially, when one who has rested in the gross and subtle forms of the breath-cycle, with the breath-cycle exhausted and the consumption of time accomplished, this single awareness alone shines forth — complete, full, brimming with the variegated power [of consciousness]. [AbhTs 6.76]

children.text: kālabheda eva saṃvedanabhedakaḥ na vedyabhedaḥ śikharasthajñānavat jñānasya yāvān avasthitikālaḥ sa eva kṣaṇaḥ prāṇodaye ca ekasmin ekam eva jñānam avaśyaṃ caitat anyathā vikalpajñānam ekaṃ na kiṃcit syāt kramikaśabdārūṣitatvāt mātrāyā api kramikatvāt // AbhTs_6.77
children.translated_text: It is the division of time alone that divides awareness, not the division of objects — like the knowledge of one standing on a peak. The duration of a cognition is its moment (<s>kṣaṇa</s>). And in one arising of <s>prāṇa</s>, there is necessarily only one cognition. Otherwise, not a single conceptual cognition would exist, since it consists of sequential phonemes, and even a <s>mātrā</s> (phonemic unit) is sequential. [AbhTs 6.77]

children.text: yad āha tasyādita udāttam ardhahrasvam iti // AbhTs_6.78
children.translated_text: As it is said: 'Of that, the first [half is] high-pitched, [lasting] half a short [vowel].' [AbhTs 6.78]

children.text: tasmāt spandāntaraṃ yāvat na uditaṃ tāvat ekam eva jñānam // AbhTs_6.79
children.translated_text: Therefore, as long as the next vibration (<s>spanda</s>) has not arisen, so long there is only one cognition. [AbhTs 6.79]

children.text: ata eva ekāśīti padasmaraṇasamaye vividhadharmānupraveśamukhena eka eva asau parameśvaraviṣayo vikalpaḥ kālagrāse na avikalpātmā eva sampadyate iti // AbhTs_6.80
children.translated_text: For this very reason, at the time of remembering the eighty-one words, through the entry of various properties, that single conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) pertaining to the Supreme Lord, at the time of the consumption of time (<s>kālagrāsa</s>), becomes non-conceptual (<s>avikalpa</s>) in nature. [AbhTs 6.80]

children.text: evam akhilaṃ kālādhvānaṃ prāṇodaya eva paśyan sṛṣṭisaṃhārāṃś ca vicitrān niḥsaṃkhyān tatraiva ākalayan ātmana eva pārameśvaryaṃ pratyabhijānan mukta eva bhavati iti // AbhTs_6.81
children.translated_text: Thus, seeing the entire path of time (<s>kālādhvan</s>) in the very arising of <s>prāṇa</s>, and calculating the innumerable and varied creations and dissolutions within it, recognizing one's own supreme sovereignty (<s>pārameśvarya</s>) — one is indeed liberated. [AbhTs 6.81]

children.text: saṃvidrūpasyātmanaḥ prāṇaśaktiṃ paśyan rūpaṃ tatragaṃ cātikālam /
children.translated_text: Seeing the power of <s>prāṇa</s> as the form of the Self whose nature is awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>), and the form dwelling therein as transcending time,

children.text: sākaṃ sṛṣṭisthemasaṃhāracakrair nityodyukto bhairavībhāvam eti // AbhTs_6.82
children.translated_text: together with the wheels of creation, maintenance, and dissolution, one who is ever engaged attains the state of <s>Bhairava</s>. [AbhTs 6.82]

children.text: tatra samasta eva ayaṃ mūrtivaicitryābhāsanaśaktijo deśādhvā saṃvidi viśrāntaḥ taddvāreṇa śūnye buddhau prāṇe nāḍīcakrānucakreṣu bahiḥ śarīre yāval liṅgasthaṇḍilapratimādau samasto 'dhvā pariniṣṭhitaḥ taṃ samastam adhvānaṃ dehe vilāpya dehaṃ ca prāṇe taṃ dhiyi tāṃ śūnye tatsaṃvedane nirbharaparipūrṇasaṃvit sampadyate ṣaṭtriṃśattattvasvarūpajñaḥ taduttīrṇāṃ saṃvidaṃ paramaśivarūpāṃ paśyan viśvamayīm api saṃvedayeta aparathā vedyabhāgam eva kaṃcit paratvena gṛhṇīyān māyāgarbhādhikāriṇaṃ viṣṇubrahmādikaṃ vā tasmād avaśyaṃ prakriyājñānapareṇa bhavitavyam // AbhTs_7.1
children.translated_text: Here, this entire spatial path (<s>deśādhvan</s>), produced by the power of manifesting the variety of forms, rests in awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>). Through that, in the void (<s>śūnya</s>), in the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), in <s>prāṇa</s>, in the <s>nāḍī</s>-wheels and sub-wheels, externally in the body, up to the <s>liṅga</s>, platform, and image — the entire path is established. Having dissolved the entire path into the body, and the body into <s>prāṇa</s>, that into the intellect, that into the void, and that into pure awareness — one becomes fully and completely replete awareness, a knower of the true nature of the thirty-six <s>tattvas</s> (principles). One who sees the awareness that transcends them, having the form of <s>Paramaśiva</s>, should experience it as pervading the universe as well. Otherwise, one would grasp only some portion of the knowable as supreme — [merely] an authority within the womb of <s>Māyā</s>, or <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the like. Therefore, one must necessarily be devoted to procedural knowledge (<s>prakriyā-jñāna</s>). [AbhTs 7.1]

children.text: tad uktaṃ na prakriyāparaṃ jñānam iti // AbhTs_7.2
children.translated_text: As it is said: 'There is no knowledge [superior to] that devoted to procedure.' [AbhTs 7.2]

children.text: tatra pṛthivītattvaṃ śatakoṭipravistīrṇaṃ brahmāṇḍagolakarūpam // AbhTs_7.3
children.translated_text: There, the earth-principle (<s>pṛthivī-tattva</s>), extending one hundred <s>koṭis</s> (billion [yojanas]), has the form of the sphere of the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>). [AbhTs 7.3]

children.text: tasya antaḥ kālāgnir narakāḥ pātālāni pṛthivī svargo yāvad brahmaloka iti // AbhTs_7.4
children.translated_text: Within it are: the fire of time (<s>kālāgni</s>), the hells, the netherworlds (<s>pātāla</s>), the earth, heaven, up to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>. [AbhTs 7.4]

children.text: brahmāṇḍabāhye rudrāṇāṃ śatam // AbhTs_7.5
children.translated_text: Outside the cosmic egg are a hundred <s>Rudras</s>. [AbhTs 7.5]

children.text: na ca brahmāṇḍānāṃ saṃkhyā vidyate // AbhTs_7.6
children.translated_text: And there is no count of the cosmic eggs. [AbhTs 7.6]

children.text: tato dharātattvād daśaguṇaṃ jalatattvam // AbhTs_7.7
children.translated_text: Then, from the earth-principle, the water-principle (<s>jala-tattva</s>) is ten times [larger]. [AbhTs 7.7]

children.text: tata uttarottaraṃ daśaguṇam ahaṃkārāntam // AbhTs_7.8
children.translated_text: Then, each successive [principle] is ten times [larger], up to <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego). [AbhTs 7.8]

children.text: tad yathā jalaṃ tejo vāyur nabhaḥ tanmātrapañcakākṣaikādaśagarbho 'haṃkāraś ceti // AbhTs_7.9
children.translated_text: Namely: water, fire (<s>tejas</s>), wind (<s>vāyu</s>), space (<s>nabhas</s>), the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), the eleven sense-organs contained in <s>ahaṃkāra</s>. [AbhTs 7.9]

children.text: ahaṃkārāt śataguṇaṃ buddhitattvam // AbhTs_7.10
children.translated_text: From <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, the <s>buddhi-tattva</s> (intellect-principle) is one hundred times [larger]. [AbhTs 7.10]

children.text: tataḥ sahasradhā prakṛtitattvam etāvat prakṛtyaṇḍam // AbhTs_7.11
children.translated_text: From that, the <s>prakṛti-tattva</s> (primordial nature) is one thousand times [larger]; this much constitutes the <s>prakṛtyaṇḍa</s> (egg of <s>Prakṛti</s>). [AbhTs 7.11]

children.text: tac ca brahmāṇḍavad asaṃkhyam // AbhTs_7.12
children.translated_text: And that, like the cosmic egg, is innumerable. [AbhTs 7.12]

children.text: prakṛtitattvāt puruṣatattvaṃ ca daśasahasradhā // AbhTs_7.13
children.translated_text: From the <s>prakṛti-tattva</s>, the <s>puruṣa-tattva</s> (self-principle) is ten thousand times [larger]. [AbhTs 7.13]

children.text: puruṣān niyatiḥ lakṣadhā // AbhTs_7.14
children.translated_text: From <s>puruṣa</s>, <s>niyati</s> (determination) is one hundred thousand times [larger]. [AbhTs 7.14]

children.text: niyater uttarottaraṃ daśalakṣadhā kalātattvāntam // AbhTs_7.15
children.translated_text: From <s>niyati</s>, each successive [principle] is ten times one hundred thousand, up to the <s>kalā-tattva</s> (limited agency). [AbhTs 7.15]

children.text: tad yathā niyatiḥ rāgo 'śuddhavidyā kālaḥ kalā ceti // AbhTs_7.16
children.translated_text: Namely: <s>niyati</s>, <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>aśuddha-vidyā</s> (impure knowledge), <s>kāla</s> (time), and <s>kalā</s> (limited agency). [AbhTs 7.16]

children.text: kalātattvāt koṭidhā māyā etāvat māyāṇḍam // AbhTs_7.17
children.translated_text: From the <s>kalā-tattva</s>, <s>Māyā</s> is one <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) times [larger]; this much constitutes the <s>Māyāṇḍa</s> (egg of <s>Māyā</s>). [AbhTs 7.17]

children.text: māyātattvāt śuddhavidyā daśakoṭiguṇitā // AbhTs_7.18
children.translated_text: From the <s>Māyā-tattva</s>, <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (pure knowledge) is multiplied by ten <s>koṭis</s>. [AbhTs 7.18]

children.text: vidyātattvād īśvaratattvaṃ śatakoṭidhā // AbhTs_7.19
children.translated_text: From the <s>Vidyā-tattva</s>, the <s>Īśvara-tattva</s> (Lord-principle) is one hundred <s>koṭis</s> times [larger]. [AbhTs 7.19]

children.text: īśvaratattvāt sādākhyaṃ sahasrakoṭidhā // AbhTs_7.20
children.translated_text: From the <s>Īśvara-tattva</s>, <s>Sadākhya</s> (<s>Sadāśiva</s>) is one thousand <s>koṭis</s> times [larger]. [AbhTs 7.20]

children.text: sādākhyāt vṛndaguṇitaṃ śaktitattvam iti śaktyaṇḍam // AbhTs_7.21
children.translated_text: From <s>Sadākhya</s>, the <s>Śakti-tattva</s> (power-principle) is multiplied by a <s>vṛnda</s>; this constitutes the <s>Śaktyaṇḍa</s> (egg of <s>Śakti</s>). [AbhTs 7.21]

children.text: sā śaktir vyāpya yato viśvam adhvānam antarbahir āste tasmād vyāpinī // AbhTs_7.22
children.translated_text: That <s>Śakti</s>, because she pervades the entire universe and the path, abiding within and without, is called <s>Vyāpinī</s> (the All-pervading). [AbhTs 7.22]

children.text: evam etāni uttarottaram āvaraṇatayā vartamānāni tattvāny uttaraṃ vyāpakaṃ pūrvaṃ vyāpyam iti sthityā vartante // AbhTs_7.23
children.translated_text: Thus, these <s>tattvas</s>, existing as successive envelopes, with the latter pervading and the former pervaded — they exist in this arrangement. [AbhTs 7.23]

children.text: yāvad aśeṣaśaktitattvānto 'dhvā śivatattvena vyāptaḥ // AbhTs_7.24
children.translated_text: Up to the entire <s>Śakti-tattva</s>, the path is pervaded by the <s>Śiva-tattva</s>. [AbhTs 7.24]

children.text: śivatattvaṃ punar aparimeyaṃ sarvādhvottīrṇaṃ sarvādhvavyāpakaṃ ca // AbhTs_7.25
children.translated_text: The <s>Śiva-tattva</s>, moreover, is immeasurable, transcending all paths and pervading all paths. [AbhTs 7.25]

children.text: etat tattvāntarālavartīni yāni bhuvanāni tatpataya eva atra pṛthivyāṃ sthitā iti // AbhTs_7.26
children.translated_text: The worlds (<s>bhuvana</s>) that exist in the interstices of these <s>tattvas</s>, their lords — they are established here on earth. [AbhTs 7.26]

children.text: teṣv āyataneṣu ye mriyante teṣāṃ tatra tatra gatiṃ te vitaranti // AbhTs_7.27
children.translated_text: Those who die in those abodes — those [lords] distribute their destinies to the respective [realms]. [AbhTs 7.27]

children.text: kramāc ca ūrdhvordhvaṃ prerayanti dīkṣākrameṇa // AbhTs_7.28
children.translated_text: And they propel [beings] successively higher and higher, by the sequence of initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>). [AbhTs 7.28]

children.text: yad idaṃ vibhavātmakaṃ bhuvanajātam uktaṃ garbhīkṛtānantavicitrabhoktṛbhogyaṃ tatra yad anugataṃ mahāprakāśarūpaṃ tat mahāsāmānyakalpaṃ paramaśivarūpam // AbhTs_8.1
children.translated_text: This multitude of worlds (<s>bhuvana</s>), which has been described as having the nature of manifestation (<s>vibhava</s>), containing within it infinite and variegated experiencers and objects of experience — therein, that which pervades it and has the form of the great light (<s>mahāprakāśa</s>), like a great universal, has the form of <s>Paramaśiva</s>. [AbhTs 8.1]

children.text: yat tu katipayakatipayabhedānugataṃ rūpaṃ tat tattvaṃ yathā pṛthivī nāma dyutikāṭhinyasthaulyādirūpā kālāgniprabhṛtivīrabhadrāntabhuvaneśādhiṣṭhitasamastabrahmāṇḍānugatā // AbhTs_8.2
children.translated_text: But that form which pervades only certain specific divisions is a <s>tattva</s> (principle); for example, 'earth' (<s>pṛthivī</s>) has the form of radiance, hardness, grossness, and so forth, and pervades all the cosmic eggs presided over by the world-lords from <s>Kālāgni</s> up to <s>Vīrabhadra</s>. [AbhTs 8.2]

children.text: tatra eṣāṃ tattvānāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvo darśyate sa ca dvividhaḥ // AbhTs_8.3
children.translated_text: There, the causal relation of these <s>tattvas</s> is to be shown; and it is twofold. [AbhTs 8.3]

children.text: pāramārthikaḥ sṛṣṭeś ca // AbhTs_8.4
children.translated_text: Ultimate (<s>pāramārthika</s>) and pertaining to creation. [AbhTs 8.4]

children.text: tatra pāramārthika etāvān kāryakāraṇabhāvo yad uta kartṛsvabhāvasya svatantrasya bhagavata evaṃvidhena śivādidharāntena vapuṣā svarūpabhinnena svarūpaviśrāntena ca prathanam // AbhTs_8.5
children.translated_text: There, the ultimate causal relation is this much: the manifestation of the autonomous Blessed Lord, whose nature is that of the agent (<s>kartṛ</s>), in such a form — from <s>Śiva</s> down to earth — which is both non-different from his own nature and resting in his own nature. [AbhTs 8.5]

children.text: kalpitas tu kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ parameśecchayā niyatiprāṇayā nirmitaḥ sa ca yāvati yadā niyatapaurvāparyāvabhāsanaṃ saty api adhike svarūpānugatam etāvaty eva tena yogīcchāto 'pi aṅkuro bījād api svapnādau ghaṭāder apīti // AbhTs_8.6
children.translated_text: But the constructed cause-and-effect relationship is produced by the will of the Supreme Lord, animated by <s>Niyati</s> (the principle of regulation). And it [operates] to the extent that, when there is the manifestation of a fixed sequence, even though what is additional also follows its own essential nature, to just that extent [it operates]. Therefore, even by the will of a <s>yogin</s>, a sprout [arises] from a seed, and in dreams and such, even a pot etc. [may appear]. [AbhTs 8.6]

children.text: tatrāpi ca parameśvarasya kartṛtvānapāya iti akalpito 'pi asau pāramārthikaḥ sthita eva // AbhTs_8.7
children.translated_text: Even in that [case], the creatorship of the Supreme Lord does not depart. Therefore, even though unconstructed, that [cause-and-effect relationship] exists as ultimately real. [AbhTs 8.7]

children.text: pāramārthike hi bhittisthānīye sthite rūpe sarvam idam ullikhyamānaṃ ghaṭate na anyathā ata eva sāmagryā eva kāruṇatvaṃ yuktam // AbhTs_8.8
children.translated_text: For when the form that stands in the place of a canvas is established as ultimately real, all this that is being sketched upon it is possible, not otherwise. Therefore, it is proper that creatorship belongs to the aggregate of conditions (<s>sāmagrī</s>) alone. [AbhTs 8.8]

children.text: sā hi samastabhāvasaṃdarbhamayī svatantrasaṃvedanamahimnā tathā niyatanijanijadeśakālabhāvarāśisvabhāvā pratyekaṃ vastusvarūpaniṣpattisamaye tathābhūtā tathābhūtāyā hi anyathābhāvo yathā yathā adhikībhavati tathā tathā kāryasyāpi vijātīyatvaṃ tāratamyena puṣyati // AbhTs_8.9
children.translated_text: For that [aggregate of conditions], consisting of the arrangement of all entities, by the glory of autonomous awareness (<s>svatantrasaṃvedana</s>), having a nature such that the mass of entities in its own fixed place, time, and realm is of a specific kind—at the time of the production of the essential nature of each individual thing, it is of such and such a form. And of that which is of such and such a form, to the extent that its becoming otherwise increases, to that extent the heterogeneity of the effect also grows proportionally. [AbhTs 8.9]

children.text: ity evaṃ saṃvedanasvātantryasvabhāvaḥ parameśvara eva viśvabhāvaśarīro ghaṭāder nirmātā kumbhakārasaṃvidas tato 'nadhikatvāt kumbhakāraśarīrasya ca bhāvarāśimadhye nikṣepāt kathaṃ kumbhakāraśarīrasya kartṛtvābhimānaḥ iti cet parameśvarakṛta evāsau ghaṭādivat bhaviṣyati // AbhTs_8.10
children.translated_text: Thus, the Supreme Lord himself, whose nature is the autonomy of awareness (<s>saṃvedanasvātantrya</s>), whose body is all entities of the universe, is the creator of pots and the like. The awareness of the potter, being not superior to that [Supreme Lord], and the body of the potter being deposited among the mass of entities—how then can the body of the potter claim creatorship? If [you ask this], that [claim] will be created by the Supreme Lord himself, just like pots and the like. [AbhTs 8.10]

children.text: tasmāt sāmagrīvādo 'pi viśvaśarīrasya saṃvedanasyaiva kartṛtāyām upodbalakaḥ // AbhTs_8.11
children.translated_text: Therefore, even the doctrine of the aggregate of conditions (<s>sāmagrīvāda</s>) serves to support the creatorship of awareness (<s>saṃvedana</s>) alone, whose body is the universe. [AbhTs 8.11]

children.text: merau hi tatrasthe na bhavet tathāvidho ghaṭaḥ // AbhTs_8.12
children.translated_text: For if [the potter stood] on Mount <s>Meru</s>, a pot of that particular kind would not come into being there. [AbhTs 8.12]

children.text: evaṃ kalpite 'smin kāryatve śāstreṣu tattvānāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvaṃ prati yat bahuprakāratvaṃ tad api saṃgataṃ gomayāt kīṭāt yogīcchāto mantrād auṣadhāt vṛścikodayavat // AbhTs_8.13
children.translated_text: Thus, when this causal efficacy is construed [in this way], the multiplicity of forms regarding the cause-and-effect relationship of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles) in the scriptures is also consistent—as in [the production of a scorpion] from cow-dung, from an insect, from the will of a <s>yogin</s>, from a <s>mantra</s>, from a medicine, like the arising of a scorpion. [AbhTs 8.13]

children.text: tatra nijatantradṛśā taṃ kalpitaṃ darśayāmaḥ // AbhTs_8.14
children.translated_text: There, we shall show that constructed [cause-and-effect relationship] from the perspective of our own <s>tantra</s> (system). [AbhTs 8.14]

children.text: tatra parameśvaraḥ pañcabhiḥ śaktibhiḥ nirbhara ity uktam sa svātantryāt śaktiṃ tāṃ tāṃ mukhyatayā prakaṭayan pañcadhā tiṣṭhati // AbhTs_8.15
children.translated_text: There, it has been said that the Supreme Lord is replete with five powers (<s>śakti</s>s). By his autonomy, prominently manifesting this or that power, he abides in fivefold manner. [AbhTs 8.15]

children.text: citprādhānye śivatattvam ānandaprādhānye śaktitattvam icchāprādhānye sadāśivatattvam icchāyā hi jñānakriyayoḥ sāmyarūpābhyupagamātmakatvāt jñānaśaktiprādhānye īśvaratattvam kriyāśaktiprādhānye vidyātattvam iti // AbhTs_8.16
children.translated_text: When consciousness (<s>cit</s>) predominates, it is <s>Śiva-tattva</s>; when bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) predominates, it is <s>Śakti-tattva</s>; when will (<s>icchā</s>) predominates, it is <s>Sadāśiva-tattva</s>—for will has the nature of embracing the equality-form of knowledge and action; when the power of knowledge (<s>jñānaśakti</s>) predominates, it is <s>Īśvara-tattva</s>; when the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>) predominates, it is <s>Vidyā-tattva</s>. [AbhTs 8.16]

children.text: atra ca tattveśvarāḥ śivaśaktisadāśiveśvarānantāḥ brahmeva nivṛttau eṣāṃ sāmānyarūpāṇāṃ viśeṣā anugativiṣayāḥ pañca tadyathā śāmbhavāḥ śāktāḥ mantramaheśvarāḥ mantreśvarāḥ mantrā iti śuddhādhvā // AbhTs_8.17
children.translated_text: And here, the lords of these <s>tattvas</s> are <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and <s>Ananta</s>—like <s>Brahmā</s> in <s>Nivṛtti</s> [<s>kalā</s>]. The particulars of these, which are of a general nature, are the objects of experience [in their respective domains]—five [categories], namely: <s>Śāmbhavas</s>, <s>Śāktas</s>, <s>Mantramaheśvaras</s>, <s>Mantreśvaras</s>, and <s>Mantras</s>. This is the pure course (<s>śuddhādhvan</s>). [AbhTs 8.17]

children.text: iyati sākṣāt śivaḥ kartā aśuddhaṃ punar adhvānam anantāparanāmāghoreśaḥ sṛjati īśvarecchāvaśena prakṣubdhabhogalolikānām aṇūnāṃ bhogasiddhyartham // AbhTs_8.18
children.translated_text: To this extent, <s>Śiva</s> is directly the creator. The impure course (<s>aśuddhādhvan</s>), however, is created by <s>Aghoreśa</s>, otherwise known as <s>Ananta</s>, by the will of <s>Īśvara</s>, for the sake of accomplishing the enjoyment of the <s>aṇus</s> (individual souls) who are agitated by their craving for experience (<s>bhogalolikā</s>). [AbhTs 8.18]

children.text: tatra loliko 'pūrṇam anyatārūpaḥ parispandaḥ akarmakam abhilāṣamātram eva bhaviṣyad avacchedayogyateti na malaḥ puṃsas tattvāntaram // AbhTs_8.19
children.translated_text: There, the craving (<s>lolikā</s>) is an incomplete movement of the nature of 'something other,' a mere objectless desire that will be susceptible to limitation—it is <s>mala</s> (impurity). The <s>mala</s> of the individual soul (<s>puṃs</s>) is not a separate <s>tattva</s> (principle). [AbhTs 8.19]

children.text: rāgatattvaṃ tu karmāvacchinno 'bhilāṣaḥ // AbhTs_8.20
children.translated_text: The <s>Rāga-tattva</s> (principle of attachment), however, is desire delimited by action (<s>karma</s>). [AbhTs 8.20]

children.text: karma tu tatra karmamātraṃ buddhidharmas tu rāgaḥ karmabhedacitra iti vibhāgo vakṣyate // AbhTs_8.21
children.translated_text: And <s>karma</s> (action) there is mere action, while <s>rāga</s> (attachment) is a property of the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>)—diversified by the variety of actions; this distinction will be explained. [AbhTs 8.21]

children.text: so 'yaṃ malaḥ parameśvarasya svātmapracchādanecchātaḥ nānyat kiṃcit vastv api ca tatparameśvarecchātmanaiva dharāder api vastutvāt // AbhTs_8.22
children.translated_text: This <s>mala</s> (impurity) arises from the Supreme Lord's desire to conceal his own Self—it is nothing other [than that]. Moreover, since even earth and the other [elements] have their reality through the will of the Supreme Lord, [mala too is of the same nature]. [AbhTs 8.22]

children.text: sa ca malo vijñānakevale vidyamāno dhvaṃsonmukha iti na svakāryaṃ karma āpyāyati // AbhTs_8.23
children.translated_text: And that <s>mala</s>, being present in the <s>vijñānakevala</s> (a soul freed from <s>karma</s> and <s>māyā</s> but not from <s>mala</s>), is on the verge of dissolution, and therefore does not nourish its own product, <s>karma</s>. [AbhTs 8.23]

children.text: pralayakevalasya tu jṛmbhamāṇa eva āsta iti malopodbalitaṃ karma saṃsāravaicitryabhoge nimittam iti tadbhogavāsanānuviddhānām aṇūnāṃ bhogasiddhaye śrīmān aghoreśaḥ sṛjati iti yuktam uktaṃ malasya ca prakṣobha īśvarecchābalād eva jaḍasya svataḥ kutracid api asāmarthyāt // AbhTs_8.24
children.translated_text: But for the <s>pralayakevala</s> (a soul freed only from <s>māyā</s>), it continues to expand. Therefore, <s>karma</s>, reinforced by <s>mala</s>, is the cause of the variety of enjoyment in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). For the sake of accomplishing enjoyment for the <s>aṇus</s> (individual souls) pervaded by the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of that enjoyment, the glorious <s>Aghoreśa</s> creates—this is rightly stated. And the agitation of <s>mala</s> is by the force of <s>Īśvara's</s> will alone, since [mala], being inert (<s>jaḍa</s>), has no capacity of its own in any respect. [AbhTs 8.24]

children.text: aṇur nāma kila cidacidrūpāvabhāsa eva tasya cidrūpam aiśvaryam eva acidrūpataiva malaḥ tasya ca sṛjataḥ parameśvarecchāmayaṃ tata eva ca nityaṃ srakṣyamāṇavastugatasya rūpasya jaḍatayābhāsayiṣyamāṇatvāt jaḍaṃ sakalakāryavyāpanādirūpatvāc ca vyāpakaṃ māyākhyaṃ tattvam upādānakāraṇaṃ tadavabhāsakāriṇī ca parameśvarasya māyā nāma śaktis tato 'nyaiva // AbhTs_8.25
children.translated_text: The <s>aṇu</s> (individual soul) is indeed nothing but an appearance of the form of both consciousness (<s>cit</s>) and non-consciousness (<s>acit</s>). Its conscious nature is lordship (<s>aiśvarya</s>) itself. Its non-conscious nature alone is <s>mala</s> (impurity). And the form of the thing to be created, which always belongs to what is about to be created by that [Supreme Lord], because it is to be manifested as inert—that inert [principle], because of its nature as pervading all effects and such—is the <s>tattva</s> (principle) called <s>Māyā</s>, the material cause (<s>upādānakāraṇa</s>). And the power of the Supreme Lord that causes the manifestation of that [Māyā] is called <s>Māyā-śakti</s> (the power of Māyā)—it is something quite different [from the tattva called Māyā]. [AbhTs 8.25]

children.text: evaṃ kalāditattvānāṃ dharāntānām api dvairūpyaṃ nirūpyam // AbhTs_8.26
children.translated_text: Thus, the dual nature of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles) from <s>Kalā</s> down to <s>Dharā</s> (earth) should also be determined. [AbhTs 8.26]

children.text: atra ca dvairūpye pramāṇam api āhur abhinavaguptaguravaḥ // AbhTs_8.27
children.translated_text: And here, regarding this dual nature, the gurus of <s>Abhinavagupta</s> also state a proof. [AbhTs 8.27]

children.text: yat saṃkalpe bhāti tat pṛthagbhūtaṃ bahir api asti sphuṭena vapuṣā ghaṭa iva // AbhTs_8.28
children.translated_text: That which appears in thought (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) also exists separately outside, with a manifest form, like a pot. [AbhTs 8.28]

children.text: tathā ca māyākalādikhapuṣpāder api eṣaiva vartanī iti kevalānvayī hetuḥ // AbhTs_8.29
children.translated_text: And thus, this is the very course [of reasoning] for <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Kalā</s>, and even for sky-flowers and such—an invariably concomitant reason (<s>kevalānvayī hetu</s>). [AbhTs 8.29]

children.text: anena ca māyākalāprakṛtibuddhyādiviṣayaṃ sākṣātkārarūpaṃ jñānaṃ ye bhajante te 'pi siddhāḥ siddhā eva // AbhTs_8.30
children.translated_text: And by this [reasoning], those who attain knowledge in the form of direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) concerning <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Kalā</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Buddhi</s>, and such objects—they too are perfected ones (<s>siddha</s>), indeed perfected. [AbhTs 8.30]

children.text: evaṃ sthite māyātattvāt viśvaprasavaḥ // AbhTs_8.31
children.translated_text: This being so, from the <s>Māyā-tattva</s> is the production of the universe. [AbhTs 8.31]

children.text: sa ca yady api akramam eva tathāpi uktadṛśā kramo 'vabhāsate iti // AbhTs_8.32
children.translated_text: And although this [production] is indeed without sequence, nevertheless, from the perspective described, sequence does appear in manifestation. [AbhTs 8.32]

children.text: so 'pi ucyate tatra pratyātma kalādivargo bhinnaḥ // AbhTs_8.33
children.translated_text: That [sequence] too is described: there, the group of <s>Kalā</s> and the rest is distinct for each individual self (<s>pratyātma</s>). [AbhTs 8.33]

children.text: tatkāryasya kartṛtvopodbalanādeḥ pratyātmabhedena upalambhāt sa tu vargaḥ kadācit ekībhavet api īśvarecchayā sāmājikātmanām iva tatra sarvo 'yaṃ kalādivargaḥ śuddhaḥ yaḥ parameśvaraviṣayatayā tatsvarūpalābhānuguṇanijakāryakārī saṃsārapratidvaṃdvitvāt // AbhTs_8.34
children.translated_text: Since its effect—the reinforcement of creatorship and the like—is perceived as differing for each individual self. However, that group may sometimes become unified by the will of <s>Īśvara</s>, as in the case of members of an audience (<s>sāmājikātman</s>). There, this entire group of <s>Kalā</s> and the rest is pure when, having the Supreme Lord as its object, it performs its own function in accordance with the attainment of his essential nature, because it is opposed to <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). [AbhTs 8.34]

children.text: sa ca parameśvaraśaktipātavaśāt tathā bhavati iti vakṣyāmas tatprakāśane // AbhTs_8.35
children.translated_text: And it becomes so by the force of the descent of the Supreme Lord's power (<s>śaktipāta</s>)—this we shall explain in the chapter on the manifestation of that [śaktipāta]. [AbhTs 8.35]

children.text: aśuddhas tu tadviparītaḥ // AbhTs_8.36
children.translated_text: The impure [group], however, is the opposite of that. [AbhTs 8.36]

children.text: tatra māyātaḥ kalā jātā yā suptasthānīyam aṇuṃ kiṃcitkartṛtvena yunakti sā ca ucchūnateva saṃsārabījasya māyāṇvor ubhayoḥ saṃyogāt utpannāpi māyāṃ vikaroti na avikāryam aṇum iti māyākāryatvam asyāḥ // AbhTs_8.37
children.translated_text: There, from <s>Māyā</s> is born <s>Kalā</s> (the principle of limited agency), which endows the <s>aṇu</s> (individual soul)—who stands in the place of one asleep—with a little creatorship (<s>kiṃcitkartṛtva</s>). And it, being like a swelling of the seed of <s>saṃsāra</s>, though produced from the conjunction of both <s>Māyā</s> and <s>aṇu</s>, transforms <s>Māyā</s> but not the untransformable <s>aṇu</s>—hence its being a product of <s>Māyā</s>. [AbhTs 8.37]

children.text: evam anyonyaśleṣāt alakṣaṇīyāntaratvaṃ puṃskalayoḥ // AbhTs_8.38
children.translated_text: Thus, due to mutual embrace, the boundary between the individual soul (<s>puṃs</s>) and <s>Kalā</s> is indistinguishable. [AbhTs 8.38]

children.text: māyāgarbhādhikāriṇas tu kasyacid īśvarasya prasādāt sarvakarmakṣaye māyāpuruṣaviveko bhavati yena māyordhve vijñānākala āste na jātucit māyādhaḥ kalāpuṃviveko vā yena kalordhve tiṣṭhati // AbhTs_8.39
children.translated_text: However, for one who has jurisdiction within <s>Māyā</s> (<s>māyāgarbhādhikārin</s>), by the grace of a certain <s>Īśvara</s>, upon the exhaustion of all <s>karma</s>, there occurs the discrimination between <s>Māyā</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> (the individual soul), by which he becomes a <s>vijñānākala</s> (one freed from <s>karma</s> and <s>māyā</s>) above <s>Māyā</s> and never [falls] below <s>Māyā</s>. Or [there may be] discrimination between <s>Kalā</s> and <s>Puṃs</s>, by which he remains above <s>Kalā</s>. [AbhTs 8.39]

children.text: prakṛtipuruṣaviveko vā yena pradhānādho na saṃsaret // AbhTs_8.40
children.translated_text: Or there may be discrimination between <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, by which he does not transmigrate below <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial nature). [AbhTs 8.40]

children.text: malapuruṣaviveke tu śivasamānatvam // AbhTs_8.41
children.translated_text: But in the discrimination between <s>mala</s> (impurity) and <s>Puruṣa</s>, there is equality with <s>Śiva</s>. [AbhTs 8.41]

children.text: puruṣapūrṇatādṛṣṭau tu śivatvam eveti // AbhTs_8.42
children.translated_text: And in the vision of the completeness of <s>Puruṣa</s>, there is <s>Śivatva</s> (the state of being <s>Śiva</s>) itself. [AbhTs 8.42]

children.text: evaṃ kalātattvam eva kiṃcitkartṛtvadāyi na ca // AbhTs_8.43
children.translated_text: Thus, it is the <s>Kalā-tattva</s> alone that bestows limited creatorship (<s>kiṃcitkartṛtva</s>), but not— [AbhTs 8.43]

children.text: kartṛtvam ajñasya iti // AbhTs_8.44
children.translated_text: creatorship of one who is ignorant. [AbhTs 8.44]

children.text: kiṃcijjñatvadāyiny aśuddhavidyā kalāto jātā sā ca vidyā buddhiṃ paśyati tadgatāṃś ca sukhādīn vivekena gṛhṇāti // AbhTs_8.45
children.translated_text: <s>Aśuddhavidyā</s> (Impure Knowledge), born from <s>Kalā</s>, is the bestower of limited knowership (<s>kiṃcijjñatva</s>). And that <s>Vidyā</s> perceives the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) and discriminatingly grasps pleasure and the other [experiences] that belong to it. [AbhTs 8.45]

children.text: buddher guṇasaṃkīrṇākārāyā vivekena grahītum asāmarthyāt // AbhTs_8.46
children.translated_text: Because the intellect, whose form is mixed with the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), is incapable of discriminating apprehension. [AbhTs 8.46]

children.text: tasmāt buddhipratibimbito bhāvo vidyayā vivicyate // AbhTs_8.47
children.translated_text: Therefore, the state of things reflected in the intellect is discriminated by <s>Vidyā</s>. [AbhTs 8.47]

children.text: kiṃcitkartṛtvaṃ kiṃcidbhāgasiddhaye kvacid eva kartṛtvam ity atra arthe paryavasyati kvacid eva ca ity atra bhāge rāgatattvasya vyāpāraḥ // AbhTs_8.48
children.translated_text: Limited creatorship (<s>kiṃcitkartṛtva</s>), [meaning] creatorship only in some respect for the accomplishment of only some portion—this resolves into the meaning: 'only in some respect.' And regarding 'only in some portion,' the operation of <s>Rāga-tattva</s> (the principle of attachment) applies. [AbhTs 8.48]

children.text: na ca avairāgyakṛtaṃ tat avairāgyasyāpi araktidarśanāt // AbhTs_8.49
children.translated_text: And that [rāga] is not caused by mere non-dispassion (<s>avairāgya</s>), since attachment is seen even in [cases of] non-dispassion. [AbhTs 8.49]

children.text: vairāgye dharmādāv api raktir dṛśyate // AbhTs_8.50
children.translated_text: For even in [cases of] dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), attachment is seen toward <s>dharma</s> and the like. [AbhTs 8.50]

children.text: tṛptasya ca annādau avairāgyābhāve 'pi antaḥstharāgānapāyāt // AbhTs_8.51
children.translated_text: And for one who is satiated regarding food and such, even in the absence of non-dispassion, because of the non-departure of the <s>rāga</s> (attachment) that remains within. [AbhTs 8.51]

children.text: tena vinā punar avairāgyānutpattiprasaṅgāt // AbhTs_8.52
children.translated_text: And without that [rāga], there would be the unwanted consequence of the non-arising of non-dispassion. [AbhTs 8.52]

children.text: kālaś ca kāryaṃ kalayaṃs tadavacchinnaṃ kartṛtvam api kalayati tulye kvacittve asminn eva kartṛtvam ity atrārthe niyater vyāpāraḥ // AbhTs_8.53
children.translated_text: And <s>Kāla</s> (time), measuring the effect, also measures the creatorship delimited by that [effect]. When there is equal capacity in various domains, the operation of <s>Niyati</s> (regulation) pertains to the meaning: 'creatorship in just this [domain].' [AbhTs 8.53]

children.text: kāryakāraṇabhāve 'pi asyā eva vyāpāraḥ tena kalāta eva etac catuṣkaṃ jātam idam eva kiṃcid adhunā jānan abhiṣvaktaḥ karomi ity evaṃrūpā saṃvid dehapuryaṣṭakādigatā paśur ity ucyate // AbhTs_8.54
children.translated_text: Even in the cause-and-effect relationship, the operation of this [Niyati] alone applies. Therefore, from <s>Kalā</s> alone this group of four has arisen. This very [soul], now knowing something, attached, 'I do'—awareness of this form, residing in the body, <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body), and the like, is called a <s>paśu</s> (bound soul). [AbhTs 8.54]

children.text: tad idaṃ māyādiṣaṭkaṃ kañcukaṣaṭkam ucyate // AbhTs_8.55
children.translated_text: This group of six beginning with <s>Māyā</s> is called the six coverings (<s>kañcukaṣaṭka</s>). [AbhTs 8.55]

children.text: saṃvido māyayā apahastitatvena kalādīnām uparipātināṃ kañcukavat avasthānāt // AbhTs_8.56
children.translated_text: Because, with awareness having been concealed by <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Kalā</s> and the rest, falling upon it from above, remain like armors (<s>kañcuka</s>). [AbhTs 8.56]

children.text: evaṃ kiṃcitkartṛtvaṃ yat māyākāryaṃ tatra kiṃcit tv aviśiṣṭaṃ yat kartṛtvaṃ viśeṣyaṃ tatra vyāpriyamāṇā kalā vidyādiprasavahetuḥ iti nirūpitam // AbhTs_8.57
children.translated_text: Thus, the limited creatorship (<s>kiṃcitkartṛtva</s>) which is the product of <s>Māyā</s>—therein, the creatorship which is the undifferentiated qualifying element is 'limited' (<s>kiṃcit</s>), the qualifiable element. <s>Kalā</s>, operating upon that, is the cause of the production of <s>Vidyā</s> and the rest—this has been established. [AbhTs 8.57]

children.text: idānīṃ viśeṣaṇabhāgo yaḥ kiṃcid ity ukto jñeyaḥ kāryaś ca taṃ yāvat sā kalā svātmanaḥ pṛthak kurute tāvat eṣa eva sukhaduḥkhamohātmakabhogyaviśeṣānusyūtasya sāmānyamātrasya tadguṇasāmyāparanāmnaḥ prakṛtitattvasya sargaḥ iti bhoktṛbhogyayugalasya samam eva kalātattvāyattā sṛṣṭiḥ // AbhTs_8.58
children.translated_text: Now, the qualifying portion which was called 'limited' (<s>kiṃcit</s>)—the knowable object, the effect—to the extent that <s>Kalā</s> separates that from itself, to that very extent this is the creation of <s>Prakṛti-tattva</s> (the principle of primordial nature), otherwise known as the equilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), which is merely the general form interwoven with the specific objects of enjoyment whose nature is pleasure, pain, and delusion. Thus, the creation of the pair—enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>) and enjoyed (<s>bhogya</s>)—is equally dependent on the <s>Kalā-tattva</s>. [AbhTs 8.58]

children.text: atra caiṣāṃ vāstavena pathā kramavandhyaiva sṛṣṭir ity uktaṃ kramāvabhāso 'pi cāstīty api uktam eva // AbhTs_8.59
children.translated_text: And here, the creation of these by the real path is indeed devoid of sequence—this has been said. And that the appearance of sequence also exists—this too has been stated. [AbhTs 8.59]

children.text: kramaś ca vidyārāgādīnāṃ vicitro 'pi dṛṣṭaḥ kaścid rajyan vetti ko 'pi vidan rajyate ityādi // AbhTs_8.60
children.translated_text: And the sequence of <s>Vidyā</s>, <s>Rāga</s>, and the rest, though varied, is observed: someone, being attached, knows; another, knowing, becomes attached—and so forth. [AbhTs 8.60]

children.text: tena bhinnakramanirūpaṇam api rauravādiṣu śāstreṣu aviruddhaṃ mantavyaṃ tad eva tu bhogyasāmānyaṃ prakṣobhagataṃ guṇatattvam // AbhTs_8.61
children.translated_text: Therefore, the determination of different sequences in the <s>Raurava</s> and other scriptures should be regarded as non-contradictory. That very general [form of] enjoyment, when agitated, is the <s>Guṇa-tattva</s> (principle of qualities). [AbhTs 8.61]

children.text: yatra sukhaṃ bhogyarūpaprakāśaḥ sattvam duḥkhaṃ prakāśāprakāśāndolanātmakam ata eva kriyārūpaṃ rajaḥ mohaḥ prakāśābhāvarūpas tamaḥ // AbhTs_8.62
children.translated_text: Therein, pleasure—the illumination in the form of the object of enjoyment—is <s>sattva</s>; pain—having the nature of oscillation between illumination and non-illumination, hence being of the form of activity—is <s>rajas</s>; delusion—having the form of absence of illumination—is <s>tamas</s>. [AbhTs 8.62]

children.text: tritayam api etat bhogyarūpam // AbhTs_8.63
children.translated_text: All three of these are of the nature of objects of enjoyment. [AbhTs 8.63]

children.text: evaṃ kṣubdhāt pradhānāt kartavyāntarodayaḥ na akṣubdhād iti // AbhTs_8.64
children.translated_text: Thus, from agitated <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial nature), the arising of different effects [occurs]; not from the un-agitated. [AbhTs 8.64]

children.text: kṣobhaḥ avaśyam eva antarāle abhyupagantavya iti siddhaṃ sāṃkhyāparidṛṣṭaṃ pṛthagbhūtaṃ guṇatattvam // AbhTs_8.65
children.translated_text: Agitation must necessarily be acknowledged as an intermediate [stage]. Thus is established the <s>Guṇa-tattva</s> as a distinct [principle] not seen by <s>Sāṃkhya</s>. [AbhTs 8.65]

children.text: sa ca kṣobhaḥ prakṛtes tattveśādhiṣṭhānād eva anyathā niyataṃ puruṣaṃ prati iti na sidhyet // AbhTs_8.66
children.translated_text: And that agitation [comes] only from the presiding of the lord of the <s>tattvas</s> (<s>tattveśa</s>) over <s>Prakṛti</s>; otherwise the rule 'toward [a specific] <s>Puruṣa</s>' would not be established. [AbhTs 8.66]

children.text: tato guṇatattvāt buddhitattvaṃ yatra puṃprakāśo viṣayaś ca pratibimbam arpayataḥ // AbhTs_8.67
children.translated_text: From that <s>Guṇa-tattva</s> [arises] the <s>Buddhi-tattva</s> (principle of intellect), wherein the light of the individual soul (<s>puṃprakāśa</s>) and the object (<s>viṣaya</s>) offer their reflections. [AbhTs 8.67]

children.text: buddhitattvāt ahaṃkāro yena buddhipratibimbite vedyasamparke kaluṣe puṃprakāśe anātmani ātmābhimānaḥ śuktau rajatābhimānavat // AbhTs_8.68
children.translated_text: From <s>Buddhi-tattva</s> [arises] <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (the principle of ego), by which, in the light of the individual soul that is reflected in the intellect—[a light] made turbid by contact with the knowable, and which is not the Self—there arises the false identification with the Self (<s>ātmābhimāna</s>), like the false identification of silver in mother-of-pearl. [AbhTs 8.68]

children.text: ata eva kāra ity anena kṛtakatvam asya uktaṃ sāṃkhyasya tu tat na yujyate sa hi na ātmano 'haṃvimarśamayatām icchati vayaṃ tu kartṛtvam api tasya icchāmaḥ // AbhTs_8.69
children.translated_text: For this very reason, by the suffix <s>kāra</s> ('making'), its constructed nature is indicated. But for the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> system, that is not appropriate, for they do not wish the Self to have the nature of 'I'-awareness (<s>ahaṃvimarśa</s>). We, however, accept creatorship as belonging to it also. [AbhTs 8.69]

children.text: tac ca śuddhaṃ vimarśa eva apratiyogi svātmacamatkārarūpo 'ham iti // AbhTs_8.70
children.translated_text: And that [creatorship], when pure, is reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) itself—the unopposed wonder at one's own Self in the form of 'I am.' [AbhTs 8.70]

children.text: eṣo 'sya ahaṃkārasya karaṇaskandhaḥ // AbhTs_8.71
children.translated_text: This is the instrument-class (<s>karaṇaskandha</s>) of this <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>. [AbhTs 8.71]

children.text: prakṛtiskandhas tu tasyaiva trividhaḥ sattvādibhedāt // AbhTs_8.72
children.translated_text: The nature-class (<s>prakṛtiskandha</s>) of that same [Ahaṃkāra] is threefold, according to the divisions of <s>sattva</s> and the rest. [AbhTs 8.72]

children.text: tatra sāttviko yasmāt manaś ca buddhīndriyapañcakaṃ ca tatra manasi janye sarvatanmātrajananasāmarthyayuktaḥ sa janakaḥ // AbhTs_8.73
children.translated_text: There, from the <s>sāttvika</s> (luminous) [aspect arises] the mind (<s>manas</s>) and the five cognitive sense-faculties (<s>buddhīndriya</s>). In [the production of] the mind, that progenitor is endowed with the capacity to generate all <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements). [AbhTs 8.73]

children.text: śrotre tu śabdajananasāmarthyaviśiṣṭa iti yāvat ghrāṇe gandhajananayogyatāyukta iti bhautikam api na yuktam ahaṃ śṛṇomi ityādyanugamāc ca sphuṭam āhaṃkārikatvam karaṇatvena ca avaśyaṃ kartraṃśasparśitvam anyathā karaṇāntarayojanāyām anavasthādyāpātāt // AbhTs_8.74
children.translated_text: But in [the production of] the ear, [the progenitor] is distinguished by the capacity to generate sound alone—and so on, up to the nose, [which is] endowed with the fitness to generate smell. Even though [sense organs are] material (<s>bhautika</s>), their nature as products of <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> is evident from the experience 'I hear' and so forth. And as instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>), they must necessarily be in contact with the agent-aspect (<s>kartraṃśa</s>); otherwise there would be an infinite regress in the connection of further instruments. [AbhTs 8.74]

children.text: kartraṃśaś ca ahaṃkāra eva tena mukhye karaṇe dve puṃsaḥ jñāne vidyā kriyāyāṃ kalā andhasya paṅgoś ca ahaṃtārūpajñānakriyānapagamāt udriktatanmātrabhāgaviśiṣṭāt tu sāttvikād eva ahaṃkārāt karmendriyapañcakam ahaṃ gacchāmi iti ahaṃkāraviśiṣṭaḥ kāryakaraṇakṣamaḥ pādendriyaṃ tasya mukhyādhiṣṭhānaṃ bāhyam anyatrāpi tad asty eva iti rugṇasyāpi na gativicchedaḥ // AbhTs_8.75
children.translated_text: And the agent-aspect is <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> itself. Therefore, the primary instruments of the individual soul (<s>puṃs</s>) are two: in knowledge, <s>Vidyā</s>; in action, <s>Kalā</s>—because 'I'-awareness-based knowledge and action do not depart from the blind and the lame [respectively]. From the <s>sāttvika</s> <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> distinguished by an excess of <s>tanmātra</s> (subtle element) portions, [arise] the five organs of action (<s>karmendriya</s>). 'I walk'—the foot-organ, distinguished by <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, is capable of effecting the action; its primary external base is [the foot], but it exists elsewhere too—therefore even for one who is injured, there is no cessation of locomotion. [AbhTs 8.75]

children.text: na ca kartavyasāṃkaryamuktād eva hetoḥ kriyā karaṇakāryā mukhyaṃ ca gamanādīnāṃ kriyātvaṃ na rūpādyupalambhasya tasya kāṇādatantre guṇatvāt tasmāt avaśyābhyupeyaḥ karmendriyavargaḥ // AbhTs_8.76
children.translated_text: Nor, for the very reason stated—that there is a confusion of what is to be done—is action to be produced by the sense organs. And the primary 'action-hood' belongs to locomotion and the like, not to the apprehension of color, etc., since in the <s>Kāṇāda</s> system [Vaiśeṣika] that is a quality. Therefore, the class of organs of action (<s>karmendriya</s>) must necessarily be accepted. [AbhTs 8.76]

children.text: sa ca pañcakaḥ anusaṃdhes tāvattvāt // AbhTs_8.77
children.translated_text: And that [class of action organs] is fivefold, because the forms of purposive activity (<s>anusaṃdhi</s>) are just that many. [AbhTs 8.77]

children.text: tathā hi bahis tāvat tyāgāya vā anusaṃdhiḥ ādānāya vā dvayāya vā ubhayarahitatvena svarūpaviśrāntaye vā tatra krameṇa pāyuḥ pāṇiḥ pāda upastha iti // AbhTs_8.78
children.translated_text: For externally, purposive activity is either for the sake of rejection, or for acquisition, or for both, or for repose in one's own nature as free from both. There, in order, [the organs are:] the organ of excretion (<s>pāyu</s>), the hands (<s>pāṇi</s>), the feet (<s>pāda</s>), and the generative organ (<s>upastha</s>). [AbhTs 8.78]

children.text: antaḥ prāṇāśrayakarmānusaṃdhes tu vāgindriyam tena indriyādhiṣṭhāne haste yat gamanaṃ tad api pādendriyasyaiva karma iti mantavyam tena karmānantyam api na indriyānantyam āvahet iyati rājasasya upaśleṣakatvam ity āhuḥ // AbhTs_8.79
children.translated_text: For the internal purposive activity of actions based on <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), however, [there is] the organ of speech (<s>vāgindriya</s>). Therefore, when locomotion occurs in the hand, which is the seat of another organ, that too should be regarded as the action of the organ of the feet. Thus, the infinity of actions does not entail an infinity of organs. 'To this extent is the connecting capacity of the <s>rajas</s> [component]'—so they say. [AbhTs 8.79]

children.text: anye tu rājasān mana ity āhuḥ // AbhTs_8.80
children.translated_text: Others say that the <s>rājasic</s> [product of <s>ahaṃkāra</s>] is the mind (<s>manas</s>). [AbhTs 8.80]

children.text: anye tu sāttvikāt mano rājasāc ca indriyāṇi iti // AbhTs_8.81
children.translated_text: Still others [say]: from the <s>sāttvika</s> [component comes] mind, and from the <s>rājasic</s>, the sense organs. [AbhTs 8.81]

children.text: bhoktraṃśāc chādakāt tu tamaḥpradhānāhaṃkārāt tanmātrāṇi vedyaikarūpāṇi pañca // AbhTs_8.82
children.translated_text: But from the <s>ahaṃkāra</s> that is predominantly <s>tamas</s>, which covers the subject-aspect, [arise] the five <s>tanmātra</s>s (subtle elements), whose nature is purely that of the knowable. [AbhTs 8.82]

children.text: śabdaviśeṣāṇāṃ hi kṣobhātmanāṃ yad ekam akṣobhātmakaṃ prāgbhāvi sāmānyam aviśeṣātmakaṃ tat śabdatanmātram // AbhTs_8.83
children.translated_text: For, of the particular sounds that have the nature of agitation, that one general [element] which precedes them, having the nature of non-agitation, devoid of particularization—that is the <s>śabdatanmātra</s> (subtle element of sound). [AbhTs 8.83]

children.text: evaṃ gandhānte 'pi vācyam // AbhTs_8.84
children.translated_text: Likewise it should be said up to the subtle element of smell (<s>gandha</s>). [AbhTs 8.84]

children.text: tatra śabdatanmātrāt kṣubhitāt avakāśadānavyāpāraṃ nabhaḥ śabdasya vācyādhyāsāvakāśasahatvāt // AbhTs_8.85
children.translated_text: Of these, from the <s>śabdatanmātra</s> when agitated, [arises] space (<s>nabhas</s>), whose function is providing room, because sound has the capacity for the superimposition of the expressible and of space. [AbhTs 8.85]

children.text: śabdatanmātraṃ kṣubhitaṃ vāyuḥ śabdas tu asya nabhasā virahābhāvāt // AbhTs_8.86
children.translated_text: The <s>śabdatanmātra</s> when agitated [further becomes] wind (<s>vāyu</s>); but sound belongs to it due to the impossibility of separation from space. [AbhTs 8.86]

children.text: rūpaṃ kṣubhitaṃ tejaḥ pūrvaguṇau tu pūrvavat // AbhTs_8.87
children.translated_text: Form (<s>rūpa</s>) when agitated [becomes] fire (<s>tejas</s>); the previous two qualities [belong to it] as before. [AbhTs 8.87]

children.text: rasaḥ kṣubhita āpaḥ pūrve trayaḥ pūrvavat // AbhTs_8.88
children.translated_text: Taste (<s>rasa</s>) when agitated [becomes] water (<s>āpas</s>); the preceding three [qualities belong to it] as before. [AbhTs 8.88]

children.text: gandhaḥ kṣubhito dharā pūrve catvāraḥ pūrvavat // AbhTs_8.89
children.translated_text: Smell (<s>gandha</s>) when agitated [becomes] earth (<s>dharā</s>); the preceding four [qualities belong to it] as before. [AbhTs 8.89]

children.text: anye śabdasparśābhyāṃ vāyuḥ ityādikrameṇa pañcabhyo dharaṇī iti manyante // AbhTs_8.90
children.translated_text: Others hold that wind [arises] from sound and touch, and so on in sequence, earth from all five. [AbhTs 8.90]

children.text: guṇasamudāyamātraṃ ca pṛthivī nānyo guṇī kaścit // AbhTs_8.91
children.translated_text: And earth is merely an aggregate of qualities; there is no other substance possessing qualities. [AbhTs 8.91]

children.text: asmiṃś ca tattvakalāpe ūrdhvordhvaguṇaṃ vyāpakaṃ nikṛṣṭaguṇaṃ tu vyāpyam // AbhTs_8.92
children.translated_text: And in this group of <s>tattva</s>s (principles), what has a higher quality is the pervader; what has a lower quality is the pervaded. [AbhTs 8.92]

children.text: sa eva guṇasya utkarṣo yat tena vinā guṇāntaraṃ na upapadyate tena pṛthivītattvaṃ śivatattvāt prabhṛti jalatattvena vyāptam evaṃ jalaṃ tejasā ityādi yāvac chaktitattvam // AbhTs_8.93
children.translated_text: The superiority of a quality consists in this: that without it, another quality is not possible. Therefore, the earth-<s>tattva</s> is pervaded by the water-<s>tattva</s> beginning from the <s>Śiva</s>-<s>tattva</s>; likewise water is [pervaded] by fire, and so on up to the <s>Śakti</s>-<s>tattva</s>. [AbhTs 8.93]

children.text: sa ca saptadhā ṣaḍardhaśāstra eva paraṃ parameśena uktaḥ // AbhTs_9.1
children.translated_text: And these [perceivers] are sevenfold, as declared by the Supreme Lord himself in the six-and-a-half scriptures (<s>ṣaḍardhaśāstra</s>). [AbhTs 9.1]

children.text: tatra śivāḥ mantramaheśāḥ mantreśāḥ mantrāḥ vijñānākalāḥ pralayākalāḥ sakalā iti sapta śaktimantaḥ // AbhTs_9.2
children.translated_text: Among them: <s>Śiva</s>s, <s>Mantramaheśvara</s>s, <s>Mantreśvara</s>s, <s>Mantra</s>s, <s>Vijñānākala</s>s, <s>Pralayākala</s>s, and <s>Sakala</s>s—these are the seven who possess power (<s>śaktimat</s>). [AbhTs 9.2]

children.text: eṣāṃ saptaiva śaktayaḥ tadbhedāt pṛthivyādipradhānatattvāntaṃ caturdaśabhir bhedaiḥ pratyekaṃ svaṃ rūpaṃ pañcadaśam // AbhTs_9.3
children.translated_text: Their powers are seven, corresponding to [the seven perceivers]. From the earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) to the <s>Pradhāna-tattva</s>, there are fourteen divisions, [and] each [perceiver's] own form constitutes the fifteenth. [AbhTs 9.3]

children.text: tatra svaṃ rūpaṃ prameyatāyogyaṃ svātmaniṣṭham aparābhaṭṭārikānugrahāt pramātṛṣu udriktaśaktiṣu yat viśrāntibhājanaṃ tat tasyaiva śāktaṃ rūpaṃ śrīmatparāparānugrahāt tac ca saptavidhaṃ śaktīnāṃ tāvattvāt // AbhTs_9.4
children.translated_text: Therein, one's own form, being suitable as an object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>), resting in one's own Self—[that form] which, by the grace of the Blessed <s>Aparā</s> Goddess, reposes in perceivers whose power is heightened, that is its <s>Śākta</s> (power-related) form, by the grace of the Blessed <s>Parāparā</s>. And that is sevenfold, because the powers are just that many. [AbhTs 9.4]

children.text: śaktimadrūpapradhāne tu pramātṛvarge yat viśrāntaṃ tac chaktimac chivarūpaṃ śrīmatparābhaṭṭārikānugrahāt tad api saptavidham // AbhTs_9.5
children.translated_text: But in the class of perceivers where the power-possessor form predominates, what reposes [there] has the <s>Śiva</s>-form of the power-possessor, by the grace of the Blessed <s>Parā</s> Goddess. That too is sevenfold. [AbhTs 9.5]

children.text: pramātṝṇāṃ śivāt prabhṛti sakalāntānāṃ tāvatām uktatvāt // AbhTs_9.6
children.translated_text: Since the perceivers from <s>Śiva</s> down to <s>Sakala</s> are just that many, as has been stated. [AbhTs 9.6]

children.text: tatra śaktibhedād eva pramātṝṇāṃ bhedaḥ sa ca sphuṭīkaraṇārthaṃ sakalādikrameṇa bhaṇyate tatra sakalasya vidyākale śaktiḥ tadviśeṣarūpatvāt buddhikarmākṣaśaktīnāṃ pralayākalasya tu te eva nirviṣayatvāt asphuṭe // AbhTs_9.7
children.translated_text: Among them, the differentiation of perceivers is due to the differentiation of powers. And that, for the purpose of clarification, is described in the order beginning with <s>Sakala</s>. The power of the <s>Sakala</s> is [that which pertains to] the <s>Vidyā-kalā</s> (power of knowledge), since it has the form of the particularization thereof; [along with] the powers of intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), action (<s>karma</s>), and the senses (<s>akṣa</s>). For the <s>Pralayākala</s>, these same [powers exist], but in an indistinct form because they are without objects. [AbhTs 9.7]

children.text: vijñānākalasya te eva vigalatkalpe tatsaṃskārasacivā prabudhyamānā śuddhavidyā mantrasya // AbhTs_9.8
children.translated_text: For the <s>Vijñānākala</s>, these same [powers], with <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual thought) fading, accompanied by the impressions thereof, [become] the awakening <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (Pure Knowledge). For the <s>Mantra</s>: [AbhTs 9.8]

children.text: tatsaṃskārahīnā saiva prabuddhā mantreśasya // AbhTs_9.9
children.translated_text: the same [Śuddhavidyā], free from those impressions, fully awakened, [is the power] of the <s>Mantreśvara</s>. [AbhTs 9.9]

children.text: saiva icchāśaktirūpatāṃ svātantryasvabhāvāṃ jighṛkṣantī mantramaheśvarasya // AbhTs_9.10
children.translated_text: That same [power], seeking to grasp the form of <s>Icchāśakti</s> (power of will) whose nature is autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>), [is the power] of the <s>Mantramaheśvara</s>. [AbhTs 9.10]

children.text: icchātmikā sphuṭasvātantryātmikā śivasya iti śaktibhedāḥ sapta mukhyāḥ // AbhTs_9.11
children.translated_text: Having the nature of will, with manifest autonomy, [is the power] of <s>Śiva</s>. Thus, the primary differentiation of powers is sevenfold. [AbhTs 9.11]

children.text: taduparāgakṛtaś ca śaktimatsu pramātṛṣu bhedaḥ karaṇabhedasya kartṛbhedaparyavasānāt śakter eva ca avyatiriktāyāḥ karaṇīkartuṃ śakyatvāt na anyasya anavasthādyāpatteḥ // AbhTs_9.12
children.translated_text: And the differentiation among the power-possessing perceivers is caused by the coloring of these [powers], since the differentiation of instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>) culminates in the differentiation of agents (<s>kartṛ</s>); and since only the power—which is non-different [from the possessor]—can be made into an instrument, not anything else, for that would lead to infinite regress and other faults. [AbhTs 9.12]

children.text: vastutaḥ punar eka eva citsvātantryānandaviśrāntaḥ pramātā tatra pṛthivī svarūpamātraviśrāntā yadā vedyate tadā svarūpam asyāḥ kevalaṃ bhāti caitracakṣurdṛṣṭaṃ caitraviditaṃ jānāmīti tatra sakalaśaktikṛtaṃ sakalaśaktimadrūpakṛtaṃ svarūpāntaraṃ bhāty eva evaṃ śivāntam api vācyaṃ śivaśaktiniṣṭhaṃ śivasvabhāvaviśrāntaṃ ca viśvaṃ jānāmi iti pratyayasya vilakṣaṇasya bhāvāt // AbhTs_9.13
children.translated_text: In reality, however, the perceiver is one alone—consciousness, resting in the bliss of its own autonomy. When earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) is known as resting merely in its own form, then its own form alone shines: 'seen by <s>Caitra</s>'s eye, known by <s>Caitra</s>, I know.' Therein, the other form produced by the <s>Sakala</s> power and by the <s>Sakala</s> power-possessor form shines as well. Likewise, this should be stated up to <s>Śiva</s>. For the cognition 'I know' the universe resting in the <s>Śiva</s>-<s>Śakti</s> nature, resting in the <s>Śiva</s>-nature—is of a distinctive kind. [AbhTs 9.13]

children.text: nanu bhāvasya cet vedyatā svaṃ vapuḥ tat sarvān prati vedyatvaṃ vedyatvam api vedyam ity anavasthā tayā ca jagato 'ndhasuptatvaṃ suprakāśam eva tayā ca vedyatvāvedyatve viruddhadharmayoga iti doṣaḥ atra ucyate // AbhTs_9.14
children.translated_text: Objection: If knowability is the own form of an entity, then everything would be knowable to all; and 'the knowability [of knowability]' would itself be knowable—leading to infinite regress. And by that, the world would be [as if in] a state of blind sleep, which is clearly not the case. And by that, there would be knowability and non-knowability [simultaneously]—a conjunction of contradictory properties—which is a fault. To this it is replied: [AbhTs 9.14]

children.text: na tat svaṃ vapuḥ svarūpasya pṛthaguktatvāt kiṃ tarhi tat pramātṛśaktau pramātari ca yat viśrāntibhājanaṃ yat rūpaṃ tat khalu tat tat svaprakāśam eva tat prakāśate na tu kiṃcid api prati iti sarvajñatvam anavasthāviruddhadharmayogaś ca iti dūrāpāstam // AbhTs_9.15
children.translated_text: That [knowability] is not its own form, since its own form has been separately stated. Rather, whatever form [of the object] reposes in the power of the perceiver (<s>pramātṛśakti</s>) and in the perceiver—that indeed is self-luminous. It shines, but not in relation to anything. Thus, omniscience [is established], and the [objections of] infinite regress and conjunction of contradictory properties are thoroughly removed. [AbhTs 9.15]

children.text: anantapramātṛsaṃvedyam api ekam eva tat tasya rūpaṃ tāvati teṣām ekābhāsarūpatvāt iti na pramātrantarasaṃvedanānumānavighnaḥ kaścit tac ca tasya rūpaṃ satyam arthakriyākāritvāt tathaiva paradṛśyamānāṃ kāntāṃ dṛṣṭvā tasyai samīrṣyati śivasvabhāvaṃ viśrāntikumbhaṃ paśyan samāviśati samastānantapramātṛviśrāntaṃ vastu paśyan pūrṇībhavati nartakīprekṣaṇavat tasyaiva nīlasya tadrūpaṃ pramātari yat viśrāntaṃ tathaiva svaprakāśasya vimarśasyodayāt iti pañcadaśātmakatvaṃ pṛthivyāḥ prabhṛti pradhānatattvaparyantam // AbhTs_9.16
children.translated_text: Although known by infinite perceivers, that [entity] is one alone; its form in that many [perceivers is such] because they have the nature of a single appearance. Thus, there is no obstacle from the inference of being known by another perceiver. And that form of it is real, because it is causally efficacious. Just as, seeing a beautiful woman seen by another, one becomes jealous toward her; seeing a thing that is the vessel of repose in the <s>Śiva</s>-nature, one becomes absorbed; seeing a thing in which all infinite perceivers repose, one becomes complete—like watching a dancer. That very form of 'blue,' which reposes in the perceiver, and likewise, from the arising of self-luminous reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>)—thus, the fifteen-fold nature [is established] for each [tattva] from earth up to the <s>Pradhāna-tattva</s>. [AbhTs 9.16]

children.text: tāvaty udriktarāgādikañcukasya sakalasya pramātṛtvāt sakalasyāpi evaṃ pāñcadaśyaṃ tasyāpi tāvad vedyatvāt // AbhTs_9.17
children.translated_text: Since the <s>Sakala</s>, whose covering sheaths (<s>kañcuka</s>) of attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and the rest are heightened, has subjectivity corresponding to [all] that, the <s>Sakala</s> too has this fifteen-fold nature, since he too is an object of knowledge to that extent. [AbhTs 9.17]

children.text: vitatya caitat nirṇītaṃ tantrāloke // AbhTs_9.18
children.translated_text: And this has been determined extensively in the <s>Tantrāloka</s>. [AbhTs 9.18]

children.text: puṃsaḥ prabhṛti kalātattvāntaṃ trayodaśadhā // AbhTs_9.19
children.translated_text: From <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>Puṃs</s>) up to the <s>Kalā-tattva</s>, [the analysis is] thirteen-fold. [AbhTs 9.19]

children.text: sakalasya tatra pramātṛtāyogena tacchaktiśaktimadātmano bhedadvayasya pratyastamayāt tathā ca sakalasya svarūpatvam eva kevalaṃ pralayākalasya svarūpatve pañcānāṃ pramātṛtve ekādaśa bhedāḥ // AbhTs_9.20
children.translated_text: When the <s>Sakala</s> [perceiver] is subsumed therein as a perceiver, the two divisions of the <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śaktimat</s> forms disappear. And thus, the own form alone of the <s>Sakala</s> [remains]; when the own form of the <s>Pralayākala</s> [is considered], with five [remaining] as perceivers, there are eleven divisions. [AbhTs 9.20]

children.text: vijñānākalasya svarūpatve caturṇāṃ pramātṛtve nava bhedāḥ // AbhTs_9.21
children.translated_text: When the own form of the <s>Vijñānākala</s> [is considered], with four [remaining] as perceivers, there are nine divisions. [AbhTs 9.21]

children.text: mantrasya svarūpatve trayāṇāṃ pramātṛtve sapta // AbhTs_9.22
children.translated_text: For the <s>Mantra</s>, with three [remaining] as perceivers in its own form, [there are] seven. [AbhTs 9.22]

children.text: mantreśasya svarūpatve dvayoḥ pramātṛtve pañca // AbhTs_9.23
children.translated_text: For the <s>Mantreśvara</s>, with two [remaining] as perceivers in its own form, five. [AbhTs 9.23]

children.text: mantramaheśasya svarūpatve bhagavata ekasyaiva pramātṛtve śaktiśaktimadbhedāt trayaḥ // AbhTs_9.24
children.translated_text: For the <s>Mantramaheśvara</s>, with only the Lord himself as perceiver in its own form, three—due to the division of <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śaktimat</s>. [AbhTs 9.24]

children.text: śivasya tu prakāśaikacitsvātantryanirbharasya na ko 'pi bhedaḥ paripūrṇatvāt // AbhTs_9.25
children.translated_text: But for <s>Śiva</s>, whose nature is brimming with the autonomy of pure luminous consciousness alone, there is no division whatsoever, due to [his] complete fullness. [AbhTs 9.25]

children.text: evam ayaṃ tattvabheda eva parameśvarānuttaranayaikākhye nirūpitaḥ bhuvanabhedavaicitryaṃ karoti narakasvargarudrabhuvanānāṃ pārthivatve samāne 'pi dūratarasya svabhāvabhedasya uktatvāt // AbhTs_9.26
children.translated_text: Thus, this very differentiation of <s>tattva</s>s (principles), as set forth in the teaching known by the single name of the Unsurpassed (<s>Anuttara</s>) system of the Supreme Lord, produces the variety of world-divisions—since, although the hells, heavens, and <s>Rudra</s>-worlds share the [same] earthly nature, a great difference of intrinsic nature has been stated. [AbhTs 9.26]

children.text: atra ca parasparaṃ bhedakalanayā avāntarabhedajñānakutūhalī tantrālokam eva avadhārayet // AbhTs_9.27
children.translated_text: And here, one who is curious about the knowledge of subdivisions through the mutual differentiation should ascertain [this] from the <s>Tantrāloka</s> itself. [AbhTs 9.27]

children.text: evam ekaikaghaṭādyanusāreṇāpi pṛthivyādīnāṃ tattvānāṃ bhedo nirūpitaḥ // AbhTs_9.28
children.translated_text: Thus, the differentiation of the <s>tattva</s>s from earth onwards has been determined also by following each individual [object such as] a pot, etc. [AbhTs 9.28]

children.text: adhunā samastaṃ pṛthivītattvaṃ pramātṛprameyarūpam uddiśya nirūpyate yo dharātattvābhedena prakāśaḥ sa śivaḥ // AbhTs_9.29
children.translated_text: Now, the entire earth-<s>tattva</s>, comprising both the perceiver and the perceived, is set forth: that luminous awareness which is non-different from the earth-<s>tattva</s>—that is <s>Śiva</s>. [AbhTs 9.29]

children.text: yathā śrutiḥ pṛthivy evedaṃ brahma iti // AbhTs_9.30
children.translated_text: As the <s>Śruti</s> [says]: 'This earth itself is <s>Brahman</s>.' [AbhTs 9.30]

children.text: dharātattvasiddhipradān prerayati sa dharāmantramaheśvaraḥ preryo dharāmantreśaḥ tasyaivābhimānikavigrahatātmako vācako mantraḥ sāṃkhyādipāśavavidyottīrṇaśivavidyākrameṇa abhyastapārthivayogo 'prāptadhruvapadaḥ dharāvijñānākalaḥ // AbhTs_9.31
children.translated_text: He who impels [beings] to grant the attainments of the earth-<s>tattva</s> is the earth-<s>Mantramaheśvara</s>. The one impelled is the earth-<s>Mantreśvara</s>. The <s>Mantra</s> that represents his body and expresses it is of the nature of identification. The earth-<s>Vijñānākala</s> is one who has practiced the yoga of earth through the sequence of <s>Śiva</s>'s knowledge, transcending the <s>pāśava</s> (fettered) knowledge of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and other [systems], but has not attained the firm stage. [AbhTs 9.31]
