children.text: pāśavavidyākrameṇa abhyastapārthivayogaḥ kalpānte maraṇe vā dharāpralayakevalaḥ // AbhTs_9.32
children.translated_text: One who has practiced the yoga of earth through the sequence of <s>pāśava</s> (fettered) knowledge, at the end of a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age) or at death, is the earth-<s>Pralayākala</s> (dissolution-individual). [AbhTs 9.32]

children.text: sauṣupte hi tattvāveśavaśād eva citrasya svapnasya udayaḥ syāt gṛhītadharābhimānas tu dharāsakalaḥ // AbhTs_9.33
children.translated_text: For in deep sleep (<s>suṣupta</s>), due to absorption in the <s>tattva</s>s, the arising of varied dreams occurs. But one who has grasped the identity with earth is the earth-<s>Sakala</s>. [AbhTs 9.33]

children.text: atrāpi śaktyudrekanyagbhāvābhyāṃ caturdaśatvam iti pramātṛtāpannasya dharātattvasya bhedāḥ svarūpaṃ tu śuddhaṃ prameyam iti evam aparatrāpi // AbhTs_9.34
children.translated_text: Here too, through the predominance or subsidence of powers, there is a fourteen-fold [classification]; thus, the divisions of the earth-<s>tattva</s> when it has attained the status of perceiver; its own form, however, is the pure knowable. Likewise in the other [tattvas] too. [AbhTs 9.34]

children.text: atha ekasmin pramātari prāṇapratiṣṭhitatayā bhedanirūpaṇam iha nīlaṃ gṛhṇataḥ prāṇaḥ tuṭiṣoḍaśakātmā vedyāveśaparyantam udeti tatra ādyā tuṭir avibhāgaikarūpā dvitīyā grāhakollāsarūpā antyā tu grāhyābhinnā tanmayī upāntyā tu sphuṭībhūtagrāhakarūpā madhye tu yat tuṭidvādaśaka tanmadhyāt ādyaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ nirvikalpasvabhāvaṃ vikalpāc chādakaṃ ṣaṭtvaṃ ca asya svarūpeṇa ekā tuṭiḥ ācchādanīye ca vikalpe pañcarūpatvam unmimiṣā unmiṣattā sā ca iyaṃ sphuṭakriyārūpatvāt tuṭidvayātmikā spandanasya ekakṣaṇarūpatvābhāvāt unmiṣitatā svakāryakartṛtvaṃ ca ity evam ācchādanīyavikalpapāñcavidhyāt svarūpāc ca ṣaṭ kṣaṇā nirvikalpakāḥ tato 'pi nirvikalpasya dhvaṃsamānatā dhvaṃso vikalpasya unmimiṣā unmiṣattā tuṭidvayātmikā unmiṣitatā ca iti ṣaṭ tuṭayaḥ // AbhTs_9.35
children.translated_text: Now, the determination of differentiation through the vital breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) established in a single perceiver: when one apprehends 'blue,' the <s>prāṇa</s>, consisting of sixteen <s>tuṭi</s>s (moments), arises up to the point of absorption in the object. Therein, the first <s>tuṭi</s> is of an undivided, unitary form; the second has the form of the flash of the perceiver; the last is non-different from the perceived, of its very nature; the penultimate has the form of the perceiver made distinct; and the twelve <s>tuṭi</s>s in the middle—of these, the first six from the center are non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpa</s>) in nature, concealing <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual thought). And their six-fold nature is: one <s>tuṭi</s> as one's own form; and the five-fold nature in the <s>vikalpa</s> to be concealed: the incipient-emerging (<s>unmimiṣā</s>), the emerging (<s>unmiṣattā</s>)—and this, being of the nature of manifest action, consists of two <s>tuṭi</s>s, since vibration cannot have the form of a single moment—the emerged (<s>unmiṣitatā</s>), and its capacity to produce its own effect. Thus, from the five-fold nature of the <s>vikalpa</s> to be concealed and from one's own form, there are six non-conceptual moments. Then, from those six non-conceptual [moments]: the coming-to-an-end-ness of the non-conceptual, its ending, the incipient-emerging of the <s>vikalpa</s>, the emerging—consisting of two <s>tuṭi</s>s—and the emerged: thus six <s>tuṭi</s>s. [AbhTs 9.35]

children.text: svakāryakartṛtā tu grāhakarūpatā iti uktaṃ na sā bhūyo gaṇyate ity evaṃ vivekadhanā gurūpaveśānuśīlinaḥ sarvatra pāñcadaśyaṃ pravibhāgena viviñcate // AbhTs_9.36
children.translated_text: But the 'capacity to produce one's own effect' is the perceiver-form—as stated, it is not counted again. Thus, one who is rich in discrimination, trained through the instruction of the guru, distinguishes the fifteen-fold nature everywhere in detail. [AbhTs 9.36]

children.text: vikalpanyūnatve tu tuṭinyūnatā sukhādisaṃvittāv iva yāvat avikalpataiva // AbhTs_9.37
children.translated_text: But when <s>vikalpa</s> diminishes, the <s>tuṭi</s>s diminish too, as in the awareness of pleasure and the like, until there is nothing but the non-conceptual. [AbhTs 9.37]

children.text: lokās tu vikalpaviśrāntyā tām ahaṃtāmayīm ahaṃtācchāditedaṃbhāvavikalpaprasarāṃ nirvikalpāṃ vimarśabhuvam aprakāśitām iva manyante duḥkhāvasthāṃ sukhaviśrāntā iva vikalpanirhrāsena tu sā prakāśata eva iti iyam asau sambandhe grāhyagrāhakayoḥ sāvadhānatā iti abhinavaguptaguravaḥ // AbhTs_9.38
children.translated_text: But ordinary people, through repose in <s>vikalpa</s>, regard that I-nature—which is the ground of reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>), pervaded by the spread of <s>vikalpa</s> whose 'this'-ness is covered by I-ness, which is non-conceptual—as if it were not manifest, [seeing it as] a state of suffering, as if resting in pleasure. But through the diminution of <s>vikalpa</s>, it does indeed shine forth. This is what is called 'attentiveness' in the connection between the perceived and the perceiver—thus [say] the gurus of <s>Abhinavagupta</s>. [AbhTs 9.38]

children.text: evaṃ ca pāñcadaśye sthite yāvat sphuṭedaṃtātmano bhedasya nyūnatā tāvat dvayaṃ dvayaṃ hrasati yāvat dvituṭikaḥ śivāveśaḥ tatra ādyā tuṭiḥ sarvataḥ pūrṇā dvitīyā sarvajñānakaraṇāviṣṭābhyasyamānā sarvajñatvasarvakartṛtvāya kalpate na tu ādyā // AbhTs_9.39
children.translated_text: And thus, with the fifteen-fold analysis established, as the distinctness of the 'this'-nature (objectivity) diminishes, pairs [of tuṭis] are reduced, until [there is] the two-<s>tuṭi</s> absorption into <s>Śiva</s>. Therein, the first <s>tuṭi</s> is complete in every respect; the second, being permeated by the instruments of all knowledge and being practiced, serves for omniscience and omnipotence—but not the first. [AbhTs 9.39]

children.text: yad āha śrīkallaṭaḥ tuṭipāta iti atra pātaśabdaṃ saiva bhagavatī śrīmatkālī mātṛsadbhāvo bhairavaḥ pratibhā ity alaṃ rahasyārahasyanena // AbhTs_9.40
children.translated_text: As the illustrious <s>Kallaṭa</s> has said: '<s>tuṭipāta</s>' (the fall of the moment)—here, the word 'fall' (<s>pāta</s>) refers to that very Blessed <s>Śrīmat Kālī</s>, <s>Mātṛsadbhāva</s>, <s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Pratibhā</s>. Enough of this [disclosure of] secret upon secret. [AbhTs 9.40]

children.text: evaṃ mantramaheśatuṭeḥ prabhṛti tattadabhyāsāt tattatsiddhiḥ // AbhTs_9.41
children.translated_text: Thus, from the <s>tuṭi</s> of the <s>Mantramaheśvara</s> onwards, through the respective practice, the respective attainments [are achieved]. [AbhTs 9.41]

children.text: athātraiva jāgradādyavasthā nirūpyante tatra vedyasya tadviṣayāyāś ca saṃvido yat vaicitryam anyonyāpekṣaṃ sat sā avasthā na vedyasya kevalasya na cāpi kevalāyāḥ saṃvido na cāpi pṛthak pṛthak dve // AbhTs_9.42
children.translated_text: Now, here the states of waking (<s>jāgrat</s>) and the rest are set forth. The variety of the knowable and of the consciousness that has it as its object, when mutually dependent, constitutes a 'state' (<s>avasthā</s>)—not of the knowable alone, nor of consciousness alone, nor of the two separately. [AbhTs 9.42]

children.text: tatra yadādhiṣṭheyatayā bahīrūpatayā bhānaṃ tadā jāgradavasthā meye mātari māne ca // AbhTs_9.43
children.translated_text: When the appearance is as what is to be governed, in an external form, then it is the waking state (<s>jāgradavasthā</s>)—in the object of knowledge (<s>meya</s>), in the knower (<s>mātṛ</s>), and in the means of knowledge (<s>māna</s>). [AbhTs 9.43]

children.text: yadā tu tatraiva adhiṣṭhānarūpatayā bhānaṃ saṃkalpaḥ tadā svapnāvasthā // AbhTs_9.44
children.translated_text: But when in that very [domain], the appearance is in the form of the governing [substrate], as mental construction (<s>saṃkalpa</s>), then it is the dream state (<s>svapnāvasthā</s>). [AbhTs 9.44]

children.text: yadā tu tatraiva adhiṣṭhātṛrūpatayā bījātmatayaiva bhānaṃ tadā suṣuptāvasthā // AbhTs_9.45
children.translated_text: But when in that very [domain], the appearance is in the form of the governing agent, as mere seed-nature (<s>bījātmatā</s>), then it is the deep sleep state (<s>suṣuptāvasthā</s>). [AbhTs 9.45]

children.text: imā eva tisraḥ prameyapramāṇapramātravasthāḥ pratyekaṃ jāgradādibhedāt caturvidhā uktāḥ // AbhTs_9.46
children.translated_text: These very three—the states of the knowable (<s>prameya</s>), the means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), and the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>)—are each said to be fourfold through the division of waking, etc. [within each]. [AbhTs 9.46]

children.text: yadā tu tasminn eva pramātṛviśrāntigate pramātuḥ pūrṇataunmukhyāt taddvāreṇa pūrṇatonmukhatayā bhānaṃ tadā turyāvasthā sā ca rūpaṃ dṛśāham ity evaṃvidham aṃśatrayam uttīrya paśyāmīti anupāyikā pramātṛtā svātantryasārā naikaṭyamadhyatvadūratvaiḥ pramātṛpramāṇaprameyatābhiṣekaṃ dadatī tadavasthātrayānugrāhakatvāt tribhedā // AbhTs_9.47
children.translated_text: But when, in that very cognizer-repose, due to the cognizer's inclination toward fullness, through that means, there is awareness through inclination toward fullness—that is the <s>turya</s> (fourth) state. And it, transcending the threefold aspect of 'form,' 'seeing,' and 'I,' is the cognizer-nature of 'I perceive'—without any means, having autonomy as its essence, bestowing the consecration of cognizer-hood, means-of-cognition-hood, and object-of-cognition-hood through proximity, middleness, and distance—and it is threefold because it supports those three states. [AbhTs 9.47]

children.text: etad eva avasthācatuṣṭayaṃ piṇḍasthapadastharūpastharūpātītaśabdair yogino vyavaharanti prasaṃkhyānadhanās tu sarvatobhadraṃ vyāptiḥ mahāvyāptiḥ pracaya iti śabdaiḥ // AbhTs_9.48
children.translated_text: This very fourfold state is designated by yogins with the terms <s>piṇḍastha</s> (abiding in the body), <s>padastha</s> (abiding in the word), <s>rūpastha</s> (abiding in form), and <s>rūpātīta</s> (transcending form). But those who are adept in <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (discernment meditation) [designate them] with the terms <s>sarvatobhadra</s> (all-auspicious), <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion), <s>mahāvyāpti</s> (great pervasion), and <s>pracaya</s> (accumulation). [AbhTs 9.48]

children.text: anvarthaṃ cātra darśitaṃ tantrāloke ślokavārttike ca // AbhTs_9.49
children.translated_text: The literal meaning of these terms has been shown in the <s>Tantrāloka</s> and the <s>Ślokavārttika</s>. [AbhTs 9.49]

children.text: yac ca sarvāntarbhūtaṃ pūrṇarūpaṃ tat turyātītaṃ sarvātītaṃ mahāpracayaṃ ca nirūpayanti // AbhTs_9.50
children.translated_text: And that which is the complete form contained within all—that they determine as <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth), <s>sarvātīta</s> (beyond all), and <s>mahāpracaya</s> (great accumulation). [AbhTs 9.50]

children.text: kiṃ ca yasya yad yadā rūpaṃ sphuṭaṃ sthiram anubandhi tat jāgrat tasyaiva tadviparyayaḥ svapnaḥ yaḥ layākalasya bhogaḥ sarvāvedanaṃ suṣuptaṃ yo vijñānākalasya bhogaḥ bhogyābhinnīkaraṇaṃ turyaṃ mantrādīnāṃ sa bhogaḥ bhāvānāṃ śivābhedas turyātītaṃ sarvātītam // AbhTs_9.51
children.translated_text: Moreover, for whomever whatever form is at any given time clear, stable, and continuous—that is the waking state of that very being. The reverse of that is dream. The experience of one who is dissolved into the <s>kalā</s> (limited power of action)—the total absence of awareness—is deep sleep. The experience of one who is a <s>vijñānākala</s> (a being with pure knowledge only)—the non-differentiation from the object of experience—is <s>turya</s> (the fourth state). The experience of <s>mantra</s>s and others—the non-difference of all entities from <s>Śiva</s>—is <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth), <s>sarvātīta</s> (beyond all). [AbhTs 9.51]

children.text: tatra svarūpasakalau 1 pralayākalaḥ 2 vijñānākalaḥ 3 mantratadīśatanmaheśavargaḥ 4 śivaḥ 5 iti pañcadaśabhede pañca avasthāḥ // AbhTs_9.52
children.translated_text: Therein, the five states exist in the fifteen-fold division of: one's own nature and <s>sakala</s> [1], <s>pralayākala</s> [2], <s>vijñānākala</s> [3], the group of <s>mantra</s>, <s>mantreśvara</s>, and <s>maheśvara</s> [4], and <s>Śiva</s> [5]. [AbhTs 9.52]

children.text: svarūpaṃ pralayākala ityādikrameṇa trayodaśabhede svarūpaṃ vijñānākalaśaktiḥ vijñānākala ity ekādaśabhede svarūpaṃ mantrāḥ tadīśāḥ maheśāḥ śivaḥ iti navabhede svarūpaṃ mantreśāḥ maheśaḥ śaktiḥ śiva iti saptabhede svarūpaṃ maheśaśaktiḥ maheśaḥ śaktiḥ śiva iti pañcabhede svarūpaṃ kriyāśaktiḥ jñānaśaktiḥ icchāśaktiḥ śiva iti tribhede abhinne 'pi śivatattve kriyājñānecchānandacidrūpakḷptyā prasaṃkhyānayogadhanāḥ pañcapadatvam āhuḥ // AbhTs_9.53
children.translated_text: In the thirteen-fold division, beginning with 'one's own nature is <s>pralayākala</s>' in sequence; in the eleven-fold, 'one's own nature is <s>vijñānākala</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>vijñānākala</s>'; in the nine-fold, 'one's own nature is <s>mantra</s>s, <s>mantreśvara</s>s, <s>maheśvara</s>s, and <s>Śiva</s>'; in the seven-fold, 'one's own nature is <s>mantreśvara</s>s, <s>maheśvara</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, <s>maheśvara</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>'; in the five-fold, 'one's own nature is <s>kriyā-śakti</s> (power of action), <s>jñāna-śakti</s> (power of knowledge), <s>icchā-śakti</s> (power of will), and <s>Śiva</s>'; in the three-fold, even in the undivided <s>Śiva-tattva</s> itself, those adept in <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (discernment meditation) declare five stages through the artificial division into <s>kriyā</s> (action), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>icchā</s> (will), <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), and <s>cit</s> (consciousness). [AbhTs 9.53]

children.text: uktas tāvat tattvādhvā // AbhTs_10.1
children.translated_text: Thus far, the path of <s>tattvas</s> (principles) has been described. [AbhTs 10.1]

children.text: kalādyadhvā tu nirūpyate tatra yathā bhuvaneṣu anugāmi kiṃcid rūpaṃ tattvam ity uktam tathā tattveṣu vargaśo yat anugāmi rūpaṃ tat kalā ekarūpakalanāsahiṣṇutvāt // AbhTs_10.2
children.translated_text: Now the path of <s>kalā</s>s (powers) and the rest is to be examined. Just as a certain form that pervades the worlds was called a <s>tattva</s> (principle), so too, that which pervades the <s>tattva</s>s group by group is a <s>kalā</s> (power), because it cannot tolerate being reduced to a single form. [AbhTs 10.2]

children.text: tad yathā pṛthivyāṃ nivṛttiḥ nivartate yatas tattvasarga iti // AbhTs_10.3
children.translated_text: Thus: in earth, [the <s>kalā</s> is] <s>Nivṛtti</s> (cessation), because the creation of <s>tattva</s>s ceases from that point. [AbhTs 10.3]

children.text: jalādipradhānānte varge pratiṣṭhā kāraṇatayāpyāyanapūraṇakāritvāt // AbhTs_10.4
children.translated_text: In the group from water up to and ending with <s>Pradhāna</s>, [the <s>kalā</s> is] <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s> (foundation), because as a cause it nourishes and fills. [AbhTs 10.4]

children.text: pumādimāyānte vidyā vedyatirobhāve saṃvidādhikyāt // AbhTs_10.5
children.translated_text: In the group from <s>Puruṣa</s> up to and ending with <s>Māyā</s>, [the <s>kalā</s> is] <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge), because when the object of knowledge disappears, there is predominance of awareness. [AbhTs 10.5]

children.text: śuddhavidyādiśaktyante śāntā kañcukataraṃgopaśamāt // AbhTs_10.6
children.translated_text: In the group from <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> up to and ending with <s>Śakti</s>, [the <s>kalā</s> is] <s>Śāntā</s> (peaceful), because the waves of the limiting sheaths (<s>kañcuka</s>s) subside. [AbhTs 10.6]

children.text: etad eva aṇḍacatuṣṭayaṃ pārthivaprākṛtamāyīyaśāktābhidham // AbhTs_10.7
children.translated_text: This very [set constitutes] the four cosmic eggs (<s>aṇḍa</s>s), designated as <s>Pārthiva</s> (earthly), <s>Prākṛta</s> (pertaining to nature), <s>Māyīya</s> (pertaining to māyā), and <s>Śākta</s> (pertaining to power). [AbhTs 10.7]

children.text: pṛthivyādiśaktīnām atra avasthānena śaktitattve yāvat parasparśo vidyate sparśasya ca sapratighatvam iti tāvati yuktam aṇḍatvam // AbhTs_10.8
children.translated_text: Here, with the abiding of [the powers] from earth up to <s>Śakti</s>, insofar as there is mutual contact within the <s>Śakti-tattva</s>, and contact implies having resistance—to that extent, the designation of 'cosmic egg' is appropriate. [AbhTs 10.8]

children.text: śivatattve śāntātītā tasyopadeśabhāvanārcādau kalyamānatvāt // AbhTs_10.9
children.translated_text: In the <s>Śiva-tattva</s>, [the <s>kalā</s> is] <s>Śāntātītā</s> (beyond the peaceful), because it is activated in instruction, contemplation, worship, and so forth. [AbhTs 10.9]

children.text: svatantraṃ tu paraṃ tattvaṃ tatrāpi yat aprameyaṃ tat kalātītam // AbhTs_10.10
children.translated_text: But the supreme autonomous <s>tattva</s>—that which even there is beyond measurement—is beyond the <s>kalā</s>s. [AbhTs 10.10]

children.text: evaṃ pañcaiva kalāḥ ṣaṭtriṃśattattvāni // AbhTs_10.11
children.translated_text: Thus there are five <s>kalā</s>s and thirty-six <s>tattva</s>s. [AbhTs 10.11]

children.text: tathāhi prameyatvaṃ dvidhā sthūlasūkṣmatvena iti daśa // AbhTs_10.12
children.translated_text: Indeed, the status of being an object of knowledge is twofold, as gross and subtle—thus ten. [AbhTs 10.12]

children.text: karaṇatvaṃ dvidhā śuddhaṃ kartṛtāsparśi ca iti daśa // AbhTs_10.13
children.translated_text: The status of being an instrument is twofold: pure, and that which does not touch the agent—thus ten. [AbhTs 10.13]

children.text: karaṇatopasarjanakartṛbhāvasphuṭatvāt pañca śuddhakartṛbhāvāt pañca vigalitavibhāgatayā vikāsonmukhatve pañca sarvāvacchedaśūnyaṃ śivatattvaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśam // AbhTs_10.14
children.translated_text: Due to the clear emergence of agent-hood as subsidiary to instrumentality, five; due to pure agent-hood, five; in the state of inclination toward unfolding through the dissolution of divisions, five; the <s>Śiva-tattva</s>, devoid of all limitation, is the thirty-sixth. [AbhTs 10.14]

children.text: tad yadā upadiśyate bhāvyate vā yat tatpratiṣṭhāpadam tat saptatriṃśam tasminn api bhāvyamāne aṣṭātriṃśam na ca anavasthā tasya bhāvyamānasya anavacchinnasvātantryayogino vedyīkaraṇe saptatriṃśa eva paryavasānāt ṣaṭtriṃśaṃ tu sarvatattvottīrṇatayā saṃbhāvyāvacchedam iti pañcakalāvidhiḥ // AbhTs_10.15
children.translated_text: When that [<s>Śiva-tattva</s>] is taught or contemplated, the foundation of that is the thirty-seventh. When even that is contemplated upon, it becomes the thirty-eighth. There is no infinite regress, because when that which is being contemplated—which is endowed with unlimited autonomy—is made into an object of knowledge, it terminates in the thirty-seventh itself. The thirty-sixth, however, is posited through the possibility of limitation as transcending all <s>tattva</s>s. Thus is the method of the five <s>kalā</s>s. [AbhTs 10.15]

children.text: vijñānākalaparyantam ātmakalā īśāntaṃ vidyākalā śiṣṭaṃ śivakalā iti tritattvavidhiḥ // AbhTs_10.16
children.translated_text: Up to <s>vijñānākala</s> is <s>ātma-kalā</s> (the power of the self); up to <s>Īśvara</s> is <s>vidyā-kalā</s> (the power of knowledge); the remainder is <s>śiva-kalā</s> (the power of <s>Śiva</s>)—thus is the method of three <s>tattva</s>s. [AbhTs 10.16]

children.text: evaṃ navatattvādy api ūhayet iti // AbhTs_10.17
children.translated_text: Likewise, the methods of nine <s>tattva</s>s and so on should also be inferred. [AbhTs 10.17]

children.text: meyāṃśagāmī sthūlasūkṣmapararūpatvāt trividho bhuvanatattvakalātmādhvabhedaḥ mātṛviśrāntyā tathaiva trividhaḥ tatra pramāṇatāyāṃ padādhvā pramāṇasyaiva kṣobhataraṃgaśāmyattāyāṃ mantrādhvā tatpraśame pūrṇapramātṛtāyāṃ varṇādhvā sa eva ca asau tāvati viśrāntyā labdhasvarūpo bhavati iti ekasyaiva ṣaḍvidhatvaṃ yuktam // AbhTs_10.18
children.translated_text: The division of the paths—world (<s>bhuvana</s>), principle (<s>tattva</s>), and power (<s>kalā</s>)—which pertains to the object-aspect, is threefold due to having the nature of gross, subtle, and supreme. Through the repose in the subject, it is likewise threefold: in the state of being a means of cognition, it is the path of words (<s>pada-adhvan</s>); in the state of the stilling of the agitation-waves of the means of cognition itself, it is the path of <s>mantra</s>s (<s>mantra-adhvan</s>); in the subsiding of that, in the state of full subjectivity, it is the path of phonemes (<s>varṇa-adhvan</s>). And that very [path] obtains its essential nature through repose to that extent. Thus the sixfold nature of what is essentially one is appropriate. [AbhTs 10.18]

children.text: tatra yāvat idam uktam tat sākṣāt kasyacit apavargāptaye yathoktasaṃgrahanītyā bhavati kasyacit vakṣyamāṇadīkṣāyām upayogagamanāt iti dīkṣādikaṃ vaktavyam // AbhTs_11.1
children.translated_text: Now, all that has been stated up to this point directly leads to the attainment of liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) for some, according to the method of the teaching as described. For others, it serves as preparation for the initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) that will be described. Therefore, initiation and related matters must now be discussed. [AbhTs 11.1]

children.text: tatra kaḥ adhikārī iti nirūpaṇārthaṃ śaktipāto vicāryate // AbhTs_11.2
children.translated_text: In this regard, in order to determine who is qualified, the descent of power (<s>śaktipāta</s>) is to be examined. [AbhTs 11.2]

children.text: tatra kecit āhuḥ jñānābhāvāt ajñānamūlaḥ saṃsāraḥ tadapagame jñānodayāt śaktipāta iti teṣāṃ samyak jñānodaya eva vikṛta iti vācyam karmajanyatve karmaphalavat bhogatvaprasaṅge bhogini ca śaktipātābhyupagatau atiprasaṅgaḥ īśvarecchānimittatve tu jñānodayasya anyonyāśrayatā vaiyarthyaṃ ca īśvare rāgādiprasaṅgaḥ viruddhayoḥ karmaṇoḥ samabalayoḥ anyonyapratibandhe karmasāmyaṃ tataḥ śaktipāta iti cet na kramikatve virodhāyogāt virodhe 'pi anyasya aviruddhasya karmaṇo bhogadānaprasaṅgāt aviruddhakarmāpravṛttau tadaiva dehapātaprasaṅgāt jātyāyuṣpradaṃ karma na pratibadhyate bhogapradam eva tu pratibadhyate iti cet kutaḥ tatkarmasadbhāve yadi śaktiḥ patet tarhi sā bhogapradāt kiṃ bibhiyāt // AbhTs_11.3
children.translated_text: Some say: since <s>saṃsāra</s> is rooted in ignorance due to the absence of knowledge, and upon its removal, with the arising of knowledge, there is <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of power). To them it should be said: what exactly is this 'arising of right knowledge' that has become distorted? If it is produced by <s>karma</s>, then like the fruit of <s>karma</s>, it would have the consequence of being merely an experience; and if <s>śaktipāta</s> were admitted for one who is merely an experiencer, there would be over-extension. But if the arising of knowledge has the Lord's will as its cause, then there is mutual dependence and also futility, as well as the consequence of attributing attachment and such to the Lord. [Some say:] when two mutually opposed <s>karma</s>s of equal strength obstruct each other, there is <s>karma</s>-equilibrium, and from that, <s>śaktipāta</s>. Not so—because if they are successive, there is no opposition; even if there is opposition, there would be the consequence of some other non-opposing <s>karma</s> giving experience; and if non-opposing <s>karma</s> does not operate, there would be the consequence of the body falling at that very moment. [Objection:] <s>Karma</s> that determines birth-type and lifespan is not obstructed; only experience-producing <s>karma</s> is obstructed. [Reply:] On what grounds? If, despite the existence of that <s>karma</s>, power were to descend, what would it have to fear from experience-producing <s>karma</s>? [AbhTs 11.3]

children.text: atha malaparipāke śaktipātaḥ so 'pi kiṃsvarūpaḥ kiṃ ca tasya nimittam iti etena vairāgyaṃ dharmaviśeṣo vivekaḥ satsevā satprāptiḥ devapūjā ityādihetuḥ pratyukta iti bhedavādināṃ sarvam asamañjasam // AbhTs_11.4
children.translated_text: Now [the objection]: <s>śaktipāta</s> occurs upon the ripening of <s>mala</s> (innate impurity). But what is its nature, and what is its cause? By this [question], the [proposed] causes—dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), a special form of <s>dharma</s>, discrimination (<s>viveka</s>), association with the virtuous, attainment of truth, worship of a deity, and so on—are all refuted. Thus, everything proposed by the dualists is untenable. [AbhTs 11.4]

children.text: svatantraparameśādvayavāde tu upapadyate etat yathāhi parameśvaraḥ svarūpācchādanakrīḍayā paśuḥ pudgalo 'ṇuḥ sampannaḥ na ca tasya deśakālasvarūpabhedavirodhaḥ tadvat svarūpasthaganavinivṛttyā svarūpapratyāpattiṃ jhaṭiti vā krameṇa vā samāśrayan śaktipātapātram aṇuḥ ucyate svātantryamātrasāraś ca asau paramaśivaḥ śakteḥ pātayitā iti nirapekṣa eva śaktipāto yaḥ svarūpaprathāphalaḥ yas tu bhogotsukasya sa karmāpekṣaḥ lokottararūpabhogotsukasya tu sa eva śaktipātaḥ parameśvarecchāpreritamāyāgarbhādhikārīyarudraviṣṇubrahmādidvāreṇa mantrādirūpatvaṃ māyāpuṃvivekaṃ puṃskalāvivekaṃ puṃprakṛtivivekaṃ puṃbuddhivivekam anyac ca phalaṃ prasnuvānaḥ tadadharatattvabhogaṃ pratibadhnāti bhogamokṣobhayotsukasya bhoge karmāpekṣo mokṣe tu tannirapekṣaḥ iti sāpekṣanirapekṣaḥ // AbhTs_11.5
children.translated_text: But in the non-dual doctrine of the autonomous supreme Lord, this is coherent. Just as the supreme Lord, through the play of concealing his own nature, becomes a <s>paśu</s> (bound soul), an individual, an <s>aṇu</s> (atom of consciousness)—without any contradiction in terms of place, time, or essential nature—so too, through the cessation of the concealment of his own nature, the <s>aṇu</s> who resorts to the recovery of his essential nature, either suddenly or gradually, is called a recipient of <s>śaktipāta</s>. And that supreme <s>Śiva</s>, whose essence is nothing but autonomy, is the one who causes the descent of power. Therefore, that <s>śaktipāta</s> which has the manifestation of one's own nature as its fruit is entirely independent. But that which pertains to one eager for experience (<s>bhoga</s>) is dependent on <s>karma</s>. For one eager for supramundane experience, that very <s>śaktipāta</s>, impelled by the will of the supreme Lord and working through the intermediary of the <s>Rudra</s>s, <s>Viṣṇu</s>s, <s>Brahmā</s>s, etc., who are qualified administrators born from the womb of <s>Māyā</s>, and who have the nature of <s>mantra</s>s and the like—produces the discrimination of <s>Puruṣa</s> from <s>Māyā</s>, of <s>Puruṣa</s> from <s>kalā</s>, of <s>Puruṣa</s> from <s>prakṛti</s>, of <s>Puruṣa</s> from <s>buddhi</s>, and other fruits—and obstructs the experience of the <s>tattva</s>s below that. For one eager for both enjoyment and liberation: in enjoyment, it is dependent on <s>karma</s>; in liberation, it is independent of it. Thus it is both dependent and independent. [AbhTs 11.5]

children.text: na ca vācyaṃ kasmāt kasmiṃścid eva puṃsi śaktipāta iti sa eva parameśvaraḥ tathā bhāti iti satattve ko 'sau pumān nāma yaduddeśena viṣayakṛtā codanā iyam // AbhTs_11.6
children.translated_text: And one should not ask: 'Why does <s>śaktipāta</s> occur in a particular individual only?' That supreme Lord simply appears in that way. In the true reality, who is this 'individual' in whose regard this questioning objection is raised? [AbhTs 11.6]

children.text: sa cāyaṃ śaktipāto navadhā tīvramadhyamandasya utkarṣamādhyasthyanikarṣaiḥ punas traividhyāt tatra utkṛṣṭatīvrāt tadaiva dehapāte parameśatā madhyatīvrāt śāstrācāryānapekṣiṇaḥ svapratyayasya prātibhajñānodayaḥ yadudaye bāhyasaṃskāraṃ vinaiva bhogāpavargapradaḥ prātibho gurur ity ucyate tasya hi na samayyādikalpanā kācit atrāpi tāratamyasadbhāvaḥ icchāvaicitryāt iti saty api prātibhatve śāstrādyapekṣā saṃvādāya syād api iti nirbhittisabhittyādibahubhedatvam ācāryasya prātibhasyāgameṣu uktam sarvathā pratibhāṃśo balīyān tatsaṃnidhau anyeṣām anadhikārāt // AbhTs_11.7
children.translated_text: This <s>śaktipāta</s> is ninefold: of intense (<s>tīvra</s>), moderate (<s>madhya</s>), and mild (<s>manda</s>), each subdivided into three again through superior, middling, and inferior [grades]. Therein: from the most intense degree (<s>utkṛṣṭa-tīvra</s>), at the very moment of the body's fall, one attains the state of the supreme Lord. From the moderate-intense (<s>madhya-tīvra</s>), there arises spontaneous intuitive knowledge (<s>prātibha-jñāna</s>) in one who does not depend on scriptures or a teacher—upon whose arising, without any external consecration, it bestows both enjoyment and liberation. Such a one is called an 'intuitive guru.' For him there is no convention of initiatory rules and the like. Even here, there are gradations due to the diversity of will. Therefore, even though one has intuitive knowledge, dependence on scriptures and the like may exist for the sake of corroboration. Thus there are many sub-divisions such as 'with wall' and 'without wall,' etc. In the <s>Āgama</s>s, many divisions of the intuitive guru and teacher are stated. In all cases, the intuitive element is predominant; in its presence, others are not qualified. [AbhTs 11.7]

children.text: bhedadarśana iva anādiśivasaṃnidhau muktaśivānāṃ sṛṣṭilayādikṛtyeṣu mandatīvrāt śaktipātāt sadguruviṣayā yiyāsā bhavati asadguruviṣayāyāṃ tu tirobhāva eva asadgurutas tu sadgurugamanaṃ śaktipātād eva // AbhTs_11.8
children.translated_text: Just as, in the presence of the beginningless <s>Śiva</s>, the liberated <s>Śiva</s>s [perform] the activities of creation, dissolution, etc.—from the mild-intense (<s>manda-tīvra</s>) degree of <s>śaktipāta</s>, the desire to seek a true guru arises. When [the desire] is directed toward a false guru, there is only further concealment. But the movement from a false guru to a true guru occurs only through <s>śaktipāta</s> itself. [AbhTs 11.8]

children.text: sadgurus tu samastaitacchāstratattvajñānapūrṇaḥ sākṣāt bhagavadbhairavabhaṭṭāraka eva yogino 'pi svabhyastajñānatayaiva mocakatve tatra yogyatvasya saubhāgyalāvaṇyādimattvasyevānupayogāt // AbhTs_11.9
children.translated_text: A true guru is one who is filled with the knowledge of the <s>tattva</s>s (principles) of all these scriptures—he is none other than the Blessed Lord <s>Bhairava</s> himself. Even yogins qualify as liberators only insofar as they possess well-practiced knowledge; mere suitability for that role, like possessing beauty or charm, is of no use. [AbhTs 11.9]

children.text: asadgurus tu anyaḥ sarva eva // AbhTs_11.10
children.translated_text: A false guru is anyone else whatsoever. [AbhTs 11.10]

children.text: evaṃ yiyāsuḥ guroḥ jñānalakṣaṇāṃ dīkṣāṃ prāpnoti yayā sadya eva mukto bhavati jīvann api atra avalokanāt kathanāt śāstrasambodhanāt caryādarśanāt carudānāt ityādayo bhedāḥ // AbhTs_11.11
children.translated_text: Thus, one who desires [liberation] receives from the guru an initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) characterized by knowledge, by which one becomes immediately liberated, even while living. Therein, the varieties include: through a glance (<s>avalokana</s>), through speech (<s>kathana</s>), through scriptural instruction (<s>śāstrasambodhanā</s>), through demonstrating conduct (<s>caryādarśana</s>), through giving a <s>caru</s> (ritual offering), and so on. [AbhTs 11.11]

children.text: abhyāsavato vā tadānīṃ sadya eva prāṇaviyojikāṃ dīkṣāṃ labhate sā tu maraṇakṣaṇa eva kāryā iti vakṣyāma iti // AbhTs_11.12
children.translated_text: Or, for one who has practiced, at that very time one receives an initiation that separates the vital breath (<s>prāṇa-viyojikā dīkṣā</s>). But that must be performed only at the moment of death—this we shall explain. [AbhTs 11.12]

children.text: tīvrās tridhā utkṛṣṭamadhyāt śaktipātāt kṛtadīkṣāko 'pi svātmanaḥ śivatāyāṃ na tathā dṛḍhapratipattiḥ bhavati pratipattiparipākakrameṇa tu dehānte śiva eva madhyamadhyāt tu śivatotsuko 'pi bhogaprepsuḥ bhavati iti tathaiva dīkṣāyāṃ jñānabhājanam sa ca yogābhyāsalabdham anenaiva dehena bhogaṃ bhuktvā dehānte śiva eva // AbhTs_11.13
children.translated_text: The intense [<s>śaktipāta</s>] is threefold: from the superior-moderate degree, even after initiation, one does not have a very firm conviction in one's own <s>Śiva</s>-nature. But through the gradual maturation of conviction, at the end of the body [i.e., at death], one becomes <s>Śiva</s> himself. From the middling-moderate degree, though eager for <s>Śiva</s>-hood, one also desires experience; thus, in that very initiation, one becomes a receptacle of knowledge. And having experienced enjoyment with this very body through the practice of yoga, at the end of the body one becomes <s>Śiva</s> himself. [AbhTs 11.13]

children.text: nikṛṣṭamadhyāt tu dehāntareṇa bhogaṃ bhuktvā śivatvam eti iti // AbhTs_11.14
children.translated_text: From the inferior-moderate degree, having experienced enjoyment through another body, one attains <s>Śiva</s>-hood. [AbhTs 11.14]

children.text: madhyas tu tridhā bhogotsukatā yadā pradhānabhūtā tadā mandatvaṃ pārameśvaramantrayogopāyatayā yatas tatra autsukyam pārameśamantrayogādeś ca yato mokṣaparyantatvam ataḥ śaktipātarūpatā // AbhTs_11.15
children.translated_text: The moderate [<s>śaktipāta</s>] is threefold: when eagerness for experience is predominant, that is its mild form—due to the means of the supreme Lord's <s>mantra</s>, yoga, etc., because the eagerness is directed toward those, and because the supreme Lord's <s>mantra</s>, yoga, etc. have liberation as their ultimate end—therefore it has the nature of <s>śaktipāta</s>. [AbhTs 11.15]

children.text: tatrāpi tāratamyāt traividhyam ity eṣa mukhyaḥ śaktipātaḥ // AbhTs_11.16
children.translated_text: Even therein, due to gradation, there is a threefold division. This is the principal <s>śaktipāta</s>. [AbhTs 11.16]

children.text: vaiṣṇavādīnāṃ tu rājānugrahavat na mokṣāntatā iti na iha vivecanam // AbhTs_11.17
children.translated_text: But for <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>s and others, [their grace] is like a royal favor—it does not lead to final liberation. Therefore, it is not discussed here. [AbhTs 11.17]

children.text: śivaśaktyadhiṣṭhānaṃ tu sarvatra iti uktam sā paraṃ jyeṣṭhā na bhavati api tu ghorā ghoratarā vā sa eṣa śaktipāto vicitro 'pi tāratamyavaicitryāt bhidyate kaścid vaiṣṇavādisthaḥ samayyādikrameṇa srotaḥpañcake ca prāptaparipākaḥ sarvottīrṇabhagavatṣaḍardhaśāstraparamādhikāritām eti anyas tu ullaṅghanakrameṇa anantabhedena ko 'pi akramam iti ata eva adharādharaśāsanasthā guravo 'pi iha maṇḍalamātradarśane 'pi anadhikāriṇaḥ ūrdhvaśāsanasthas tu guruḥ adharādharaśāsanaṃ pratyuta prāṇayati pūrṇatvāt iti sarvādhikārī // AbhTs_11.18
children.translated_text: However, the governance of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> is present everywhere. As stated, that [grace of theirs] is not the supreme or <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> (the eldest power); rather it is <s>Ghorā</s> (terrible) or <s>Ghoratarā</s> (more terrible). This <s>śaktipāta</s>, though varied, is differentiated by the variety of gradation. Someone established in a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> or other [system], through the sequence of initiatory conventions and the five streams, having attained maturity, reaches the supreme authority of the all-transcending scripture of the Blessed <s>Ṣaḍardha</s> (the <s>Trika</s>). Another, through the method of leaping over stages, in infinite variety; yet another, without any sequence at all. Therefore, gurus established in lower and inferior scriptures are not qualified even to witness the <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred diagram) here. But a guru established in the supreme scripture, on the contrary, enlivens the lower and inferior scriptures, because of his fullness—thus he is qualified for all. [AbhTs 11.18]

children.text: sa ca daiśiko guruḥ ācāryo dīkṣakaḥ cumbakaḥ sa cāyaṃ pūrṇajñāna eva sarvottamaḥ tena vinā dīkṣādyasampatteḥ // AbhTs_11.19
children.translated_text: He is the regional teacher (<s>daiśika</s>), the guru, the preceptor (<s>ācārya</s>), the initiator (<s>dīkṣaka</s>), the 'magnetizer' (<s>cumbaka</s>). And this one, endowed with full knowledge alone, is the very best. Without him, initiation and the rest cannot be accomplished. [AbhTs 11.19]

children.text: yogī tu phalotsukasya yukto yadi upāyopadeśena avyavahitam eva phalaṃ dātuṃ śaktaḥ upāyopadeśena tu jñāne eva yukto mokṣe 'pi abhyupāyāt jñānapūrṇatākāṅkṣī ca bahūn api gurūn kuryāt // AbhTs_11.20
children.translated_text: A yogin, however, is suitable for one who is eager for results, if through instruction in method he is capable of giving the result directly. But through instruction in method, he is suitable only for knowledge; and for liberation too, through subsidiary means. And one who desires the fullness of knowledge should have even many gurus. [AbhTs 11.20]

children.text: uttamottamādijñānabhedāpekṣayā teṣu varteta sampūrṇajñānagurutyāge tu prāyaścittam eva // AbhTs_11.21
children.translated_text: One should remain with them in accordance with the distinctions of highest, middling, and other degrees of knowledge. But in abandoning a guru of full knowledge, only expiation is [the remedy]. [AbhTs 11.21]

children.text: nanu so 'pi abruvan viparītaṃ vā bruvan kiṃ na tyājyaḥ naiva iti brūmaḥ tasya hi pūrṇajñānatvāt eva rāgādyabhāva iti avacanādikaṃ śiṣyagatenaiva kenacit ayogyatvānāśvastatvādinā nimittena syāt iti tadupāsane yatanīyaṃ śiṣyeṇa na tattyāge // AbhTs_11.22
children.translated_text: Objection: 'What if he too speaks incorrectly, or says the opposite—is he not to be abandoned?' We say: no. For it is precisely because he possesses full knowledge that he is free from attachment and the like. His silence or similar behavior must be due to some cause residing in the disciple—such as unworthiness, lack of trust, and so on. Therefore, the disciple should strive to attend upon him, not to abandon him. [AbhTs 11.22]

children.text: evam anugrahanimittaṃ śaktipāto nirapekṣa eva karmādiniyatyapekṣaṇāt // AbhTs_11.23
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of grace), whose purpose is <s>anugraha</s> (divine favor), is entirely independent — since the regulation by <s>karma</s> and the like is [itself] dependent [upon it]. [AbhTs 11.23]

children.text: tirobhāva iti tirobhāvo hi karmādyapekṣagāḍhaduḥkhamohabhāgitvaphalaḥ yathāhi prakāśasvātantryāt prabuddho 'pi mūḍhavat ceṣṭate hṛdayena ca mūḍhaceṣṭāṃ nindati tathā mūḍho 'pi prabuddhaceṣṭāṃ mantrārādhanādikāṃ kuryāt nindec ca yathā ca asya mūḍhaceṣṭā kriyamāṇāpi prabuddhasya dhvaṃsam eti tathā asya prabuddhaceṣṭā sā tu nindyamānā niṣiddhācaraṇarūpatvāt svayaṃ ca tayaiva viśaṅkamānatvāt enaṃ duḥkhamohapaṅke nimajjayati na tu utpannaśaktipātasya tirobhāvo 'sti atrāpi ca karmādyapekṣā pūrvavat niṣedhyā tatrāpi ca icchāvaicitryāt etad dehamātropabhogyaduḥkhaphalatvaṃ vā dīkṣāsamayacaryāgurudevāgnyādau sevānindanobhayaprasaktānām iva prāk śivaśāsanasthānāṃ tattyāginām iva // AbhTs_11.24
children.translated_text: Regarding <s>tirobhāva</s> (concealment): <s>tirobhāva</s> indeed, dependent on <s>karma</s> and the like, has as its fruit the state of being subject to intense suffering and delusion. Just as one who is awakened through the sovereignty of [divine] light (<s>prakāśa</s>) still behaves like one deluded, yet inwardly condemns deluded behavior — so too one who is deluded may perform the conduct of the awakened, such as <s>mantra</s>-worship and the like, and condemn it. And just as the deluded conduct of the awakened one, even when performed, is destroyed — so too the awakened conduct of the deluded one, being condemned and being of the nature of prohibited behavior, and he himself being apprehensive on account of that very thing, causes him to sink into the mire of suffering and delusion. However, for one in whom <s>śaktipāta</s> has arisen, there is no <s>tirobhāva</s>. And here too the dependence on <s>karma</s> and the like is to be rejected as before. But therein too, due to the variety of [the Lord's] will (<s>icchā</s>), the fruit may be suffering experienced only in this one body, or — as for those formerly established in the order of <s>Śiva</s> who were devoted to or contemptuous of or both attracted and repelled by <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), <s>samaya</s> (observances), <s>caryā</s> (conduct), <s>guru</s>, <s>deva</s> (deity), fire, and the like — [such is the case] for those who have abandoned those [practices]. [AbhTs 11.24]

children.text: tatrāpi icchāvaicitryāt tirobhūto 'pi svayaṃ vā śaktipātena yujyate mṛto vā bandhugurvādikṛpāmukhena ity evaṃ kṛtyabhāgitvaṃ svātmani anusaṃdadhat parameśvara eva iti na khaṇḍitam ātmānaṃ paśyet // AbhTs_11.25
children.translated_text: Therein too, due to the variety of [the Lord's] will, one who is concealed (<s>tirobhūta</s>) may either himself be joined with <s>śaktipāta</s>, or after death [may receive it] through the compassionate agency of relatives, <s>guru</s>, and the like. Thus, one who contemplates within one's own Self the state of being the agent of all five divine acts (<s>kṛtya</s>) [perceives that] one is none other than <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) — one should not see oneself as divided. [AbhTs 11.25]

children.text: dīkṣādikaṃ vaktavyam iti uktam ato dīkṣāsvarūpanirūpaṇārthaṃ prāk kartavyaṃ snānam upadiśyate // AbhTs_12.1
children.translated_text: It was stated that <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) and related topics are to be discussed. Therefore, for the purpose of determining the true nature of <s>dīkṣā</s>, the bath (<s>snāna</s>) to be performed beforehand is [first] taught. [AbhTs 12.1]

children.text: snānaṃ ca śuddhatā ucyate śuddhatā ca parameśvarasvarūpasamāveśaḥ // AbhTs_12.2
children.translated_text: And 'bath' (<s>snāna</s>) is called 'purity' (<s>śuddhatā</s>); and purity is absorption into the essential nature of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord). [AbhTs 12.2]

children.text: kāluṣyāpagamo hi śuddhiḥ kāluṣyaṃ ca tadekarūpe 'pi atatsvabhāvarūpāntarasaṃvalanābhimānaḥ // AbhTs_12.3
children.translated_text: For purity is the removal of turbidity (<s>kāluṣya</s>); and turbidity is the false identification (<s>abhimāna</s>) of [one's nature] — though it is of one single form — with another form that is not its true nature. [AbhTs 12.3]

children.text: tad iha svatantrānandacinmātrasāre svātmani viśvatrāpi vā tadanyarūpasaṃvalanābhimānaḥ aśuddhiḥ sā ca mahābhairavasamāveśena vyapohyate so 'pi kasyacit jhaṭiti bhavet kasyāpi upāyāntaramukhaprekṣī // AbhTs_12.4
children.translated_text: Here, in one's own Self whose essential core is nothing but autonomous bliss-consciousness (<s>svatantra-ānanda-cinmātra</s>) — whether [considered] universally or [in any particular] — the false identification with another form: that is impurity. And it is removed by immersion in <s>Mahābhairava</s> (the Great Terrific One). This [immersion] may occur for some suddenly, but for others it proceeds through the doorway of other means. [AbhTs 12.4]

children.text: tatrāpi ca ekadvitryādibhedena samastavyastatayā kvacit kasyacit kadācit ca tathā āśvāsopalabdheḥ vicitro bhedaḥ // AbhTs_12.5
children.translated_text: And therein too, through the distinction of one, two, three, and so forth — in whole and in part — somewhere, for someone, and at some time — there is a varied difference, since the repose [of realization] is obtained [variously]. [AbhTs 12.5]

children.text: sa ca aṣṭadhā kṣitijalapavanahutāśanākāśasomasūryātmarūpāsu aṣṭāsu mūrtiṣu mantranyāsamahimnā parameśvararūpatayā bhāvitāsu tādātmyena ca dehe parameśvarasamāviṣṭe śarīrādivibhāgavṛtteḥ caitanyasyāpi parameśvarasamāveśaprāptiḥ kasyāpi tu snānavastrādituṣṭijanakatvāt parameśopāyatām etīti uktaṃ ca śrīmadānandādau dhṛtiḥ āpyāyo vīryaṃ maladāho vyāptiḥ sṛṣṭisāmarthyaṃ sthitisāmarthyam abhedaś ca ity etāni teṣu mukhyaphalāni teṣu teṣu upāhitasya mantrasya tattadrūpadhāritvāt // AbhTs_12.6
children.translated_text: And that [bath] is eightfold — in the eight <s>mūrtis</s> (forms) consisting of earth, water, wind, fire, space, moon, sun, and Self — which through the greatness of <s>mantra-nyāsa</s> (ritual placement of mantras) have been contemplated as forms of <s>Parameśvara</s>; and through identity with these, when the body has been pervaded by <s>Parameśvara</s>, even for consciousness — whose operation involves the division of body and the like — the attainment of <s>Parameśvara</s>-immersion [occurs]. But for some, since [even ordinary] bathing, garments, and the like produce satisfaction, this [too] attains the status of a means to <s>Parameśvara</s>. And it has been said in the blessed <s>Ānanda</s> [Tantra] and other [texts]: steadfastness, nourishment, vigor, burning of impurity, pervasion, the power of creation, the power of maintenance, and non-duality — these are the primary fruits in those [respective forms], because the <s>mantra</s> placed in each [form] takes on the nature of that very [form]. [AbhTs 12.6]

children.text: vīroddeśena tu viśeṣaḥ tad yathā raṇareṇuḥ vīrāmbhaḥ mahāmarut vīrabhasma śmaśānanabhaḥ tadupahitau candrārkau ātmā nirvikalpakaḥ // AbhTs_12.7
children.translated_text: But through the teaching of the heroic (<s>vīra</s>) [tradition], there is a special [variant]: namely, battle-dust, heroic waters, the great wind, heroic ash, the sky of the cremation ground, the moon and sun situated therein, and the Self — free from conceptualization. [AbhTs 12.7]

children.text: punar api bāhyābhyantaratayā dvitvam bahirupāsyamantratādātmyena tanmayīkṛte tatra tatra nimajjanam ity uktam // AbhTs_12.8
children.translated_text: Again, through the distinction of external and internal, there is a twofold [classification]. Through identity with the externally-worshiped <s>mantra</s>, having become one with it, immersion therein in each [form] — thus it has been stated. [AbhTs 12.8]

children.text: viśeṣas tu ānandadravyaṃ vīrādhāragataṃ nirīkṣaṇena śivamayīkṛtya tatraiva mantracakrapūjanam tataḥ tenaiva dehaprāṇobhayāśritadevatācakratarpaṇam iti mukhyaṃ snānam // AbhTs_12.9
children.translated_text: The special [practice] is: the bliss-substance (<s>ānanda-dravya</s>) situated in the <s>vīra</s>-receptacle, having been made into the nature of <s>Śiva</s> through gazing, therein [one performs] the worship of the <s>mantra-cakra</s> (circle of mantras); then with that very [substance], the satisfaction-offering (<s>tarpaṇa</s>) to the deity-circle abiding in the body, <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), and both — this is the primary bath. [AbhTs 12.9]

children.text: ābhyantaraṃ yathā tattaddharādirūpadhāraṇayā tatra tatra pārthivādau cakre tanmayībhāvaḥ // AbhTs_12.10
children.translated_text: The internal [bath] is as follows: through assuming the form of earth and the other [elements] in their respective [contemplations], one attains identity with the respective earth-circle and so forth in those [levels]. [AbhTs 12.10]

children.text: atha prasannahṛdayo yāgasthānaṃ yāyāt tac ca yatraiva hṛdayaṃ prasādayuktaṃ parameśvarasamāveśayogyaṃ bhavati tad eva na tu asya anyal lakṣaṇam uktāv api dhyeyatādātmyam eva kāraṇam tad api bhāvaprasādād eva iti nānyat sthānam // AbhTs_13.1
children.translated_text: Now, with a pleased heart, one should go to the place of worship (<s>yāga-sthāna</s>). And that [place] is wherever the heart becomes endowed with serenity and fit for immersion in <s>Parameśvara</s> — that alone [is the place]; no other characteristic [is required]. Even in [texts] that state [particular features of a place], identity with the object of meditation is the [real] cause — and that too [arises] from the serenity of inner disposition alone; therefore no other place [is needed]. [AbhTs 13.1]

children.text: pīṭhaparvatāgram ityādis tu śāstre sthānoddeśa etatpara eva boddhavyaḥ // AbhTs_13.2
children.translated_text: The mention of a '<s>pīṭha</s> (sacred seat), mountain-peak,' and so forth in the scriptures as the designation of a place should be understood as having this very [inner] meaning. [AbhTs 13.2]

children.text: teṣu teṣu pīṭhādisthāneṣu parameśaniyatyā parameśvarāviṣṭānāṃ śaktīnāṃ dehagrahaṇāt āryadeśā iva dhārmikāṇāṃ mlecchadeśā iva adhārmikāṇām parvatāgrādeś caikāntatvena vikṣepaparihārāt aikāgryapadatvam iti // AbhTs_13.3
children.translated_text: In those various <s>pīṭha</s>-places and the like, because the <s>Śaktis</s> (powers) pervaded by <s>Parameśvara</s> assume bodies there by <s>Parameśvara</s>'s own regulation — just as the <s>Ārya</s> lands [are the abode] of the righteous, and the <s>mleccha</s> lands of the unrighteous — and because mountain-peaks and the like, due to their solitary nature, afford freedom from distraction, they become places of one-pointedness. [AbhTs 13.3]

children.text: tatra yāgagṛhāgre bahir eva sāmānyanyāsaṃ kuryāt karayoḥ pūrvaṃ tato dehe // AbhTs_13.4
children.translated_text: There, in front of the worship-chamber, outside, one should perform the general <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement) — first on the hands, then on the body. [AbhTs 13.4]

children.text: hrīṃ na pha hrīṃ hrīṃ ā kṣa hrīṃ ity ābhyāṃ śaktiśaktimadvācakābhyāṃ mālinīśabdarāśimantrābhyām ekenaiva ādau śaktiḥ tataḥ śaktimān iti muktau pādāgrāc chiro'ntam bhuktau tu sarvo viparyayaḥ // AbhTs_13.5
children.translated_text: '<s>Hrīṃ na pha hrīṃ</s>' and '<s>Hrīṃ ā kṣa hrīṃ</s>' — with these two [mantras] denoting <s>Śakti</s> and the Possessor of <s>Śakti</s>, being the <s>mantras</s> of the <s>Mālinī</s> syllable-aggregate — with the first alone [placed] first as <s>Śakti</s>, then the Possessor of <s>Śakti</s>. For liberation (<s>mukti</s>), [the placement proceeds] from the tips of the feet to the top of the head; but for enjoyment (<s>bhukti</s>), everything is reversed. [AbhTs 13.5]

children.text: mālinī hi bhagavatī mukhyam śāktaṃ rūpaṃ bījayonisaṃghaṭṭena samastakāmadugham // AbhTs_13.6
children.translated_text: For the blessed <s>Mālinī</s> is the primary <s>Śākta</s> (pertaining to <s>Śakti</s>) form, which, through the union of seed and womb (<s>bīja-yoni</s>), yields all desires. [AbhTs 13.6]

children.text: anvarthaṃ caitan nāma rudraśaktimālābhir yuktā phaleṣu puṣpitā saṃsāraśiśirasaṃhāranādabhramarī siddhimokṣadhāriṇī dānādānaśaktiyuktā iti ralayor ekatvasmṛteḥ // AbhTs_13.7
children.translated_text: And this name is etymologically fitting: she is endowed with garlands (<s>mālā</s>) of <s>Rudra</s>-<s>śaktis</s>, she flowers in the fruits [of spiritual attainment], she is a female bee whose humming destroys the cold of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly bondage), she holds <s>siddhis</s> (powers) and liberation, and she possesses the power of giving and taking — since <s>ra</s> and <s>la</s> are traditionally considered identical. [AbhTs 13.7]

children.text: ata eva hi bhraṣṭavidhir api mantra etannyāsāt pūrṇo bhavati sāñjano 'pi gāruḍavaiṣṇavādir nirañjanatām etya mokṣaprado bhavati // AbhTs_13.8
children.translated_text: For this very reason, even a <s>mantra</s> that has deviated from [proper] procedure, through this <s>nyāsa</s> becomes complete; even one tainted [with impurity], belonging to the <s>Gāruḍa</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, or other [traditions], having attained the state of being free from stain, becomes a bestower of liberation. [AbhTs 13.8]

children.text: dehanyāsānantaram arghapātre ayam eva nyāsaḥ // AbhTs_13.9
children.translated_text: After the body-<s>nyāsa</s>, this same <s>nyāsa</s> [is performed] in the <s>arghapātra</s> (offering vessel). [AbhTs 13.9]

children.text: iha hi kriyākārakāṇāṃ parameśvarābhedapratipattidārḍhyasiddhaye pūjākriyā udāharaṇīkṛtā tatra ca sarvakārakāṇām itthaṃ parameśvarībhāvaḥ tatra yaṣṭrādhārasya sthānaśuddhyāpādānakaraṇayor arghapātraśuddhinyāsābhyām yaṣṭur dehanyāsāt yājyasya sthaṇḍilādinyāsāt // AbhTs_13.10
children.translated_text: Here, for the purpose of establishing firm certainty in the non-difference of all factors of ritual action (<s>kāraka</s>) from <s>Parameśvara</s>, the ritual of worship (<s>pūjā-kriyā</s>) is taken as the example. And therein, the <s>Parameśvara</s>-nature of all factors [is effected] as follows: of the worshiper's substrate, through the purification of the place (<s>sthāna-śuddhi</s>); of the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) and the recipient (<s>apādāna</s>), through the purification-<s>nyāsa</s> of the <s>arghapātra</s>; of the worshiper himself, through the body-<s>nyāsa</s>; and of the object of worship, through the <s>nyāsa</s> on the <s>sthaṇḍila</s> (altar platform) and the like. [AbhTs 13.10]

children.text: evaṃ kriyākrameṇāpi parameśvarīkṛtasamastakārakaḥ tayaiva dṛśā sarvakriyāḥ paśyan vināpi pramukhajñānayogābhyāṃ parameśvara eva bhavati // AbhTs_13.11
children.translated_text: Thus, even through the sequence of ritual action, one whose entire [set of] factors has been made into <s>Parameśvara</s>, seeing all activities with that very vision — even without the direct [paths of] knowledge-<s>yoga</s> — becomes <s>Parameśvara</s> himself. [AbhTs 13.11]

children.text: evam arghapātre nyasya puṣpadhūpādyaiḥ pūjayitvā tadvipruḍbhir yāgasāraṃ puṣpādi ca prokṣayet // AbhTs_13.12
children.translated_text: Having thus performed <s>nyāsa</s> in the <s>arghapātra</s> and having worshiped it with flowers, incense, and the like, one should sprinkle the essential implements of worship and the flowers and so forth with drops from it. [AbhTs 13.12]

children.text: tataḥ prabhāmaṇḍale bhūmau khe vā oṃ bāhyaparivārāya nama iti pūjayet // AbhTs_13.13
children.translated_text: Then, in the zone of radiance (<s>prabhāmaṇḍala</s>), whether on the ground or in space: 'Oṃ, homage to the outer retinue' — thus one should worship. [AbhTs 13.13]

children.text: tato dvārasthāne oṃ dvāradevatācakrāya nama iti pūjayet // AbhTs_13.14
children.translated_text: Then, at the doorway: 'Oṃ, homage to the door-deity-circle' — thus one should worship. [AbhTs 13.14]

children.text: agupte tu bahiḥsthāne sati praviśya maṇḍalasthaṇḍilāgra eva bāhyaparivāradvāradevatācakrapūjāṃ pūrvoktaṃ ca nyāsādi kuryāt na bahiḥ // AbhTs_13.15
children.translated_text: But if the outer place is not secluded, one should enter and perform the worship of the outer retinue and door-deity-circle, as well as the previously described <s>nyāsa</s> and the rest, at the very head of the <s>maṇḍala</s>-platform inside — not outside. [AbhTs 13.15]

children.text: tato 'pi phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ iti astrajaptapuṣpaṃ prakṣipya vighnān apasāritān dhyātvā antaḥ praviśya parameśvarakiraṇeddhayā dṛṣṭyā abhito yāgagṛhaṃ paśyet // AbhTs_13.16
children.translated_text: Then, having thrown a flower consecrated with '<s>phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ</s>' (the weapon-mantra), having meditated on the obstacles as removed, entering within and with a gaze kindled by the rays of <s>Parameśvara</s>, one should look upon the worship-chamber on all sides. [AbhTs 13.16]

children.text: tatra mumukṣur uttarābhimukhas tiṣṭhet yathā bhagavadaghoratejasā jhaṭity eva pruṣṭapāśo bhavet // AbhTs_13.17
children.translated_text: Therein, one who desires liberation should stand facing north, so that through the fiery energy of the blessed <s>Aghora</s> [form of <s>Śiva</s>], one's bonds (<s>pāśa</s>) may be instantly burned away. [AbhTs 13.17]

children.text: tatra parameśvarasvātantryam eva mūrtyābhāsanayā diktattvam avabhāsayati // AbhTs_13.18
children.translated_text: Therein, the sovereignty of <s>Parameśvara</s> alone, through the manifestation of [His] form (<s>mūrti</s>), illuminates direction (<s>dik</s>) as a principle (<s>tattva</s>). [AbhTs 13.18]

children.text: tatra citprakāśa eva madhyaṃ tata itarapravibhāgapravṛtteḥ prakāśasvīkāryam ūrdhvam atathābhūtam adhaḥ prakāśanasammukhīnaṃ pūrvam itarat aparam saṃmukhībhūtaprakāśatvāt anantaraṃ tatprakāśadhārārohasthānaṃ dakṣiṇam ānukūlyāt tatsammukhaṃ tu avabhāsyatvāt uttaram iti dikcatuṣkam // AbhTs_13.19
children.translated_text: Therein, the light of consciousness (<s>cit-prakāśa</s>) alone is the center, since the differentiation of other [directions] proceeds from it. Above is what is to be appropriated by light — what is not of that nature [is] below. What faces the illumination is the east; the other is the west. Because it has the nature of light facing toward [the center], what is immediately next — the place of ascending upon the stream of that light — is the south, due to its congruence; and what faces that [south] is the north, since it is the object of illumination. Thus [the Lord establishes] the four cardinal directions. [AbhTs 13.19]

children.text: tatra madhye bhagavān ūrdhve 'sya aiśānaṃ vaktram adhaḥ pātālavaktram pūrvādidikcatuṣke śrītatpuruṣāghorasadyovāmākhyaṃ dikcatuṣkamadhye anyāś catasraḥ // AbhTs_13.20
children.translated_text: Therein, in the center [stands] the Blessed Lord; above Him, the <s>Īśāna</s> face; below, the <s>Pātāla</s> face; in the four cardinal directions of east and so forth, the [faces] called <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, <s>Sadyojāta</s>, and <s>Vāma</s>; and in the intermediate four directions, four others. [AbhTs 13.20]

children.text: ity evaṃ saṃvinmahimaiva mūrtikṛtaṃ digbhedaṃ bhāsayati iti dik na tattvāntaram // AbhTs_13.21
children.translated_text: Thus, it is the greatness of consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>) alone that illuminates the differentiation of directions as produced by [the Lord's] form — therefore direction is not a separate <s>tattva</s> (principle). [AbhTs 13.21]

children.text: yathā yathā ca svacchāyā laṅghayitum iṣṭā satī puraḥ puro bhavati tathā parameśvaramadhyatām eti sarvādhiṣṭhātṛtaiva mādhyasthyam ity uktam // AbhTs_13.22
children.translated_text: Just as one's own shadow, when one desires to leap over it, always appears in front — so [the Lord] attains centrality in <s>Parameśvara</s>; the state of being the overseer of all is [what is meant by] centrality — so it is said. [AbhTs 13.22]

children.text: evaṃ yathā bhagavān digvibhāgakārī tathā sūryo 'pi sa hi pārameśvary eva jñānaśaktir ity uktaṃ tatra tatra tatra pūrvaṃ vyakteḥ pūrvā yatraiva ca tathā tatraiva evaṃ svātmādhīnāpi svasammukhīnasya deśasya purastāttvāt // AbhTs_13.23
children.translated_text: Just as the Blessed Lord is the creator of directional differentiation, so too is the sun — for it has been stated [in scripture] that the sun is nothing but the knowledge-power (<s>jñāna-śakti</s>) of <s>Parameśvara</s>. Therein, 'east' is prior [= the direction] of prior manifestation, and wherever that [priority holds], there [is the east]. Thus, [direction] too is dependent on one's own Self, since the region facing oneself is 'in front.' [AbhTs 13.23]

children.text: evaṃ svātmasūryaparameśatritayaikībhāvanayā dikcarcā iti abhinavaguptaguravaḥ // AbhTs_13.24
children.translated_text: Thus, through the unification of the triad — one's own Self, the sun, and <s>Parameśvara</s> — there is the contemplation of directions (<s>dik-carcā</s>). So [say] the teachers [in the lineage of] <s>Abhinavagupta</s>. [AbhTs 13.24]

children.text: evaṃ sthite uttarābhimukham upaviśya dehapuryaṣṭakādau ahambhāvatyāgena dehatāṃ dahet saṃnidhāv api paradehavat adehatvāt tato nistaraṅgadhruvadhāmarūḍhasya dṛṣṭisvābhāvyāt yā kila ādyā spandakalā saiva mūrtiḥ tadupari yathopadiṣṭayājyadevatācakranyāsaḥ prādhānyena ca iha śaktayo yājyāḥ // AbhTs_13.25
children.translated_text: This being so, having sat facing north, one should, through the abandonment of the ego-sense in the body, the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>), and the rest, burn the [identification with the] body — since even in proximity [to the body], due to its being like another's body, there is no body-hood. Then, from the natural state of vision of one who has ascended to the unwavering, steady, radiant [level] — that which is the primary pulsation-<s>kalā</s> (<s>spanda-kalā</s>), that alone is the [divine] form. Upon it, one [performs] the <s>nyāsa</s> of the deity-circle to be worshiped, as instructed. And here primarily, the <s>Śaktis</s> (powers) are to be worshiped. [AbhTs 13.25]

children.text: tadāsanatvāt bhagavannavātmādīnāṃ śakter eva ca pūjyatvāt iti guravaḥ // AbhTs_13.26
children.translated_text: Because they constitute the seat (<s>āsana</s>) of the Blessed Lord whose Self is ninefold and so forth, and because it is <s>Śakti</s> alone that is to be worshiped — so [say] the teachers. [AbhTs 13.26]

children.text: tatra ca pañca avasthā jāgradādyāḥ ṣaṣṭhī ca anuttarā nāma svabhāvadaśā anusaṃdheyā // AbhTs_13.27
children.translated_text: And therein, five states — waking and the rest — and a sixth called <s>anuttara</s> (the unsurpassed), the state of one's own nature, are to be contemplated. [AbhTs 13.27]

children.text: iti ṣoḍhā nyāso bhavati // AbhTs_13.28
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>nyāsa</s> becomes sixteenfold. [AbhTs 13.28]

children.text: tatra kāraṇānāṃ brahmaviṣṇurudreśasadāśivaśaktirūpāṇāṃ pratyekam adhiṣṭhānāt ṣaṭtriṃśattattvakalāpasya laukikatattvottīrṇasya bhairavabhaṭṭārakābhedavṛtte nyāse pūrṇatvāt bhairavībhāvaḥ tena etat anavakāśam // AbhTs_13.29
children.translated_text: Therein, because the causes (<s>kāraṇas</s>) — whose forms are <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, and <s>Śakti</s> — each individually preside, the aggregate of thirty-six <s>tattvas</s> (principles), which transcends the worldly <s>tattvas</s>, in the <s>nyāsa</s> whose operation is the non-duality of <s>Bhairava-bhaṭṭāraka</s> (the Lord <s>Bhairava</s>), becomes complete — [hence] the state of <s>Bhairavī</s> (becoming <s>Bhairava</s>). Therefore, this [objection] finds no scope: [AbhTs 13.29]

children.text: yad āhuḥ ataraṅgarūḍhau labdhāyāṃ punaḥ kiṃ tattvasṛṣṭir nyāsādinā iti // AbhTs_13.30
children.translated_text: What they say: 'Once the waveless [state] has been attained, why again [perform] the creation of <s>tattvas</s> through <s>nyāsa</s> and the like?' [AbhTs 13.30]

children.text: tāvat hi tad ataraṅgaṃ bhairavavapuḥ yat svātmani avabhāsitasṛṣṭisaṃhārāvaicitryakoṭi // AbhTs_13.31
children.translated_text: [The answer is:] That waveless <s>Bhairava</s>-body is precisely that within which there shines the multitude of the variety of creation and dissolution in one's own Self. [AbhTs 13.31]

children.text: evam anyonyamelakayogena parameśvarībhūtaṃ prāṇadehabuddhyādi bhāvayitvā bahir antaḥ puṣpadhūpatarpaṇādyair yathāsambhavaṃ pūjayet // AbhTs_13.32
children.translated_text: Thus, having contemplated the <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), body, intellect, and the rest as having become <s>Parameśvara</s> through mutual fusion-<s>yoga</s>, one should worship externally and internally — with flowers, incense, satisfaction-offerings, and the like — as far as possible. [AbhTs 13.32]

children.text: tatra śarīre prāṇe dhiyi ca tadanusāreṇa śūlābjanyāsaṃ kuryāt tad yathā ādhāraśaktimūle mūlaṃ kanda āmūlasārakaṃ lambikānte kalātattvānto daṇḍaḥ māyātmako granthiḥ catuṣkikātmā śuddhavidyāpadmaṃ tatraiva sadāśivabhaṭṭārakaḥ sa eva mahāpretaḥ prakarṣeṇa līnatvāt bodhāt prādhānyena vedyātmakadehakṣayāt nādāmarśātmakatvāc ca iti // AbhTs_13.33
children.translated_text: Therein, in the body, in the <s>prāṇa</s>, and in the intellect, in accordance with that [scheme], one should perform the trident-and-lotus <s>nyāsa</s> (<s>śūlābja-nyāsa</s>). Namely: at the root of the foundation-power (<s>ādhāra-śakti</s>) is the root; the bulb (<s>kanda</s>); the staff that extends from the root up to the end of <s>lambikā</s> (the uvula), ending in the <s>kalā-tattva</s>; the knot (<s>granthi</s>), which is of the nature of <s>Māyā</s>, consisting of four [levels]; the lotus of <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (Pure Knowledge); therein, <s>Sadāśiva-bhaṭṭāraka</s> (the Lord <s>Sadāśiva</s>) himself — He is the <s>Mahāpreta</s> (Great Corpse), because He is supremely absorbed (<s>līna</s>), because of [His] awakening (<s>bodha</s>), because primarily the body whose nature is the object of knowledge is [therein] dissolved, and because [He] is of the nature of <s>nāda</s> (resonance) and <s>āmarśa</s> (reflective awareness). [AbhTs 13.33]

children.text: tan nābhyutthitaṃ tanmūrdharandhratrayanirgataṃ nādāntarvartiśaktivyāpinīsamanārūpamarātrayaṃ dviṣaṭkāntaṃ tadupari śuddhapadmatrayam aunmanasam etasmin viśvamaye bhede āsanīkṛte adhiṣṭhātṛtayā vyāpakabhāvena ādheyabhūtāṃ yathābhimatāṃ devatāṃ kalpayitvā yat tatraiva samasvabhāvanirbharātmani viśvabhāvārpaṇaṃ tad eva pūjanaṃ yad eva tanmayībhavanaṃ tad dhyānaṃ yat tathāvidhāntaḥparāmarśasadbhāvanādāndolanaṃ sa japaḥ yat tathāvidhaparāmarśakramaprabuddhamahātejasā tathābalād eva viśvātmīkaraṇaṃ sa homaḥ tad evaṃ kṛtvā parivāraṃ tata eva vahnirāśer visphuliṅgavat dhyātvā tathaiva pūjayet // AbhTs_13.34
children.translated_text: Arising from that [Sadāśiva lotus], emerging through the three apertures at its crown, the triad of <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Vyāpinī</s>, and <s>Samanā</s> — which abide within the <s>nāda</s> and constitute the three <s>marās</s> (mystical states) — ending in the twelve [levels]; above that, the three pure lotuses; [and at the summit] the <s>Aunmanasa</s> (the state beyond mind). When this all-encompassing differentiation has been made into a seat (<s>āsana</s>), through one's capacity as overseer, in a pervading manner, having established therein the desired deity as what is to be sustained — then: that very offering of the entire universe into that [deity] whose nature is filled with equanimous essence — that alone is worship (<s>pūjana</s>); that very becoming one with it is meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>); that oscillation of the inner contemplation of such a nature in excellent awareness is recitation (<s>japa</s>); that universal self-identification through the great radiance awakened by such a sequence of contemplation, forcefully — that is the fire-offering (<s>homa</s>). Having done thus, one should meditate on the retinue as [emanating] from that very fire-mass like sparks, and worship [them] in the same manner. [AbhTs 13.34]

children.text: dvādaśāntam idaṃ prāgraṃ viśūlaṃ mūlataḥ smaran // AbhTs_13.35
children.translated_text: This [trident] extending forward up to the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (twelve-finger-breadths above the head), remembering the trident from the root — [AbhTs 13.35]

children.text: devīcakrāgragaṃ tyaktakramaḥ khecaratāṃ vrajet // AbhTs_13.36
children.translated_text: having gone to the forefront of the goddess-circle, one should enter the state of <s>Khecarī</s> (sky-traveler), having abandoned [sequential] order. [AbhTs 13.36]

children.text: mūlādhārād dviṣaṭkāntavyomāgrāpūraṇātmikā // AbhTs_13.37
children.translated_text: From the <s>mūlādhāra</s> (root-support) up to the end of the twelve [levels], filling the space at the summit — [AbhTs 13.37]

children.text: khecarīyaṃ khasaṃcāramsthitibhyāṃ khāmṛtāśanāt // AbhTs_13.38
children.translated_text: this is the <s>Khecarī</s> [state] — through the twin [aspects of] movement in the void and abiding [therein], and through the consumption of the nectar of the void. [AbhTs 13.38]

children.text: evam antaryāgamātrād eva vastutaḥ kṛtakṛtyatā // AbhTs_13.39
children.translated_text: Thus, through the inner worship alone, in reality, the state of having accomplished one's purpose [is attained]. [AbhTs 13.39]

children.text: satyataḥ tadāviṣṭasya tathāpi bahir api kāryo yāgo 'vacchedahānaya eva yo 'pi tathā samāveśabhāk na bhavati tasya mukhyo bahiryāgaḥ tadabhyāsāt samāveśalābho yatas tasyāpi tu paśutātirodhānāyāntaryāgaḥ tadarūḍhāv api tatsaṃkalpabalasya śuddhipradatvāt // AbhTs_13.40
children.translated_text: In truth, for one who is pervaded by that [inner realization], nevertheless the external worship too should be performed — for the very purpose of removing limitation. And for one who does not partake of such immersion, the external worship is primary — since through its practice, the attainment of immersion [occurs]. But even for him, the inner worship [serves] for the concealment of his [residual] animal nature (<s>paśutā</s>); and even when one has not yet ascended to that [inner state], because the force of that intention has the power to grant purification. [AbhTs 13.40]

children.text: atha yadā dīkṣāṃ cikīrṣet tadādhivāsanārthaṃ bhūmiparigrahaṃ gaṇeśārcanaṃ kumbhakalaśayoḥ pūjāṃ sthaṇḍilārcanaṃ havanaṃ ca kuryāt // AbhTs_13.41
children.translated_text: Now, when one wishes to perform <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), for the purpose of the preparatory consecration (<s>adhivāsana</s>), one should perform: the claiming of the ground (<s>bhūmi-parigraha</s>), the worship of <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, the worship of the pitcher and water-vessel (<s>kumbha-kalaśa</s>), the worship on the altar-platform (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>), and the fire-offering (<s>havana</s>). [AbhTs 13.41]

children.text: nityanaimittikayos tu sthaṇḍilādyarcanahavane eva // AbhTs_13.42
children.translated_text: But for regular and occasional [rites], the worship and oblation are to be performed on the altar (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>) and so forth. [AbhTs 13.42]

children.text: tatra adhivāsanaṃ śiṣyasya saṃskṛtayogyatādhānam amblīkaraṇam iva dantānāṃ devasya kartavyonmukhatvagrāhaṇam guros tadgrahaṇam // AbhTs_13.43
children.translated_text: There, the consecration (<s>adhivāsana</s>) of the disciple is the imparting of fitness for the ritual transformation—like the curing of the teeth [of a vessel]; the deity's readiness to act; and the guru's grasping of that [readiness]. [AbhTs 13.43]

children.text: upakaraṇadravyāṇāṃ yāgagṛhāntarvartitayā parameśatejobṛṃhaṇena pūjopakaraṇayogyatārpaṇam iti // AbhTs_13.44
children.translated_text: The ritual implements and substances, by being placed within the worship-chamber and thereby nourished by the radiance of the Supreme Lord, are rendered fit as implements of worship. [AbhTs 13.44]

children.text: tatra sarvopakaraṇapūrṇaṃ yāgagṛhaṃ vidhāya bhagavatīṃ mālinīṃ mātṛkāṃ vā smṛtvā tadvarṇatejaḥpuñjabharitaṃ gṛhītaṃ bhāvayan puṣpāñjaliṃ kṣipet // AbhTs_13.45
children.translated_text: There, having arranged the worship-chamber complete with all implements, recalling the Blessed <s>Mālinī</s> or <s>Mātṛkā</s>, contemplating the offering of flowers (<s>puṣpāñjali</s>) as filled with the mass of radiance of her syllables, one should cast [the offering]. [AbhTs 13.45]

children.text: tata uktāstrajaptāni yathāsambhavaṃ siddhārthadhānyākṣatalājādīni tejorūpāṇi vikīrya aiśānyāṃ diśi krameṇa saṃghaṭṭayet iti bhūparigrahaḥ // AbhTs_13.46
children.translated_text: Then, having scattered white mustard seeds, grain, unbroken rice, parched grain, and such—recited upon with the weapon [mantra] as prescribed—in the form of radiance, as resources allow, one should gather them sequentially beginning from the northeastern direction. This is the claiming of the earth (<s>bhūparigraha</s>). [AbhTs 13.46]

children.text: tataḥ śuddhavidyāntam āsanaṃ dattvā gaṇapateḥ pūjā tataḥ kumbham ānandadravyapūritam alaṃkṛtaṃ pūjayet tato yājyam anu pūgaṃ nyasya tatra mukhyaṃ mantraṃ sarvādhiṣṭhātṛtayā vidhipūrvakatvena smaran aṣṭottaraśatamantritaṃ tena taṃ kumbhaṃ kuryāt // AbhTs_13.47
children.translated_text: Then, having given a seat [consecrated] up to <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (Pure Knowledge), worship of <s>Gaṇapati</s> [is performed]. Then one should worship the vessel (<s>kumbha</s>), filled with bliss-substances and adorned. Then, placing the betel-nut (<s>pūga</s>) after the disciple, recalling the primary <s>mantra</s> with the authority over all [deities], preceded by proper ritual procedure, one should make that vessel consecrated with one hundred and eight [repetitions of the] <s>mantra</s>. [AbhTs 13.47]

children.text: dvitīyakalaśe vighnaśamanāya astraṃ yajet // AbhTs_13.48
children.translated_text: In the second vessel, one should worship the weapon [mantra] for the pacification of obstacles. [AbhTs 13.48]

children.text: tataḥ svasvadikṣu lokapālān sāstrān pūjayet // AbhTs_13.49
children.translated_text: Then one should worship the <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians) with their weapons in their respective directions. [AbhTs 13.49]

children.text: tataḥ śiṣyasya prāk dīkṣitasya haste astrakalaśaṃ dadyāt // AbhTs_13.50
children.translated_text: Then one should give the weapon-vessel into the hand of the disciple who has been previously initiated. [AbhTs 13.50]

children.text: svayaṃ ca guruḥ kumbham ādadīta // AbhTs_13.51
children.translated_text: And the guru himself should take the [main] vessel (<s>kumbha</s>). [AbhTs 13.51]

children.text: tataḥ śiṣyaṃ gṛhaparyanteṣu vighnaśamanāya dhārāṃ pātayantaṃ sakumbho 'nugacchet imaṃ mantraṃ paṭhan bho bhoḥ śakra tvayā svasyāṃ diśi vighnapraśāntaye // AbhTs_13.52
children.translated_text: Then, with the disciple pouring a stream [of water] at the boundaries of the house for the pacification of obstacles, he should follow with the vessel, reciting this <s>mantra</s>: 'O <s>Śakra</s>, in your own direction, for the pacification of obstacles, [AbhTs 13.52]

children.text: sāvadhānena karmāntaṃ bhavitavyaṃ śivājñayā // AbhTs_13.53
children.translated_text: By the command of <s>Śiva</s>, you must be attentive until the end of the rite.' [AbhTs 13.53]

children.text: tryakṣare nāmni bho ity ekam eva // AbhTs_13.54
children.translated_text: In a name of three syllables, 'bho' counts as one only. [AbhTs 13.54]

children.text: tata aiśānyāṃ diśi kumbhaṃ sthāpayet // AbhTs_13.55
children.translated_text: Then one should place the vessel in the northeastern direction. [AbhTs 13.55]

children.text: vikiropari astrakalaśam // AbhTs_13.56
children.translated_text: The weapon-vessel upon the scattered [grains]. [AbhTs 13.56]

children.text: tata ubhayapūjanam // AbhTs_13.57
children.translated_text: Then worship of both [vessels]. [AbhTs 13.57]

children.text: tataḥ sthaṇḍilamadhye parameśapūjanam // AbhTs_13.58
children.translated_text: Then worship of the Supreme Lord in the center of the altar (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>). [AbhTs 13.58]

children.text: tataḥ agnikuṇḍaṃ parameśvaraśaktirūpatayā bhāvayitvā tatra agniṃ prajvālya hṛdayāntarbodhāgninā saha ekīkṛtya mantraparāmarśasāhityena jvalantaṃ śivāgniṃ bhāvayitvā tatra nyasya abhyarcya mantrān tarpayet ājyena tilaiś ca // AbhTs_13.59
children.translated_text: Then, having contemplated the fire-pit as having the form of the Supreme Lord's power (<s>śakti</s>), having kindled the fire therein and unified it with the fire of inner awakening in the heart, having contemplated the blazing <s>Śiva</s>-fire with the accompaniment of <s>mantra</s>-awareness, having placed [the fire] there and worshipped it, one should satisfy the <s>mantras</s> with clarified butter (<s>ājya</s>) and sesame seeds. [AbhTs 13.59]

children.text: arghapātreṇa ca prokṣaṇam eva tilājyādīnāṃ saṃskāraḥ // AbhTs_13.60
children.translated_text: And the sprinkling from the oblation-vessel (<s>arghapātra</s>) is itself the consecration of the sesame, butter, and other [substances]. [AbhTs 13.60]

children.text: sruksruvayoś ca parameśābhedadṛṣṭir eva hi saṃskāraḥ // AbhTs_13.61
children.translated_text: And for the ladle (<s>sruk</s>) and spoon (<s>sruva</s>), the vision of non-difference from the Supreme Lord is indeed the consecration. [AbhTs 13.61]

children.text: tato yathāśakti hutvā sruksruvau ūrdhvādhomukhatayā śaktiśivarūpau parasparonmukhau vidhāya samapādotthito dvādaśāntagaganoditaśivapūrṇacandraniḥsṛtapatatparāmṛtadhārābhāvanāṃ kurvan vauṣaḍantaṃ mantram uccārayan ca ājyakṣayāntaṃ tiṣṭhet iti pūrṇāhutiḥ mantracakrasaṃtarpaṇī // AbhTs_13.62
children.translated_text: Then, having offered [oblations] according to one's capacity, placing the ladle and spoon facing upward and downward respectively—as forms of <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śiva</s>, facing each other—standing upright with even feet, contemplating the stream of supreme nectar (<s>parāmṛta</s>) falling from the full moon of <s>Śiva</s> risen in the sky of the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (the twelfth space above the head), and uttering the <s>mantra</s> ending with <s>vauṣaṭ</s>, one should stand until the butter is exhausted. This is the full oblation (<s>pūrṇāhuti</s>), which satisfies the circle of <s>mantras</s>. [AbhTs 13.62]

children.text: tataś caruṃ prokṣitam ānīya sthaṇḍilakalaśakumbhavahniṣu bhāgaṃ bhāgaṃ nivedya ekabhāgam avaśeṣya śiṣyāya bhāgaṃ dadyāt // AbhTs_13.63
children.translated_text: Then, bringing the consecrated ritual porridge (<s>caru</s>), having offered a portion each to the altar, vessel, pitcher, and fire, and setting aside one portion, one should give a share to the disciple. [AbhTs 13.63]

children.text: tato dantakāṣṭham // AbhTs_13.64
children.translated_text: Then the tooth-stick (<s>dantakāṣṭha</s>). [AbhTs 13.64]

children.text: tatpāto 'gniyamanirṛtidikṣu adhaś ca na śubha iti // AbhTs_13.65
children.translated_text: Its falling in the directions of fire (<s>Agni</s>), <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Nirṛti</s>, or downward, is inauspicious. [AbhTs 13.65]

children.text: tatra homo 'stramantreṇa kāryaḥ // AbhTs_13.66
children.translated_text: In that [case], an oblation with the weapon-<s>mantra</s> should be performed. [AbhTs 13.66]

children.text: tato vikṣepaparihāreṇa bhāvimantradarśanayogyatāyai baddhanetraṃ śiṣyaṃ praveśya jānusthitaṃ taṃ kṛtvā puṣpāñjaliṃ kṣepayet // AbhTs_13.67
children.translated_text: Then, for the removal of distraction and for fitness to behold the future <s>mantra</s>, having brought in the disciple with his eyes blindfolded, having made him kneel, one should have him cast the offering of flowers (<s>puṣpāñjali</s>). [AbhTs 13.67]

children.text: tataḥ sahasā apāsitanetrabandho 'sau śaktipātānugṛhītakaraṇatvāt saṃnihitamantraṃ tatsthānaṃ sākṣātkāreṇa paśyan tanmayo bhavati anugṛhītakaraṇānāṃ mantrasaṃnidhiḥ pratyakṣaḥ yatas trasyatām iva bhūtānām // AbhTs_13.68
children.translated_text: Then, the blindfold suddenly removed, he—because his faculties are graced by the descent of power (<s>śaktipāta</s>)—seeing the <s>mantra</s> present at that location through direct realization (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>), becomes identified with it. For those whose faculties are graced, the presence of the <s>mantra</s> is directly perceived, since [even] beings seem to tremble [before it]. [AbhTs 13.68]

children.text: tataḥ svadakṣiṇahaste dīpyatayā devatācakraṃ pūjayitvā taṃ hastaṃ mūrdhahṛnnābhiṣu śiṣyasya pāśān dahantaṃ nikṣipet // AbhTs_13.69
children.translated_text: Then, having worshipped the circle of deities with his right hand [held] as blazing, he should place that hand on the head, heart, and navel of the disciple, burning [his] bonds (<s>pāśa</s>). [AbhTs 13.69]

children.text: tato vāme somyatayā pūjayitvā śuddhatattvāpyāyinaṃ tataḥ praṇāmaṃ kuryāt // AbhTs_13.70
children.translated_text: Then, having worshipped with the left hand [held] as gentle (<s>somya</s>), nourishing the pure <s>tattvas</s> (principles), thereafter he should make obeisance. [AbhTs 13.70]

children.text: tato bhūtadevatādigbaliṃ madyamāṃsajalādipūrṇaṃ bahir dadyāt ācāmeta // AbhTs_13.71
children.translated_text: Then he should give the offering to the <s>bhūtas</s> (beings), deities, and the directions outside, filled with liquor, meat, water, and such, and sip water [for purification]. [AbhTs 13.71]

children.text: tataḥ svayaṃ carubhojanaṃ kṛtvā śiṣyātmanā saha aikyam āpannaḥ prabuddhavṛttiḥ tiṣṭhet // AbhTs_13.72
children.translated_text: Then, having himself eaten the ritual porridge (<s>caru</s>), having attained unity with the Self of the disciple, he should remain with awakened awareness. [AbhTs 13.72]

children.text: svapan api prabhāte śiṣyaḥ cet aśubhaṃ svapnaṃ vadet tat asmai na vyākuryāt // AbhTs_13.73
children.translated_text: Even if sleeping—if in the morning the disciple reports an inauspicious dream, he should not interpret it for him. [AbhTs 13.73]

children.text: śaṅkātaṅkau hi tathāsya syātām kevalam astreṇa tanniṣkṛtiṃ kuryāt // AbhTs_13.74
children.translated_text: For that would cause him apprehension and anxiety. One should merely perform a counteraction with the weapon [mantra]. [AbhTs 13.74]

children.text: tatas tathaiva parameśvaraṃ pūjayitvā tadagre śiṣyasya prāṇakrameṇa praviśya hṛtkaṇṭhatālulalāṭarandhradvādaśānteṣu ṣaṭsu kāraṇaṣaṭkasparśaṃ kurvan pratyekam aṣṭau saṃskārān cintayan kaṃcit kālaṃ śiṣyaprāṇaṃ tatraiva viśramayya punar avarohet // AbhTs_13.75
