children.translated_text: Then, having worshipped the Supreme Lord in the same manner, before him, entering into the disciple through the sequence of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), touching the six causal [principles] at the six [points]—heart, throat, palate, forehead, <s>randhra</s> (cranial aperture), and <s>dvādaśānta</s> (twelfth space)—contemplating eight <s>saṃskāras</s> (ritual transformations) at each, and for some time resting the disciple's <s>prāṇa</s> right there, he should descend again. [AbhTs 13.75]

children.text: ity evāpāditāṣṭācatvāriṃśatsaṃskāroparikṛtarudrāṃśāpattiḥ samayībhavati // AbhTs_13.76
children.translated_text: Thus, with the forty-eight <s>saṃskāras</s> so accomplished, the attainment of the <s>Rudra</s>-portion effected upon [the disciple]—he becomes a <s>samayī</s> (one who has received the samaya initiation). [AbhTs 13.76]

children.text: tataḥ asmai pūjyaṃ mantraṃ puṣpādyaiḥ saha arpayet // AbhTs_13.77
children.translated_text: Then one should bestow upon him the <s>mantra</s> to be worshipped, together with flowers and other [offerings]. [AbhTs 13.77]

children.text: tataḥ samayān asmai nirūpayet // AbhTs_13.78
children.translated_text: Then one should set forth the observances (<s>samaya</s>) for him. [AbhTs 13.78]

children.text: gurau sarvātmanā bhaktiḥ tathā śāstre deve tatpratidvaṃdvini parāṅmukhatā guruvat guruputrādeḥ vidyāsambandhakṛtasya tatpūrvadīkṣitādeḥ saṃdarśanam yaunasambandhasya tadārādhanārtham na tu svata iti mantavyam // AbhTs_13.79
children.translated_text: Devotion to the guru with one's whole being; likewise to the scripture and the deity; aversion toward what is opposed to those; showing respect to the guru's son and others, to those connected by knowledge-lineage, and to those previously initiated by the guru, just as to the guru [himself]. The reason for [showing respect to those connected by] family relationship is for the purpose of serving [the guru], not on its own account—this should be understood. [AbhTs 13.79]

children.text: striyo vandhyāyās tajjugupsāhetuṃ na kuryāt // AbhTs_13.80
children.translated_text: One should not do anything that would cause disgust toward a barren woman. [AbhTs 13.80]

children.text: devatānāma gurunāma tathā mantraṃ pūjākālāt ṛte na uccārayet // AbhTs_13.81
children.translated_text: One should not utter the name of the deity, the name of the guru, or the <s>mantra</s> except at the time of worship. [AbhTs 13.81]

children.text: gurūpabhuktaṃ śayyādi na bhuñjīta // AbhTs_13.82
children.translated_text: One should not use a bed or the like that has been used by the guru. [AbhTs 13.82]

children.text: yat kiṃcit laukikaṃ krīḍādi tat gurusaṃnidhau na kuryāt // AbhTs_13.83
children.translated_text: Whatever worldly activity, such as play and the like, one should not do in the presence of the guru. [AbhTs 13.83]

children.text: tadvyatirekeṇa na anyatra utkarṣabuddhiṃ kuryāt // AbhTs_13.84
children.translated_text: Apart from [the guru], one should not regard anything else as superior. [AbhTs 13.84]

children.text: sarvatra śrāddhādau gurum eva pūjayet // AbhTs_13.85
children.translated_text: Everywhere, in <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites) and such, one should worship the guru alone. [AbhTs 13.85]

children.text: sarveṣu ca naimittikeṣu śākinītyādiśabdān na vadet // AbhTs_13.86
children.translated_text: And at all occasional [rites], one should not utter words like '<s>Śākinī</s>' and so forth. [AbhTs 13.86]

children.text: parvadināni pūjayet // AbhTs_13.87
children.translated_text: One should perform worship on festival days. [AbhTs 13.87]

children.text: vaiṣṇavādyair adhodṛṣṭibhiḥ saha saṃgatiṃ na kuryāt // AbhTs_13.88
children.translated_text: One should not associate with <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> and others who have a downward vision (<s>adhodṛṣṭi</s>). [AbhTs 13.88]

children.text: etacchāsanasthān pūrvajātibuddhyā na paśyet // AbhTs_13.89
children.translated_text: One should not regard those established in this teaching with the notion of [inferior] birth-status. [AbhTs 13.89]

children.text: guruvarge gṛhāgate yathāśakti yāgaṃ kuryāt // AbhTs_13.90
children.translated_text: When members of the guru-family come to the house, one should perform worship according to one's capacity. [AbhTs 13.90]

children.text: adhomārgasthitaṃ kaṃcit vaiṣṇavādyaṃ tacchāstrakulāt gurūkṛtyāpi tyajet // AbhTs_13.91
children.translated_text: Even if one has made a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> or another of the lower path into a guru by that school's lineage, one should abandon [that association]. [AbhTs 13.91]

children.text: tadāpi na utkarṣabuddhyā paśyet // AbhTs_13.92
children.translated_text: Even then, one should not regard [them] with the notion of superiority. [AbhTs 13.92]

children.text: liṅgibhiḥ saha samācāramelanaṃ na kuryāt tān kevalaṃ yathāśakti pūjayet // AbhTs_13.93
children.translated_text: One should not mix in conduct with <s>liṅgins</s> (those who bear external religious marks); one should merely worship them according to one's capacity. [AbhTs 13.93]

children.text: śaṅkās tyajet // AbhTs_13.94
children.translated_text: One should abandon doubts. [AbhTs 13.94]

children.text: cakre sthitaś caramāgryādivibhāgaṃ janmakṛtaṃ na saṃkalpayet // AbhTs_13.95
children.translated_text: When standing in the [ritual] circle (<s>cakra</s>), one should not conceive of distinctions based on birth, such as lowest and highest. [AbhTs 13.95]

children.text: śarīrāt ṛte na anyat āyatanatīrthādikaṃ bahumānena paśyet // AbhTs_13.96
children.translated_text: Apart from the body, one should not regard anything else—temple, sacred ford (<s>tīrtha</s>), and such—with special reverence. [AbhTs 13.96]

children.text: mantrahṛdayam anavarataṃ smaret ity evaṃ śiṣyaḥ śrutvā praṇamya abhyupagamya guruṃ dhanadāraśarīraparyantayā dakṣiṇayā paritoṣya pūrvadīkṣitāṃś ca dīnānāthādikān tarpayet // AbhTs_13.97
children.translated_text: One should constantly remember the heart of the <s>mantra</s>. Thus, the disciple, having heard [these observances], having bowed, having assented, should satisfy the guru with offerings (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) extending to wealth, wife, and body; and should also satisfy the previously initiated, the destitute, the helpless, and others. [AbhTs 13.97]

children.text: bhāvividhinā ca mūrticakraṃ tarpayet // AbhTs_13.98
children.translated_text: And with the ritual of inner contemplation (<s>bhāvividhi</s>), he should satisfy the circle of embodied [deities]. [AbhTs 13.98]

children.text: itthaṃ samayībhavati // AbhTs_13.99
children.translated_text: Thus he becomes a <s>samayī</s> (covenant-holder). [AbhTs 13.99]

children.text: mantrābhyāse nityapūjāyāṃ śravaṇe 'dhyayane adhikārī naimittike tu sarvatra gurum eva abhyarthayet // AbhTs_13.100
children.translated_text: He is authorized for the practice of <s>mantra</s>, daily worship, hearing, and study. But for occasional [rites], he should in all cases entreat the guru alone. [AbhTs 13.100]

children.text: iti sāmayiko vidhiḥ // AbhTs_13.101
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>sāmayika</s> (covenant) procedure. [AbhTs 13.101]

children.text: atha putrakadīkṣāvidhiḥ // AbhTs_14.1
children.translated_text: Now, the procedure of <s>putraka-dīkṣā</s> (son-initiation). [AbhTs 14.1]

children.text: sa ca vistīrṇaḥ tantrālokāt avadhāryaḥ // AbhTs_14.2
children.translated_text: That is extensive and should be ascertained from the <s>Tantrāloka</s>. [AbhTs 14.2]

children.text: saṃkṣiptas tu ucyate // AbhTs_14.3
children.translated_text: But the abridged [version] is stated [here]. [AbhTs 14.3]

children.text: samayyantaṃ vidhiṃ kṛtvā tṛtīye 'hni triśūlābje maṇḍale sāmudāyikaṃ yāgaṃ pūjayet tatra bāhyaparivāraṃ dvāradevatācakraṃ ca bahiḥ pūjayet tato maṇḍalapūrvabhāge aiśakoṇāt ārabhya āgneyāntaṃ paṅktikrameṇa gaṇapatiṃ guruṃ paramaguruṃ parameṣṭhinaṃ pūrvācāryān yoginīcakraṃ vāgīśvarīṃ kṣetrapālaṃ ca pūjayet // AbhTs_14.4
children.translated_text: Having performed the procedure up to the <s>samaya</s> [initiation], on the third day, in the <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred diagram) of the trident-lotus, one should worship the collective worship (<s>sāmudāyika yāga</s>). Therein, one should worship the outer retinue and the circle of door-deities outside. Then, on the eastern side of the <s>maṇḍala</s>, beginning from the northeastern corner to the southeastern [corner], in a row one should worship <s>Gaṇapati</s>, the guru, the supreme guru (<s>paramaguru</s>), the supreme-of-the-supreme (<s>parameṣṭhin</s>), the former teachers, the circle of <s>yoginīs</s>, <s>Vāgīśvarī</s>, and <s>Kṣetrapāla</s>. [AbhTs 14.4]

children.text: tata ājñāṃ samucitām ādāya śūlamūlāt prabhṛti sitakamalāntaṃ samastam adhvānaṃ nyasya arcayet tato madhyame triśūle madhyārāyāṃ bhagavatī śrīparābhaṭṭārikā bhairavanāthena saha vāmārāyāṃ tathaiva śrīmadaparā dakṣiṇārāyāṃ śrīparāparā dakṣiṇe triśūle madhye śrīparāparā vāme triśūle madhye śrīmadaparā dve tu yathāsvam // AbhTs_14.5
children.translated_text: Then, having received the appropriate command, beginning from the base of the trident up to the white lotus, having placed and worshipped the entire course (<s>adhvan</s>). Then, on the middle trident, on the central spoke: the Blessed <s>Śrī Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s> together with Lord <s>Bhairava</s>; on the left spoke, likewise the glorious <s>Aparā</s>; on the right spoke, <s>Śrī Parāparā</s>. On the right trident, in the center, <s>Śrī Parāparā</s>; on the left trident, in the center, the glorious <s>Aparā</s>. And the two [flanking spokes] according to their own [positions]. [AbhTs 14.5]

children.text: evaṃ sarvasthānādhiṣṭhātṛtve bhagavatyāḥ sarvaṃ pūrṇaṃ tadadhiṣṭhānāt bhavati iti // AbhTs_14.6
children.translated_text: Thus, through the presiding lordship of the Blessed Goddess over all places, everything becomes complete through her sovereignty. [AbhTs 14.6]

children.text: tato madhyaśūlamadhyārāyāṃ samastaṃ devatācakraṃ lokapālāstraparyantam abhinnatayaiva pūjayet tadadhiṣṭhānāt sarvatra pūjitam // AbhTs_14.7
children.translated_text: Then, on the central spoke of the middle trident, one should worship the entire circle of deities, up to the world-guardians and weapons, as non-different [from the Goddess]. Through her sovereignty, [what is worshipped] there is worshipped everywhere. [AbhTs 14.7]

children.text: tataḥ kumbhe kalaśe maṇḍale agnau svātmani ca abhedabhāvanayā pañcādhikaraṇam anusaṃdhiṃ kuryāt tataḥ parameśvarādvayarasabṛṃhitena puṣpādinā viśeṣapūjāṃ kuryāt // AbhTs_14.8
children.translated_text: Then, in the vessel (<s>kumbha</s>), the pitcher (<s>kalaśa</s>), the <s>maṇḍala</s>, the fire, and one's own Self, one should perform the five-fold contemplative integration (<s>anusaṃdhi</s>) with the awareness of non-difference. Then, with flowers and other [offerings] nourished by the non-dual essence of the Supreme Lord, one should perform the special worship. [AbhTs 14.8]

children.text: kiṃ bahunā tarpaṇanaivedyaparipūrṇaṃ vittaśāṭhyavirahito yāgasthānaṃ kuryāt // AbhTs_14.9
children.translated_text: What more [need be said]? One should make the worship-place complete with satisfaction-offerings (<s>tarpaṇa</s>) and food-offerings (<s>naivedya</s>), free from miserliness regarding wealth. [AbhTs 14.9]

children.text: asati vitte tu mahāmaṇḍalayāgo na kartavya eva // AbhTs_14.10
children.translated_text: But in the absence of wealth, the great <s>maṇḍala</s> worship should definitely not be performed. [AbhTs 14.10]

children.text: paśūṃś ca jīvato nivedayet // AbhTs_14.11
children.translated_text: And one should offer the sacrificial animals (<s>paśu</s>) while living. [AbhTs 14.11]

children.text: te 'pi hi evam anugṛhītā bhavanti iti kāruṇikatayā paśuvidhau na vicikitset // AbhTs_14.12
children.translated_text: For they too are thereby graced. Therefore, out of compassion, one should not hesitate in the procedure regarding the animal (<s>paśu</s>). [AbhTs 14.12]

children.text: tato 'gnau parameśvaraṃ tilājyādibhiḥ saṃtarpya tadagre 'nyaṃ paśuṃ vapāhomārthaṃ kuryāt devatācakraṃ tadvapayā tarpayet punar maṇḍalaṃ pūjayet tataḥ parameśvaraṃ vijñapya sarvābhinnasamastaṣaḍadhvaparipūrṇam ātmānaṃ bhāvayitvā śiṣyaṃ puro 'vasthitaṃ kuryāt // AbhTs_14.13
children.translated_text: Then, having satisfied the Supreme Lord in the fire with sesame, clarified butter, and other [substances], before him one should prepare another animal for the purpose of the fat-oblation (<s>vapāhoma</s>), satisfy the circle of deities with its fat, and again worship the <s>maṇḍala</s>. Then, having informed the Supreme Lord, having contemplated oneself as filled with the complete six courses (<s>ṣaḍadhva</s>), all non-different, one should place the disciple before [oneself]. [AbhTs 14.13]

children.text: parokṣadīkṣāyāṃ jīvanmṛtarūpāyām agre taṃ dhyāyet tadīyāṃ vā pratikṛtiṃ darbhagomayādimayīm agre sthāpayet // AbhTs_14.14
children.translated_text: In the case of initiation at a distance (<s>parokṣadīkṣā</s>), which applies to the living or the dead, one should meditate on him [the disciple] before [oneself], or place before oneself his effigy made of <s>darbha</s> grass, cow-dung, and the like. [AbhTs 14.14]

children.text: tathāvidhaṃ śiṣyam arghapātravipruṭprokṣitaṃ puṣpādibhiś ca pūjitaṃ kṛtvā samastam adhvānaṃ taddehe nyaset // AbhTs_14.15
children.translated_text: Having thus sprinkled the disciple with drops from the oblation-vessel (<s>arghapātra</s>) and worshipped him with flowers and other [offerings], one should place the entire course (<s>adhvan</s>) upon his body. [AbhTs 14.15]

children.text: tata itthaṃ vicārayet bhogecchoḥ śubhaṃ na śodhayet // AbhTs_14.16
children.translated_text: Then one should deliberate thus: For one who desires enjoyment (<s>bhogecchu</s>), the auspicious [karma] should not be purified. [AbhTs 14.16]

children.text: mumukṣos tu śubhāśubham ubhayam api // AbhTs_14.17
children.translated_text: But for one who desires liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>), both the auspicious and the inauspicious. [AbhTs 14.17]

children.text: nirbījāyāṃ tu samayapāśān api śodhayet sā ca āsannamaraṇasya atyantamūrkhasyāpi kartavyā iti parameśvarājñā tasyāpi tu gurudevatāgnibhaktiniṣṭhatvamātrāt siddhiḥ // AbhTs_14.18
children.translated_text: But in the seedless [initiation] (<s>nirbījā</s>), one should purify even the bonds of the <s>samaya</s> observances. And that [initiation] should be given even to one near death or to one who is utterly ignorant—such is the command of the Supreme Lord. Even for such a one, perfection is achieved merely through devotion to the guru, the deity, and the fire. [AbhTs 14.18]

children.text: atra ca sarvatra vāsanāgrahaṇam eva bhedakam mantrāṇāṃ vāsanānuguṇyena tattatkāryakāritvāt // AbhTs_14.19
children.translated_text: And here, in all cases, it is the grasping of the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) alone that is the differentiating factor, since <s>mantras</s> produce their respective effects in accordance with the impressions. [AbhTs 14.19]

children.text: evaṃ vāsanābhedam anusaṃdhāya mukhyamantraparāmarśaviśeṣeṇa samastam adhvānaṃ svadehagataṃ śivādvayabhāvanayā śodhayet // AbhTs_14.20
children.translated_text: Thus, having contemplated the differentiation of impressions, with a specific awareness of the primary <s>mantra</s>, one should purify the entire course (<s>adhvan</s>) residing in one's own body through the contemplation of non-duality with <s>Śiva</s>. [AbhTs 14.20]

children.text: evaṃ krameṇa pādāṅguṣṭhāt prabhṛti dvādaśāntaparyantaṃ svātmadehasvātmacaitanyābhinnīkṛtadehacaitanyasya śiṣyasya āsādya tatraiva anantānandasarasi svātantryaiśvaryasāre samastecchājñānakriyāśaktinirbharasamastadevatācakreśvare samastādhvabharite cinmātrāvaśeṣaviśvabhāvamaṇḍale tathāvidharūpaikīkāreṇa śiṣyātmanā saha ekībhūto viśrāntim āsādayet ity evaṃ parameśvarābhinno 'sau bhavati // AbhTs_14.21
children.translated_text: Thus, progressively, from the tip of the big toe up to the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (twelfth space above the head), arriving at [the state where] the consciousness of the disciple's body has been made non-different from the consciousness of one's own body and one's own Self—there, in that very lake of infinite bliss (<s>anantānandasaras</s>), whose essence is the autonomy of sovereignty, replete with all powers of will, knowledge, and action, the lord of the entire circle of deities, filled with the entire course, the sphere of the universe-nature with consciousness alone remaining—through unification with that very form, having become one with the Self of the disciple, one should attain repose. Thus, he becomes non-different from the Supreme Lord. [AbhTs 14.21]

children.text: tato yadi bhogecchuḥ syāt tato yatraiva tattve bhogecchā asya bhavati tatraiva samastavyastatayā yojayet // AbhTs_14.22
children.translated_text: Then, if he desires enjoyment, one should connect him, completely and in every particular, with whatever <s>tattva</s> (principle) he desires enjoyment in. [AbhTs 14.22]

children.text: tadanantaraṃ śeṣavṛttaye parameśvarasvabhāvāt jhaṭiti prasṛtaṃ śuddhatattvamayaṃ deham asmai cintayet ity eṣā samastapāśaviyojikā dīkṣā // AbhTs_14.23
children.translated_text: Immediately thereafter, for the continuation of what remains [of life], one should contemplate for him a body made of pure <s>tattvas</s>, swiftly projected from the nature of the Supreme Lord. This is the initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) that severs all bonds. [AbhTs 14.23]

children.text: tataḥ śiṣyo guruṃ dakṣiṇābhiḥ pūrvavat pūjayet // AbhTs_14.24
children.translated_text: Then the disciple should worship the guru with offerings (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) as before. [AbhTs 14.24]

children.text: tato 'gnau śiṣyasya vidhiṃ kuryāt śrīparāmantraḥ amukasyāmukaṃ tattvaṃ śodhayāmi iti svāhāntaṃ pratitattvaṃ tisra āhutayaḥ ante pūrṇā vauṣaḍantā // AbhTs_14.25
children.translated_text: Then one should perform the rite for the disciple in the fire: the <s>Śrī Parā mantra</s>, 'I purify such-and-such <s>tattva</s> of so-and-so,' ending with <s>svāhā</s>, three oblations per <s>tattva</s>, and at the end a full [oblation] ending with <s>vauṣaṭ</s>. [AbhTs 14.25]

children.text: evaṃ śivāntatattvaśuddhiḥ tato yojanikoktakrameṇa pūrṇāhutiḥ // AbhTs_14.26
children.translated_text: Thus is the purification of <s>tattva</s>s (principles) up to <s>Śiva</s>. Then, according to the procedure stated in the <s>yojanikā</s> (unification ritual), [follows] the <s>pūrṇāhuti</s> (complete oblation). [AbhTs 14.26]

children.text: bhogecchoḥ bhogasthāne yojanikārtham aparā śuddhatattvasṛṣṭyartham anyā // AbhTs_14.27
children.translated_text: For one desiring enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>), another [oblation] for the purpose of the <s>yojanikā</s> at the place of enjoyment; yet another for the purpose of creation of the pure <s>tattva</s>s. [AbhTs 14.27]

children.text: tato guroḥ dakṣiṇābhiḥ pūjanam ity eṣā putrakadīkṣā // AbhTs_14.28
children.translated_text: Then, worship of the guru with offerings (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>)—this is the <s>putraka-dīkṣā</s> (son-initiation), [AbhTs 14.28]

children.text: yatra vartamānam ekaṃ varjayitvā bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyac ca karma śudhyati // AbhTs_14.29
children.translated_text: In which, except for the one present [karma], both past and future <s>karma</s> is purified. [AbhTs 14.29]

children.text: yadā punar āsannamaraṇasya svayaṃ vā bandhumukhena śaktipāta upajāyate tadā asmai sadyaḥ samutkramaṇadīkṣāṃ kuryāt // AbhTs_15.1
children.translated_text: When, however, for one who is near death, <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of power) arises either spontaneously or through the agency of a kinsman, then one should immediately perform for him the <s>samutkramaṇa-dīkṣā</s> (initiation of ascent/departure). [AbhTs 15.1]

children.text: samastam adhvānaṃ śiṣye nyasya taṃ ca krameṇa śodhayitvā bhagavatīṃ kālarātrīm marmakartanīṃ nyasya tayā kramāt kramaṃ marmapāśān vibhidya brahmarandhravarti śiṣyacaitanyaṃ kuryāt // AbhTs_15.2
children.translated_text: Having deposited the entire path (<s>adhvan</s>) in the disciple, and having purified it in sequence, and having deposited the Blessed Goddess <s>Kālarātrī</s>, the cutter of the vital joints (<s>marman</s>), and by her cutting the bonds at the vital joints one by one, one should make the disciple's consciousness ascend to the <s>brahmarandhra</s> (aperture at the crown of the head). [AbhTs 15.2]

children.text: tataḥ pūrvoktakrameṇa yojanikārthaṃ pūrṇāhutiṃ dadyāt yathā pūrṇāhutyante jīvo niṣkrāntaḥ paramaśivābhinno bhavati // AbhTs_15.3
children.translated_text: Then, according to the procedure described earlier, one should offer the <s>pūrṇāhuti</s> (complete oblation) for the purpose of the <s>yojanikā</s> (unification), so that at the conclusion of the <s>pūrṇāhuti</s>, the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), having departed, becomes non-different from the supreme <s>Śiva</s>. [AbhTs 15.3]

children.text: bubhukṣos tu dvitīyā pūrṇāhutiḥ // AbhTs_15.4
children.translated_text: But for one who desires experience, there is a second <s>pūrṇāhuti</s>. [AbhTs 15.4]

children.text: bhogasthāne yojanāya tatkāle ca tasya jīvalayaḥ nātra śeṣavartanam brahmavidyāṃ vā karṇe paṭhet sā hi parāmarśasvabhāvā sadyaḥ prabuddhapaśucaitanye prabuddhavimarśaṃ karoti // AbhTs_15.5
children.translated_text: For the purpose of unification at the place of enjoyment. And at that time, there is the dissolution of his individual life-force. There is no continuation of residual [<s>karma</s>] here. Or one may recite the <s>brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>) into his ear, for it, being of the nature of reflective awareness (<s>parāmarśa</s>), immediately produces awakened reflective cognition in the consciousness of the awakened <s>paśu</s> (bound soul). [AbhTs 15.5]

children.text: samayyāder api ca etatpāṭhe 'dhikāraḥ // AbhTs_15.6
children.translated_text: Even for one of the <s>samaya</s> (novice) grade, there is qualification for this recitation. [AbhTs 15.6]

children.text: sapratyayāṃ nirbījāṃ tu yadi dīkṣāṃ mūḍhāya āyātaśaktipātāya ca darśayet tadā hi śivahastadānakāle ayaṃ vidhiḥ trikoṇam āgneyaṃ jvālākarālaṃ rephavisphuliṅgaṃ bahirvātyācakradhyāyamānaṃ maṇḍalaṃ dakṣiṇahaste cintayitvā tatraiva haste bījaṃ kiṃcit nikṣipya ūrdhvādhorephavibodhitaphaṭkāraparamparābhiḥ asya tāṃ jananaśaktiṃ dahet evaṃ kurvan taṃ hastaṃ śiṣyasya mūrdhani kṣipet iti dvayor api eṣā dīkṣā nirbījā svakāryakaraṇasāmarthyavidhvaṃsinī bhavati sthāvarāṇām api dīkṣyatvena uktatvāt vāyupurāntarvyavasthitaṃ dodhūyamānaṃ śiṣyaṃ laghūbhūtaṃ cintayet yena tulayā laghuḥ dṛśyate iti // AbhTs_15.7
children.translated_text: But if one were to perform a <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) that is 'with-conviction' (<s>sapratyayā</s>) yet 'seedless' (<s>nirbījā</s>) for one who is deluded or for one upon whom <s>śaktipāta</s> has come, then at the time of 'giving the hand of <s>Śiva</s>'—this is the procedure: one should visualize in the right hand a fiery triangle, terrifying with flames, with sparks of the syllable <s>ra</s>, surrounded by an externally revolving circle of wind-<s>maṇḍala</s>; having deposited a seed-syllable in that very hand, one should burn that being's generative power with successive <s>phaṭ</s>-sounds awakened by the syllable <s>ra</s> above and below. Having done so, one should place that hand on the disciple's head. This initiation of both [types] is 'seedless'—it destroys the capacity of one's own body-instruments. Since even immovable beings are declared to be eligible for initiation—one should visualize the disciple, situated within the city of breath (<s>vāyupura</s>), as being shaken and becoming light, whereby he is seen to be light on a scale. [AbhTs 15.7]

children.text: atha parokṣasya dīkṣā dvividhaś ca saḥ mṛto jīvaṃś ca // AbhTs_16.1
children.translated_text: Now, initiation of one who is absent is described. Such a person is of two kinds: dead or living. [AbhTs 16.1]

children.text: tatra kṛtaguruseva eva mṛta udvāsito vā abhicārādihato ḍimbāhato mṛtyukṣaṇoditatathāruciḥ mukhāntarāyātaśaktipāto vā tathā dīkṣya ity ājñā // AbhTs_16.2
children.translated_text: Therein, a dead person who has served the guru, or who has been expelled, or killed by hostile rites or struck down by a <s>ḍimba</s> (supernatural being), or who at the moment of death had the appropriate inclination, or who is requested through another's mouth, or [who died with] special attachment to the guru or aversion to <s>saṃsāra</s>—[is eligible]. [AbhTs 16.2]

children.text: atra ca mṛtadīkṣāyām adhivāsādi na upayujyate // AbhTs_16.3
children.translated_text: And here, in the initiation of the dead, the preliminary consecration (<s>adhivāsa</s>) and so on are not applicable. [AbhTs 16.3]

children.text: maṇḍale mantraviśeṣasaṃnidhaye yatra bahulā kriyā uttamam upakaraṇaṃ puṣpādi sthānaṃ pīṭhādi maṇḍalaṃ triśūlābjādi ākṛtiḥ dhyeyaviśeṣaḥ mantraḥ svayaṃ dīptaś ca dhyānaparasya yoginaḥ tadekabhaktisamāveśaśālino jñāninaś ca sambandhaḥ ity ete saṃnidhānahetavo yathottaram uktāḥ // AbhTs_16.4
children.translated_text: In the <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred diagram), in the proximity of the specific <s>mantra</s>, where there is abundant ritual action—the finest materials, flowers, etc.; the seat, <s>pīṭha</s> (pedestal), etc.; the <s>maṇḍala</s>— [AbhTs 16.4]

children.text: samuditatve tu kā kathā syāt iti parameśvareṇa uktam // AbhTs_16.5
children.translated_text: But when [these] are fully available, what more need be said? Thus spoke the Supreme Lord. [AbhTs 16.5]

children.text: tato devaṃ pūjayitvā tadākṛtiṃ kuśādimayīm agre sthāpayitvā gurvāsāditajñānopadeśakrameṇa tāṃ paśyet sa ca mūlādhārād udetya prasṛtasuvitatānantanāḍyadhvadaṇḍaṃ vīryeṇākramya nāsāgaganaparigataṃ vikṣipan vyāptum īṣṭe // AbhTs_16.6
children.translated_text: Then, having worshipped the deity, one should place before oneself an effigy made of <s>kuśa</s> grass or the like in its form, and should view it according to the sequence of knowledge-instruction transmitted by the guru— [AbhTs 16.6]

children.text: yāvad dhūmābhirāmapracitataraśikhājālakenādhvacakraṃ saṃchādyābhīṣṭajīvānayanam iti mahāñ jālanāmā prayogaḥ // AbhTs_16.7
children.translated_text: 'Having covered the circle of the paths with a dense network of beautiful smoke-colored flame-crests, then drawing the desired soul'—this is the great procedure called <s>Jāla</s> (the Net)— [AbhTs 16.7]

children.text: etenācchādanīyaṃ vrajati paravaśaṃ saṃmukhīnatvam ādau paścād ānīyate cet sakalam atha tato 'py adhvamadhyād yatheṣṭam // AbhTs_16.8
children.translated_text: 'The being to be covered by this first becomes subject to another's will and turns face-forward; then it is drawn in; if completely [drawn], then from that too, the path-circle'— [AbhTs 16.8]

children.text: ākṛṣṭāv uddhatau vā mṛtajanaviṣaye karṣaṇīye 'tha jīve yogaḥ śrīśaṃbhunāthāgamaparigamito jālanāmā mayoktaḥ // AbhTs_16.9
children.translated_text: 'Whether attracted or elevated, in the case of a dead person who is to be drawn, or in the case of a living one—the yoga called <s>Jāla</s> (the Net), comprehended from the scripture of the Lord <s>Śambhunātha</s>'— [AbhTs 16.9]

children.text: bahir api itthaṃ kathaṃ na bhavati ākarṣaṇādau vinābhyāsāt iti cet rāgadveṣādiyogavaśena tatpravṛttau aiśvaryāveśāyogāt // AbhTs_16.10
children.translated_text: Objection: 'How does this not work externally too—in attraction and the like—without practice?' [Reply:] Through the connection with passion, aversion, and other forces, the operation that proceeds from that— [AbhTs 16.10]

children.text: tato niyatiniyantritatvāt abhyāsādyapekṣā syād eva // AbhTs_16.11
children.translated_text: Then, because of being governed by <s>Niyati</s> (fixed destiny), there would indeed be dependence on practice and the like. [AbhTs 16.11]

children.text: iha tu anugrahātmakaparameśvaratāveśāt tathābhāvaḥ // AbhTs_16.12
children.translated_text: But here, because of the identification with the supreme Lord whose nature is grace, such [power] obtains. [AbhTs 16.12]

children.text: parameśvara eva hi guruśarīrādhiṣṭhānadvāreṇa anugrāhyān anugṛhṇāti // AbhTs_16.13
children.translated_text: For it is the Supreme Lord himself who, through the medium of governing the guru's body, bestows grace on those who are to receive grace. [AbhTs 16.13]

children.text: sa ca acintyamahimā iti uktaprāyam // AbhTs_16.14
children.translated_text: And he is of inconceivable greatness—this has been more or less stated. [AbhTs 16.14]

children.text: evaṃ jālaprayogākṛṣṭo jīvo dārbhaṃ jātīphalādi vā śarīraṃ samāviṣṭo bhavati na ca spandate manaḥpraṇādisāmagryabhāvāt tadanudhyānabalāt tu spandate 'pi tādṛśe 'pi tasmin pūrvavat prokṣaṇādisaṃskāraḥ pūrṇāhutiyojanikāntaḥ // AbhTs_16.15
children.translated_text: Thus, the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) drawn by the application of the <s>Jāla</s> (Net) procedure enters and possesses a body made of <s>darbha</s> grass, or nutmeg, etc. And it does not move, for the mind, breath, and body are in a contracted state— [AbhTs 16.15]

children.text: atra paraṃ pūrṇāhutyā tasya dārbhādyākārasya paratejasi layaḥ kartavyaḥ // AbhTs_16.16
children.translated_text: After this, by means of the <s>pūrṇāhuti</s> (complete oblation), the dissolution of that <s>darbha</s>-form body into the supreme radiance should be performed. [AbhTs 16.16]

children.text: evam uddhṛto 'sau pūrṇāhutyaiva apavṛjyate yadi svarnarakapretatiryakṣu sthitaḥ // AbhTs_16.17
children.translated_text: Thus elevated, that being is liberated by the <s>pūrṇāhuti</s> itself, whether stationed among gods, humans, hells, <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), or animals. [AbhTs 16.17]

children.text: manuṣyas tu tadaiva jñānaṃ yogaṃ dīkṣāṃ vivekaṃ vā labhate // AbhTs_16.18
children.translated_text: But a human being at that very time obtains knowledge, yoga, initiation, or discrimination. [AbhTs 16.18]

children.text: adhikāriśarīratvāt iti mṛtoddharaṇam // AbhTs_16.19
children.translated_text: Because of having a body qualified for [receiving such]. This is the elevation of the dead (<s>mṛtoddhāraṇa</s>). [AbhTs 16.19]

children.text: jīvato 'pi parokṣasya utpanne śaktipāte 'yam eva kramaḥ dārbhākṛtikalpanajīvākṛṣṭivarjam // AbhTs_16.20
children.translated_text: For a living person who is absent but upon whom <s>śaktipāta</s> has arisen, this very same procedure [applies], except for the fabrication of the <s>darbha</s> effigy and the attraction of the soul. [AbhTs 16.20]

children.text: dhyānamātropasthāpitasyaiva asya saṃskāraḥ // AbhTs_16.21
children.translated_text: The consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of this one who has been established through meditation alone. [AbhTs 16.21]

children.text: dīkṣā ca bhogabhokṣobhayadāyinī // AbhTs_16.22
children.translated_text: The initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) bestows both enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). [AbhTs 16.22]

children.text: svavāsanābalīyastvāt bhogavāsanāvicchedasya ca asaṃbhāvyamānatvāt bahubhiḥ dīkṣāyām ūrdhvaśāsanasaṃskāro balavān anyas tu tatsaṃskārāya syāt // AbhTs_16.23
children.translated_text: Because of the predominance of one's own latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), and because the interruption of the latent impression of enjoyment is not considered possible, by many [teachers] the initiation is taught with the [additional] consecration of the higher scripture— [AbhTs 16.23]

children.text: paroṣasyāpi dīkṣitasya tathaiva jñānādyāvirbhāvaḥ iti // AbhTs_16.24
children.translated_text: For one who has been initiated even in absentia, the manifestation of knowledge and the like occurs in the same way. [AbhTs 16.24]

children.text: vaiṣṇavādidakṣiṇatantrānteṣu śāsaneṣu ye sthitāḥ tadgṛhītavratā vā ye ca uttamaśāsanasthā api anadhikṛtādharaśāsanagurūpasevinaḥ te yadā śaktipātena pārameśvareṇa unmukhīkriyante tadā teṣām ayaṃ vidhiḥ tatra enaṃ kṛtopavāsam anyadine sādhāraṇamantrapūjitasya tadīyāṃ ceṣṭāṃ śrāvitasya bhagavato 'gre praveśayet tatrāsya vrataṃ gṛhītvā ambhasi kṣipet tato 'sau snāyāt tataḥ prokṣya carudantakāṣṭhābhyāṃ saṃskṛtya baddhanetraṃ praveśya sādhāraṇena mantreṇa parameśvarapūjāṃ kārayet // AbhTs_17.1
children.translated_text: Those who are established in <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> and other southern <s>Tantra</s>s and other scriptures, or those who have taken vows in those traditions, and also those who are established in the supreme scripture but are not yet qualified [for full initiation]— [AbhTs 17.1]

children.text: tataḥ sādhāraṇamantreṇa śivīkṛte agnau vrataśuddhiṃ kuryāt tanmantrasampuṭaṃ nāma kṛtvā prāyaścittaṃ śodhayāmi iti svāhāntaṃ śataṃ juhuyāt // AbhTs_17.2
children.translated_text: Then, having made the fire sacred to <s>Śiva</s> through a general <s>mantra</s>, one should perform the purification of the vow. Having formed the <s>saṃpuṭa</s> (enclosure) of that <s>mantra</s> around the name, one should perform the expiation— [AbhTs 17.2]

children.text: tato 'pi pūrṇāhutiḥ vauṣaḍantena // AbhTs_17.3
children.translated_text: Then too, the <s>pūrṇāhuti</s> (complete oblation) with [the mantra] ending in <s>vauṣaṭ</s>. [AbhTs 17.3]

children.text: tato vrateśvaram āhūya pūjayitvā tasya śivājñayā akiṃcitkaraḥ tvam asya bhava iti śrāvaṇāṃ kṛtvā taṃ tarpayitvā visṛjya agniṃ visṛjet iti liṅgoddhāraḥ // AbhTs_17.4
children.translated_text: Then, having invoked the lord of the vow (<s>vrateśvara</s>) and worshipped him, by the command of <s>Śiva</s>—'You are rendered powerless over this one'—having made this pronouncement, that [vow-lord] is dismissed. [AbhTs 17.4]

children.text: tato 'sya adhivāsādi prāgvat // AbhTs_17.5
children.translated_text: Then, the preliminary consecration (<s>adhivāsa</s>) and so on for this person, as before. [AbhTs 17.5]

children.text: dīkṣā yatheccham // AbhTs_17.6
children.translated_text: The initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) according to one's wish. [AbhTs 17.6]

children.text: svabhyastajñāninaṃ sādhakatve gurutve vā abhiṣiñcet yataḥ sarvalakṣaṇahīno 'pi jñānavān eva sādhakatve anugrahakaraṇe ca adhikṛtaḥ na anyaḥ abhiṣikto 'pi // AbhTs_18.1
children.translated_text: One should consecrate a person of well-practiced knowledge into the position of <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner) or guru, for even one devoid of all [external] marks, if endowed with knowledge, is qualified for the <s>sādhaka</s> status— [AbhTs 18.1]

children.text: svādhikārasamarpaṇe guruḥ dīkṣādi akurvan api na pratyavaiti pūrvaṃ tu pratyavāyena adhikārabandhena vidyeśapadadāyinā bandha eva asya dīkṣādyakaraṇam so 'bhiṣikto mantradevatātādātmyasiddhaye ṣāṇmāsikaṃ pratyahaṃ japahomaviśeṣapūjācaraṇena vidyāvrataṃ kuryāt tadanantaraṃ labdhatanmayībhāvo dīkṣādau adhikṛtaḥ tatra na ayogyān dīkṣeta na ca yogyaṃ pariharet dīkṣitam api jñānadāne parīkṣeta chadmagṛhītajñānam api jñātvā upekṣeta atra ca abhiṣekavibhavena devapūjādikam // AbhTs_18.2
children.translated_text: A guru who surrenders his own authority—even without performing initiation and the like—incurs no transgression. But previously, [it was held that] through the transgression of the bond of authority— [AbhTs 18.2]

children.text: atha adharaśāsanasthānāṃ gurvantānām api maraṇasamanantaraṃ mṛtoddhāroditaśaktipātayogād eva antyasaṃskārākhyāṃ dīkṣāṃ kuryāt ūrdhvaśāsanasthānām api luptasamayānām akṛtaprāyaścittānām iti parameśvarājñā // AbhTs_19.1
children.translated_text: Now, even for those established in lower scriptures, including gurus, immediately after death, through the descent of power (<s>śaktipāta</s>) arising from the elevation of the dead (<s>mṛtoddhāra</s>), the final consecration— [AbhTs 19.1]

children.text: tatra yo mṛtoddhāre vidhiḥ uktaḥ sa sarva eva śarīre kartavyaḥ pūrṇāhutyā śavaśarīradāhaḥ mūḍhānāṃ tu pratītirūḍhaye sapratyayām antyeṣṭiṃ kriyājñānayogabalāt kuryāt tatra śavaśarīre saṃhārakrameṇa mantrān nyasya jālakrameṇa ākṛṣya rodhanavedhanaghaṭṭanādi kuryāt prāṇasaṃcārakrameṇa hṛdi kaṇṭhe lalāṭe ca ity evaṃ śavaśarīraṃ kampate // AbhTs_19.2
children.translated_text: The entire procedure described for the elevation of the dead is to be performed on the body. Through the <s>pūrṇāhuti</s>, the cremation of the corpse. For deluded ones, that— [AbhTs 19.2]

children.text: tataḥ paramaśive yojanikāṃ kṛtvā tat dahet pūrṇāhutyā antyeṣṭyā śuddhānām anyeṣām api vā śrāddhadīkṣāṃ tryahaṃ turye dine māsi māsi saṃvatsare saṃvatsare kuryāt // AbhTs_19.3
children.translated_text: Then, having performed the <s>yojanikā</s> (unification) with the supreme <s>Śiva</s>, one should burn that by the <s>pūrṇāhuti</s>; the funeral rites of the pure ones; for others too, the <s>śrāddha-dīkṣā</s> (ancestor-initiation)— [AbhTs 19.3]

children.text: tatra homāntaṃ vidhiṃ kṛtvā naivedyam ekahaste kṛtvā tadīyāṃ vīryarūpāṃ śaktiṃ bhogyākārāṃ paśugatabhogyaśaktitādātmyapratipannāṃ dhyātvā parameśvare bhoktari arpayet ity evaṃ bhogyabhāve nivṛtte patir eva bhavati antyeṣṭimṛtoddharaṇaśrāddhadīkṣāṇām anyatamenāpi yadyapi kṛtārthatā tathāpi bubhukṣoḥ kriyābhūyastvaṃ phalabhūyastvāya iti sarvam ācaret // AbhTs_19.4
children.translated_text: Having performed the procedure up to the oblation, having placed the food offering in one hand, [one should visualize] his power in the form of potency (<s>vīrya</s>), in the form of the object of experience, [as existing] in the bound soul— [AbhTs 19.4]

children.text: mumukṣor api tanmayībhāvasiddhaye ayam jīvataḥ pratyaham anuṣṭhānābhyāsavat // AbhTs_19.5
children.translated_text: Even for one who desires liberation, for the attainment of identity with that [supreme], this [procedure] is like daily practice for one who is still living. [AbhTs 19.5]

children.text: tattvajñāninas tu na ko 'py ayam antyeṣṭyādiśrāddhānto vidhiḥ upayogī tanmaraṇaṃ tadvidyāsaṃtānināṃ parvadinaṃ saṃvidaṃśapūraṇāt tāvataḥ saṃtānasya ekasaṃvinmātraparamārthatvāt jīvato jñānalābhasaṃtānadivasavat // AbhTs_19.6
children.translated_text: But for one who knows the <s>tattva</s>s (principles), no procedure whatsoever—from funeral rites to <s>śrāddha</s>—is useful. His death is [a matter for] those who carry on his lineage of knowledge— [AbhTs 19.6]

children.text: sarvatra ca atra śrāddhādividhau mūrtiyāgaḥ pradhānam iti śrīsiddhāmatam tadvidhiś ca vakṣyate naimittikaprakāśane // AbhTs_19.7
children.translated_text: And in every case here, in the rites of <s>śrāddha</s> and the like, worship of the embodied form (<s>mūrti-yāga</s>) is primary—thus is the doctrine of the <s>Śrī Siddha</s> [tradition]. Its procedure will be described in the occasional rites— [AbhTs 19.7]

children.text: tatra yā dīkṣā saṃskārasiddhyai jñānayogyān prati yā ca tadaśaktān prati mokṣadīkṣā sabījā tasyāṃ kṛtāyām ājīvaṃ śeṣavartanaṃ guruḥ upadiśet // AbhTs_20.1
children.translated_text: Now, the initiation that is for the accomplishment of consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>), directed toward those qualified for knowledge, and the liberation-initiation directed toward those lacking that capacity—in the 'with-seed' (<s>sabījā</s>) [form of the latter], once performed— [AbhTs 20.1]

children.text: tatra nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyam iti trividhaṃ śeṣavartanam antyaṃ ca sādhakasyaiva tat na iha niścetavyam // AbhTs_20.2
children.translated_text: Therein, the residual practice (<s>śeṣavartana</s>) is threefold: obligatory (<s>nitya</s>), occasional (<s>naimittika</s>), and optional (<s>kāmya</s>). The final [rites] belong only to the <s>sādhaka</s>; this is not to be determined here— [AbhTs 20.2]

children.text: tatra niyatabhavaṃ nityaṃ tanmayībhāva eva naimittikaṃ tadupayogi saṃdhyopāsanaṃ pratyaham anuṣṭhānaṃ parvadinaṃ pavitrakam ityādi // AbhTs_20.3
children.translated_text: Therein, the obligatory arises necessarily by nature; the identity with that [<s>Śiva</s>] is itself [the obligatory]. The occasional is what is useful for that—the <s>sandhyā</s> worship (twilight devotions), daily practice— [AbhTs 20.3]

children.text: tad api nityaṃ svakālanaiyatyāt iti kecit // AbhTs_20.4
children.translated_text: That too is 'obligatory,' some say, because of its fixed temporal regularity. [AbhTs 20.4]

children.text: naimittikaṃ tu tacchāsanasthānām api aniyatam tadyathā gurutadvargāgamanaṃ tatparvadinaṃ jñānalābhadinam ityādikam iti kecit // AbhTs_20.5
children.translated_text: The occasional, however, is indefinite even for those established in that scriptural tradition. Such as: visiting the guru and his circle, their festival days, the day of receiving knowledge— [AbhTs 20.5]

children.text: tatra niyatapūjā saṃdhyopāsā gurupūjā parvapūjā pavitrakam iti avaśyaṃbhāvi // AbhTs_20.6
children.translated_text: Therein, the fixed worship is: <s>sandhyā</s> worship, worship of the guru, festival worship, and the <s>pavitraka</s> (purification rite)—these are obligatory. [AbhTs 20.6]

children.text: naimittikam jñānalābhaḥ śāstralābho gurutadvargagṛhāgamanaṃ tadīyajanmasaṃskāraprāyaṇadināni laukikotsavaḥ śāstravyākhyā ādimadhyāntā devatādarśanaṃ melakaṃ svapnājñā samayaniṣkṛtilābhaḥ ity etat naimittikaṃ viśeṣārcanakāraṇam // AbhTs_20.7
children.translated_text: The occasional: attainment of knowledge, attainment of scripture, visiting the house of the guru and his circle, their days of birth, consecration, death, and worldly [occasions]— [AbhTs 20.7]

children.text: tatra kṛtadīkṣākasya śiṣyasya pradhānaṃ mantraṃ savīryakaṃ saṃvittisphuraṇasāram alikhitaṃ vaktrāgamenaiva arpayet tataḥ tanmayībhāvasiddhyarthaṃ sa śiṣyaḥ saṃdhyāsu tanmayībhāvābhyāsaṃ kuryāt taddvāreṇa sarvakālaṃ tathāvidhasaṃskāralābhasiddhyarthaṃ pratyahaṃ ca parameśvaraṃ ca sthaṇḍile vā liṅge vā abhyarcayet // AbhTs_20.8
children.translated_text: For a disciple who has been initiated, the principal <s>mantra</s>, endowed with potency (<s>savīryaka</s>), whose essence is the flashing of awareness (<s>saṃvitti-sphuraṇa</s>), unwritten, coming from the mouth [of the guru]— [AbhTs 20.8]

children.text: tatra hṛdye sthaṇḍile vimalamakuravad dhyāte svam eva rūpaṃ yājyadevatācakrābhinnaṃ mūrtibimbitam iva dṛṣṭvā hṛdyapuṣpagandhāsavatarpaṇanaivedyadhūpadīpopahārastutigītavādyanṛttādinā pūjayet japet stuvīta tanmayībhāvam aśaṅkitaṃ labdhum // AbhTs_20.9
children.translated_text: There, in the heart-<s>sthaṇḍila</s> (sacred ground) meditated upon like a spotless mirror, having seen one's own form reflected as if in an image, undifferentiated from the circle of deities to be worshipped, one should worship, recite, and praise through flowers, incense, food-offerings, libations, oblations, dhūpa, lamps, offerings, hymns, songs, instrumental music, dance and the like—of the heart—in order to attain <s>tanmayībhāva</s> (identification) without hesitation.

children.text: ādarśe hi svamukham aviratam avalokayataḥ tatsvarūpaniścitiḥ acireṇaiva bhavet na cātra kaścit kramaḥ pradhānam ṛte tanmayībhāvāt // AbhTs_20.10
children.translated_text: For one who gazes continuously at one's own face in a mirror, certainty of its true nature arises very quickly; and here no sequential method is primary, apart from <s>tanmayībhāva</s> (becoming one with that).

children.text: paramantratanmayībhāvāviṣṭasya nivṛttapaśuvāsanākalaṅkasya bhaktirasānuvedhavidrutasamastapāśajālasya yat adhivasati hṛdayaṃ tad eva paramam upādeyam iti asmadguravaḥ // AbhTs_20.11
children.translated_text: For one who is possessed by identification with the supreme <s>mantra</s>, whose stain of <s>paśu</s>-impressions (bound-soul tendencies) has ceased, and whose entire net of bonds has been dissolved through the permeation of the rasa of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion)—whatever dwells in his heart, that alone is the supreme object to be accepted. Thus [say] our <s>guru</s>s.

children.text: adhiśayya pāramārthikaḥ bhāvaprasaraṃ prakāśam ullasati yā // AbhTs_20.12
children.translated_text: She who, transcending the ultimate, causes the effulgence of <s>prakāśa</s> (light) to shine forth in the flow of contemplative states,

children.text: paramāmṛtadṛktvaṃ tayārcayante rahasyavidaḥ // AbhTs_20.13
children.translated_text: as the supreme <s>amṛta</s>-vision—with her the knowers of the secret worship.

children.text: kṛtvādhāradharāṃ camatkṛtirasaprokṣākṣaṇakṣālitām āttair mānasataḥ svabhāvakusumaiḥ svāmodasaṃdohibhiḥ // AbhTs_20.14
children.translated_text: Having made the support-ground purified by the sprinkling of the rasa of <s>camatkṛti</s> (wonder), with flowers of one's own nature mentally gathered, which exude their own fragrance,

children.text: ānandāmṛtanirbharasvahṛdayānarghārghapātrakramāt tvāṃ devyā saha dehadevasadane devārcaye 'harniśam // AbhTs_20.15
children.translated_text: through the sequence of the priceless <s>arghya</s>-vessel that is one's own heart overflowing with the <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) of <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), I worship you, O <s>Deva</s>, together with the <s>Devī</s>, day and night in the temple of the body-deity.

children.text: iti ślokadvayoktam artham antar bhāvayan devatācakraṃ bhāvayet // AbhTs_20.16
children.translated_text: Inwardly contemplating the meaning expressed in these two verses, one should meditate upon the <s>devatācakra</s> (circle of deities).

children.text: tato mudrāpradarśanaṃ japaḥ tannivedanam // AbhTs_20.17
children.translated_text: Then comes the display of <s>mudrā</s>s, <s>japa</s> (recitation), and the offering thereof.

children.text: bodhyaikātmyena visarjanam // AbhTs_20.18
children.translated_text: The dismissal is through identity with awakened consciousness.

children.text: mukhyaṃ naivedyaṃ svayam aśnīyāt sarvaṃ vā jale kṣipet jalajā hi prāṇinaḥ pūrvadīkṣitāḥ carubhojanadvāreṇa iti āgamavidaḥ // AbhTs_20.19
children.translated_text: The principal <s>naivedya</s> (food-offering) one should consume oneself, or cast everything into water; for aquatic beings are creatures previously initiated who [receive] through the partaking of the sacrificial offering—so say the knowers of <s>āgama</s>.

children.text: mārjāramūṣakaśvādibhakṣaṇe tu śaṅkā janitā nirayāya iti jñānī api lokānugrahecchayā na tādṛk kuryāt lokaṃ vā parityajya āsīta iti sthaṇḍilayāgaḥ // AbhTs_20.20
children.translated_text: But regarding the consumption [of offerings] by cats, mice, dogs and the like, the doubt arises that it leads to hell; therefore even a <s>jñānin</s> (knower), out of desire to benefit the world, should not act thus, or should abandon worldly [concerns] and remain [in seclusion]. Thus [concludes] the <s>sthaṇḍila-yāga</s> (sacred-ground worship).

children.text: atha liṅge tatra na rahasyamantraiḥ liṅgaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet viśeṣāt vyaktam iti pūrvapratiṣṭhiteṣu āvāhanavisarjanakrameṇa pūjāṃ kuryāt ādhāratayā // AbhTs_20.21
children.translated_text: Now regarding the <s>liṅga</s>: one should not install a <s>liṅga</s> there with secret <s>mantra</s>s—this is especially clear. In previously installed [<s>liṅga</s>s], one should perform worship through the sequence of invocation and dismissal, using them as a support.

children.text: tatra gurudehaṃ svadehaṃ śaktidehaṃ rahasyaśāstrapustakaṃ vīrapātram akṣasūtraṃ prāharaṇaṃ bāṇīyaṃ mauktikaṃ sauvarṇaṃ puṣpagandhadravyādihṛdyavastukṛtaṃ makuraṃ vā liṅgam arcayet // AbhTs_20.22
children.translated_text: There, the <s>guru</s>'s body, one's own body, the body of <s>Śakti</s>, a manuscript of the secret scripture, a <s>vīra-pātra</s> (hero's vessel), a rosary, a weapon, an arrow, a pearl, gold, or a mirror made of flowers, incense, substances and other heart-pleasing objects—any of these may serve as the <s>liṅga</s> to be worshipped.

children.text: tatra ca ādhārabalād eva adhikādhikamantrasiddhiḥ bhavati iti pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ pradhānam ādhāraguṇānuvidhāyitvāt ca mantrāṇāṃ tatra tatra sādhye tattatpradhānam iti śāstraguravaḥ // AbhTs_20.23
children.translated_text: And there, by the very power of the support, increasingly greater <s>mantra-siddhi</s> (perfection of mantra) arises; thus each preceding [support] is primary. And since <s>mantra</s>s follow the qualities of their support, in each particular aim, each particular [support] is primary—so say the teachers of the <s>śāstra</s>.

children.text: sarvatra parameśvarābhedābhimāna eva paramaḥ saṃskāraḥ // AbhTs_20.24
children.translated_text: In all cases, the conviction of non-difference from <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) alone is the highest consecration.

children.text: atha parvavidhiḥ // AbhTs_20.25
children.translated_text: Now the rules regarding <s>parvan</s> (sacred junctures).

children.text: tatra sāmānyaṃ sāmānyasāmānyaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣo viśeṣasāmānyaṃ viśeṣo viśeṣaviśeṣaś ca iti ṣoḍhā parva // AbhTs_20.26
children.translated_text: Therein, the general, the general-general, the general-particular, the particular-general, the particular, and the particular-particular—thus <s>parvan</s> is sixfold.

children.text: pūraṇāt vidheḥ // AbhTs_20.27
children.translated_text: [This is known] from the fullness of the rule.

children.text: tatra māsi māsi prathamaṃ pañcamaṃ dinaṃ sāmānyam caturthāṣṭamanavamacaturdaśapañcadaśāni dvayor api pakṣayoḥ sāmānyasāmānyam anayor ubhayor api rāśyoḥ vakṣyamāṇatattattithyucitagrahanakṣatrayoge sāmānyaviśeṣaḥ mārgaśīrṣasya prathamarātribhāgaḥ kṛṣṇanavamyām pauṣasya tu rātrimadhyaṃ kṛṣṇanavamyām māghasya rātrimadhyaṃ śuklapañcadaśyām phālgunasya dinamadhyaṃ śukladvādaśyām caitrasya śuklatrayodaśyām vaiśākhasya kṛṣṇāṣṭamyām jyaiṣṭhasya kṛṣṇanavamyām āṣāḍhasya prathame dine śrāvaṇasya divasapūrvabhāgaḥ kṛṣṇaikādaśyām bhādrapadasya dinamadhyaṃ śuklaṣaṣṭyām āśvayujasya śuklanavamīdinam kārttikasya prathamo rātribhāgaḥ śuklanavamyām iti viśeṣaparva // AbhTs_20.28
children.translated_text: There, in each month, the first and fifth days are general; the fourth, eighth, ninth, fourteenth, and fifteenth of both fortnights are general-general. When either of these two groups coincides with the conjunction of planets and stars appropriate to the respective <s>tithi</s>s to be described, that is general-particular. The first night-watch of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> on <s>Kṛṣṇa-navamī</s>; midnight of <s>Pauṣa</s> on <s>Kṛṣṇa-navamī</s>; midnight of <s>Māgha</s> on <s>Śukla-pañcadaśī</s>; midday of <s>Phālguna</s> on <s>Śukla-dvādaśī</s>; <s>Śukla-trayodaśī</s> of <s>Caitra</s>; <s>Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī</s> of <s>Vaiśākha</s>; <s>Kṛṣṇa-navamī</s> of <s>Jyaiṣṭha</s>; the first day of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>; the first part of the day on <s>Kṛṣṇa-ekādaśī</s> of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>; midday on <s>Śukla-ṣaṣṭhī</s> of <s>Bhādrapada</s>; the day of <s>Śukla-navamī</s> of <s>Āśvayuja</s>; the first night-watch on <s>Śukla-navamī</s> of <s>Kārttika</s>—these are the particular <s>parvan</s>s.

children.text: citrācandrau maghājīvau tiṣyacandrau pūrvaphālgunībudhau śravaṇabudhau śatabhiṣakcandrau dityau rohiṇīśukrau viśākhābṛhaspatī śravaṇacandrau iti // AbhTs_20.29
children.translated_text: <s>Citrā</s>-Moon, <s>Maghā</s>-Jupiter, <s>Tiṣya</s>-Moon, <s>Pūrvaphālgunī</s>-Mercury, <s>Śravaṇa</s>-Mercury, <s>Śatabhi ṣak</s>-Moon, the two <s>Āditya</s>s, <s>Rohiṇī</s>-Venus, <s>Viśākhā</s>-Jupiter, <s>Śravaṇa</s>-Moon—these [are the respective conjunctions].

children.text: yadi mārgaśīrṣādikrameṇa yathāsaṃkhyaṃ bhavati āśvayujaṃ varjayitvā tadā viśeṣaviśeṣaḥ // AbhTs_20.30
children.translated_text: If these occur in the order beginning with <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> according to their respective count, excluding <s>Āśvayuja</s>, then that is the particular-particular [<s>parvan</s>].

children.text: anyaviśeṣaś cet anyaparvaṇi tadā tat anuparva ity āhuḥ // AbhTs_20.31
children.translated_text: If another particular [conjunction] occurs on another <s>parvan</s> day, then that is called <s>anuparvan</s> (subsidiary sacred juncture), they say.

children.text: bhagrahayoge ca na velā pradhānam // AbhTs_20.32
children.translated_text: And when there is a conjunction of planets and the like, the time-period is not primary.

children.text: tither eva viśeṣalābhāt anuyāgakālānuvṛttis tu parvadine mukhyā anuyāgaprādhānyāt parvayāgānām anuyāgo mūrtiyāgaḥ cakrayāgaḥ iti paryāyāḥ // AbhTs_20.33
children.translated_text: Since the <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) itself yields the particular benefit, the observance of the <s>anuyāga</s> (subsidiary worship) time is primary on the <s>parvan</s> day. Due to the primacy of <s>anuyāga</s>, the <s>parvan-yāga</s>s have these synonyms: <s>anuyāga</s>, <s>mūrti-yāga</s> (embodied worship), and <s>cakra-yāga</s> (circle worship).

children.text: tatra guruḥ tadvargyaḥ sasaṃtānaḥ tattvavit kanyā antyā veśyā aruṇā tattvavedinī vā iti cakrayāge mukhyapūjyāḥ viśeṣāt sāmastyena // AbhTs_20.34
children.translated_text: Therein, the <s>guru</s>, those of his group, those with their lineage, a knower of the <s>tattva</s>s, a maiden, a woman of the lowest caste, a courtesan, a woman of the <s>Aruṇā</s> [class], or a woman who knows the <s>tattva</s>s—these are the principal ones to be worshipped in the <s>cakra-yāga</s>, especially when taken collectively.

children.text: tatra madhye guruḥ tadāvaraṇakrameṇa gurvādisamayyantaṃ vīraḥ śaktiḥ iti krameṇa ity evaṃ cakrasthityā vā paṅktisthityā vā āsīta tato gandhadhūpapuṣpādibhiḥ krameṇa pūjayet tataḥ pātraṃ sadāśivarūpaṃ dhyātvā śaktyamṛtadhyātena āsavena pūrayitvā tatra bhoktrīṃ śaktiṃ śivatayā pūjayitvā tayaiva devatācakratarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā naraśaktiśivātmakatritayamelakaṃ dhyātvā āvaraṇāvataraṇakrameṇa mokṣabhogaprādhānyaṃ bahir antaś ca tarpaṇaṃ kuryāt punaḥ pratisaṃcaraṇakrameṇa evaṃ pūrṇaṃ bhramaṇaṃ cakraṃ puṣṇāti // AbhTs_20.35
children.translated_text: There, the <s>guru</s> sits in the center; in the order of successive circles, from the <s>guru</s> to the <s>samayī</s> (initiate), [seated as] <s>vīra</s> (hero) and <s>śakti</s> alternately—thus in circular arrangement or in rows. Then one should worship sequentially with incense, perfume, flowers and the like. Then, having meditated upon the vessel as the form of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, having filled it with liquor consecrated by meditation on <s>Śakti-amṛta</s>, having worshipped the female partner (<s>Śakti</s>) therein as <s>Śiva</s>, having thereby performed the <s>tarpaṇa</s> (satisfaction) of the circle of deities, meditating on the threefold union of <s>nara</s> (individual), <s>śakti</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>, one should perform <s>tarpaṇa</s> both externally and internally in the order of descending through the circles, with predominance of either liberation or enjoyment. Then again in the order of reabsorption—thus the complete revolution of the <s>cakra</s> is nourished.

children.text: tatra ādhāre viśvamayaṃ pātraṃ sthāpayitvā devatācakraṃ tarpayitvā svātmānaṃ vanditena tena tarpayet pātrābhāve bhadraṃ vellitaśuktiḥ vā dakṣahastena pātrākāraṃ bhadraṃ dvābhyām uparigatadakṣiṇābhyāṃ niḥsaṃdhīkṛtābhyām vellitaśuktiḥ patadbhiḥ bindubhiḥ vetālaguhyakāḥ saṃtuṣyanti dhārayā bhairavaḥ atra praveśo na kasyacit deyaḥ pramādāt praviṣṭasya vicāraṃ na kuryāt kṛtvā punar dviguṇaṃ cakrayāgaṃ kuryāt tato 'vadaṃśān bhojanādīn ca agre yatheṣṭaṃ vikīryeta guptagṛhe vā saṃketābhidhānavarjaṃ devatāśabdena sarvān yojayet iti vīrasaṃkarayāgaḥ // AbhTs_20.36
children.translated_text: There, having placed the vessel containing the universe upon the support, having satisfied the circle of deities, one should satisfy oneself with the consecrated [offering]. In the absence of a vessel, a <s>bhadra</s> (auspicious cup), a conch shell, or [a cup formed by] the right hand in the shape of a vessel—the <s>bhadra</s> with both [hands], with the right one placed above, sealed together—or the conch shell; with falling drops the <s>vetāla</s>s and <s>guhyaka</s>s are satisfied; with a stream, <s>Bhairava</s>. No one should be admitted into this [rite]; for one who has entered by mistake, no inquiry should be made; [but] having done so, one should perform double the <s>cakra-yāga</s>. Thereafter, portions of food and the like should be distributed as desired, or in a secret dwelling, avoiding code-names, one should designate everyone by the word '<s>devatā</s>.' Thus [concludes] the <s>vīra-saṃkara-yāga</s> (hero-confluence worship).

children.text: tato 'nte dakṣiṇātāmbūlavastrādibhiḥ tarpayet iti pradhānatamo 'yaṃ mūrtiyāgaḥ // AbhTs_20.37
children.translated_text: Then at the end, one should satisfy [them] with gifts, betel, garments and the like from the right. This is the most principal <s>mūrti-yāga</s> (embodied worship).

children.text: adṛṣṭamaṇḍalo 'pi mūrtiyāgena parvadināni pūjayan varṣād eva putrakoktaṃ phalam eti vinā saṃdhyānuṣṭhānādibhiḥ iti vṛddhānāṃ bhogināṃ strīṇāṃ vidhir ayam śaktipāte sati upadeṣṭavyo guruṇā // AbhTs_20.38
children.translated_text: Even one who has not seen the <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred diagram), by worshipping on <s>parvan</s> days through the <s>mūrti-yāga</s> alone, attains within a year the fruit described for the <s>putraka</s> (son-initiate), without the <s>saṃdhyā</s>-observances and the like. This is the rule for the elderly, for householders, and for women, and the <s>guru</s> should instruct them in this when <s>śaktipāta</s> has occurred.

children.text: atha pavitrakavidhiḥ // AbhTs_20.39
children.translated_text: Now the procedure for the <s>pavitraka</s> (purificatory thread rite).

children.text: sa ca śrīratnamālātriśiromataśrīsiddhāmatādau vidhipūrvakaḥ pārameśvarājñāpūrakaś ca uktaṃ caitat śrītantrāloke vinā pavitrakeṇa sarvaṃ niṣphalam iti // AbhTs_20.40
children.translated_text: This is described with proper ritual in the <s>Śrīratnamālā</s>, <s>Triśiromata</s>, <s>Śrīsiddhāmata</s> and other [texts], and it fulfills the command of <s>Parameśvara</s>. It has been stated in the <s>Śrītantrāloka</s>: 'Without the <s>pavitraka</s>, everything is fruitless.'

children.text: tatra āṣāḍhaśuklāt kulapūrṇimādināntaṃ kāryaṃ pavitrakam tatra kārttikakṛṣṇapañcadaśī kulacakraṃ nityācakraṃ pūrayati iti śrīnityātantravidaḥ // AbhTs_20.41
children.translated_text: There, from the bright fortnight of <s>Āṣāḍha</s> until the <s>kulapūrṇimā</s> and similar [dates], the <s>pavitraka</s> should be performed. The full-moon day of <s>Kārttika-Kṛṣṇa</s> [<s>pañcadaśī</s>] fulfills the <s>kulacakra</s> and <s>nityācakra</s>—so say the knowers of the <s>Śrīnityātantra</s>.

children.text: māghaśuklapañcadaśī iti śrībhairavakulormividaḥ // AbhTs_20.42
children.translated_text: The bright fifteenth of <s>Māgha</s>—so say the knowers of the <s>Śrībhairavakūlormī</s>.

children.text: dakṣiṇāyanāntapañcadaśī iti śrītantrasadbhāvavidaḥ // AbhTs_20.43
children.translated_text: The fifteenth at the end of the southern solstice—so say the knowers of the <s>Śrītantrasadbhāva</s>.

children.text: tatra vibhavena devaṃ pūjayitvā āhutyā tarpayitvā pavitrakaṃ dadyāt sauvarṇamuktāratnaviracitāt prabhṛti paṭasūtrakārpāsakuśagarbhāntam api kuryāt // AbhTs_20.44
children.translated_text: There, having worshipped the deity with [appropriate] splendor and having satisfied [the deity] with oblations, one should give the <s>pavitraka</s>. One may make it from gold, pearls, and gems down to [a cord of] silk thread, cotton, or <s>kuśa</s>-grass.

children.text: tac ca tattvasaṃkhyagranthikaṃ padakalābhuvanavarṇamantrasaṃkhyagranthi ca jānvantam ekaṃ nābhyantam aparaṃ kaṇṭhāntam anyat śirasi anyat iti catvāri pavitrakāṇi devāya gurave ca samastādhvaparipūrṇatadrūpabhāvanena dadyāt śeṣebhya ekam iti // AbhTs_20.45
children.translated_text: And it should have knots equal to the number of <s>tattva</s>s, and knots [also] equal to the number of <s>pada</s>s, <s>kalā</s>s, <s>bhuvana</s>s, <s>varṇa</s>s, and <s>mantra</s>s. One [reaching] to the knees, another to the navel, another to the throat, another on the head—thus four <s>pavitraka</s>s. One should give them to the deity and the <s>guru</s> through meditation on their form as the fulfillment of the entire <s>adhvan</s> (cosmic path). One [is given] to the rest.

children.text: tato mahotsavaḥ kāryaḥ cāturmāsyaṃ saptadinaṃ tridinaṃ ca iti mukhyānvāpatkalpāḥ sati vibhave māsi māsi pavitrakam atha vā caturṣu māseṣu atha vā sakṛt tadakaraṇe prāyaścittaṃ japet jñānī api sambhavadvitto 'pi akaraṇe pratyavaiti lobhopahitajñānākaraṇe jñānanindāpatteḥ // AbhTs_20.46
children.translated_text: Then a great festival should be performed—lasting four months, seven days, or three days—these being the primary, secondary, and emergency alternatives. If one has the means, [one should offer] the <s>pavitraka</s> every month; or else every four months; or else just once. For not performing it, one should recite [<s>mantra</s>s] as expiation. Even a <s>jñānin</s> who has the means, if he does not perform it, falls back—because non-performance out of greed, even when knowledge is present, incurs the blame of disrespecting knowledge.

children.text: yadā prāpyāpi vijñānaṃ dūṣitaṃ parameśaśāsanaṃ tadā prāyaścittī // AbhTs_20.47
children.translated_text: When knowledge, even though attained, corrupts the command of <s>Parameśa</s> (the Supreme Lord), then [one becomes] subject to expiation.

children.text: iti vacanāt // AbhTs_20.48
children.translated_text: Thus from this statement.

children.text: ity eṣa pavitrakavidhiḥ // AbhTs_20.49
children.translated_text: This is the procedure for the <s>pavitraka</s>.

children.text: jñānalābhādau laukikotsavānte 'pi sarvatra saṃvidullāsādhikyaṃ devatācakrasaṃnidhiḥ viśeṣato bhavati iti tathāvidhādhikyaparyālocanayā tathāvidham eva viśeṣam anuyāgādau kuryāt // AbhTs_20.50
children.translated_text: At the attainment of knowledge and at the conclusion of worldly festivals and everywhere [else], there is an abundance of the blossoming of consciousness, especially in the presence of the <s>devatācakra</s> (circle of deities). Therefore, through the consideration of such an increase, one should perform such special [rites] in the <s>anuyāga</s> and other [observances].

children.text: atha vyākhyāvidhiḥ // AbhTs_20.51
children.translated_text: Now the procedure for teaching (<s>vyākhyā</s>).

children.text: sarvaśāstrasampūrṇaṃ guruṃ vyākhyārtham abhyarthayeta so 'pi svaśiṣyāya paraśiṣyāyāpi vā samucitasaṃskārocitaṃ śāstraṃ vyācakṣīta adharaśāsanasthāyāpi karuṇāvaśāt īśvarecchāvaicitryodbhāvitaśaktipātasambhāvanābhāvitahṛdayo vyācakṣīta marmopadeśavarjam // AbhTs_20.52
children.translated_text: One should request a <s>guru</s> who is accomplished in all <s>śāstra</s>s for the purpose of exposition. He too, whether for his own disciple or another's, should expound the scripture appropriate to the proper consecration. Even for one established in a lower [tradition's] teaching, out of compassion, with a heart that contemplates the possibility of <s>śaktipāta</s> arising from the variety of the Lord's will, he should expound—except for the secret essential instructions.

children.text: tatra nimnāsanasthitebhyaḥ tatparebhyo niyamitavāṅmanaḥkāyebhyo vyākhyā kriyamāṇā phalavatī bhavati prathamaṃ gandhādiliptāyāṃ bhuvi ullikhya saṃkalpya vā padmādhāraṃ caturaśraṃ padmatrayaṃ padmamadhye vāgīśīṃ vāmadakṣiṇayoḥ gaṇapatigurū ca pūjayet ādhārapadme vyākhyeyakalpadevatām // AbhTs_20.53
children.translated_text: There, the exposition delivered to those seated on low seats, who are superior [in qualification], with speech, mind, and body restrained, becomes fruitful. First, on the ground anointed with incense and the like, having drawn or mentally established a square lotus-base, three lotuses, and in the middle of the lotus [having placed] <s>Vāgīśī</s> (the Goddess of Speech), and on the left and right <s>Gaṇapati</s> and the <s>Guru</s>, one should worship them. On the base-lotus, [one should worship] the deity of the scripture being expounded.

children.text: tataḥ sāmānyārghapātrayogena cakraṃ tarpayet tato vyācakṣīta sūtravākyapaṭalagrantham pūrvāparāviruddhaṃ kurvan tantrāvṛttiprasaṅgasamuccayavikalpādiśāstranyāyaucityena pūrvaṃ pakṣaṃ samyak ghaṭayitvā samyak ca dūṣayan sādhyaṃ sādhayan tātparyavṛttiṃ pradarśayan paṭalāntaṃ vyācakṣīta nādhikam tatrāpi vastvante vastvante tarpaṇaṃ pūjanam iti yāvad vyākhyāsamāptiḥ // AbhTs_20.54
children.translated_text: Then, by means of the general <s>arghya-pātra</s> (offering vessel), one should satisfy the <s>cakra</s>. Then one should expound the text—<s>sūtra</s>, sentence, word, and section—making it consistent from beginning to end, with propriety according to the methods of <s>śāstra</s> such as <s>tantra</s> (principal statement), <s>āvṛtti</s> (repetition), <s>prasaṅga</s> (contextual relevance), <s>samuccaya</s> (aggregation), and <s>vikalpa</s> (alternative). Having properly constructed the prior position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) and properly refuting it, establishing the thesis and demonstrating the purport, one should expound up to the end of the section, not beyond. Therein also, at each topic's conclusion, [there should be] <s>tarpaṇa</s> (satisfaction offering) and worship—until the completion of the exposition.

children.text: tato 'pi pūjayitvā vidyāpīṭhaṃ visarjya upalipya agādhe tat kṣepayet // AbhTs_20.55
children.translated_text: Then, having worshipped and dismissed the <s>vidyāpīṭha</s> (seat of knowledge), having re-anointed [the ground], one should cast it into deep water.

children.text: iti vyākhyāvidhiḥ // AbhTs_20.56
children.translated_text: This is the procedure for teaching.

children.text: atha samayaniṣkṛtiḥ // AbhTs_20.57
children.translated_text: Now the rules regarding transgression (<s>samaya-niṣkṛti</s>).

children.text: yady api tattvajñānaniṣṭhasya prāyaścittādi na kiṃcit tathāpi caryāmātrād eva mokṣabhāginaḥ tān anugrahītum ācāravartanīṃ darśayet // AbhTs_20.58
children.translated_text: Although for one established in the knowledge of <s>tattva</s>s there is no expiation or the like, nevertheless, for those who attain liberation through mere observance alone, to benefit them one should demonstrate the path of conduct.

children.text: atattvajñānī tu caryaikāyattabhogamokṣaḥ samayollaṅghane kṛte prāyaścittam akurvan varṣaśataṃ kravyādo bhavatīti iti prāyaścittavidhiḥ vaktavyaḥ tatra strīvadhe prāyaścittaṃ nāsti anyatra tu balābalaṃ jñātvā akhaṇḍāṃ bhagavatīṃ mālinīm ekavārāt prabhṛti trilakṣāntam āvartayet yāvat śaṅkāvicyutiḥ bhavati tadante viśeṣapūjā tatrāpi cakrayāgaḥ sa hi sarvatra śeṣabhūtaḥ // AbhTs_20.59
children.translated_text: But one who does not know the <s>tattva</s>s, whose enjoyment and liberation depend solely on observance—if he has committed a transgression of the vows and does not perform expiation, he becomes a flesh-eating spirit for a hundred years. Thus the procedure for expiation must be stated. Therein, for the killing of a woman there is no expiation. But in other cases, having assessed the gravity, one should recite the undivided <s>Bhagavatī Mālinī</s> [<s>mantra</s>] from one time up to three hundred thousand times, until the doubt-free state is attained. At the conclusion of that, special worship [is performed]; and therein also the <s>cakra-yāga</s>, for that is the culmination of everything.

children.text: iti samayaniṣkṛtividhiḥ // AbhTs_20.60
children.translated_text: This is the procedure for transgression-remedy.

children.text: atha gurupūjāvidhiḥ // AbhTs_20.61
children.translated_text: Now the procedure for <s>guru-pūjā</s> (worship of the teacher).

children.text: sarvayāgānteṣu upasaṃhṛte yāge aparedyuḥ gurupūjāṃ kuryāt pūrvaṃ hi sa vidhyaṅgatayā toṣito na tu prādhānyena iti tāṃ prādhānyena akurvan adhikārabandhena baddho bhavati // AbhTs_20.62
children.translated_text: At the conclusion of all [other] worship rites, having completed the worship, one should perform <s>guru-pūjā</s> on the following day. For previously he was satisfied incidentally, as part of the ritual, and not as the principal [object of worship]. Therefore, one who does not perform it as the principal [rite] remains bound by the bond of [ritual] obligation.

children.text: iti tāṃ sarvathā caret // AbhTs_20.63
children.translated_text: Thus one should perform it in all ways.

children.text: tatra svāstikaṃ maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā tatra sauvarṇaṃ pīṭhaṃ dattvā tatra samastam adhvānaṃ pūjayitvā tatpīṭhaṃ tena adhiṣṭhāpya tasmai pūjāṃ kṛtvā tarpaṇaṃ bhojanaṃ dakṣiṇām ātmānam iti nivedya naivedyocchiṣṭaṃ prārthya vanditvā svayaṃ prāśya cakrapūjāṃ kuryāt // AbhTs_20.64
children.translated_text: There, having made a <s>svastika maṇḍala</s>, having placed upon it a golden seat, having worshipped the entire <s>adhvan</s> (cosmic path) thereon, having seated [the <s>guru</s>] upon that seat, having performed worship to him, [having offered] <s>tarpaṇa</s>, food, gifts, and oneself—having thus made an offering—requesting the remnants of the <s>naivedya</s>, bowing, partaking of them oneself, one should then perform the <s>cakra-pūjā</s> (circle worship).

children.text: ita gurupūjāvidhiḥ // AbhTs_20.65
children.translated_text: This is the procedure for <s>guru-pūjā</s>.

children.text: evaṃ samastaṃ nityaṃ naimittikaṃ karma nirūpitam // AbhTs_21.1
children.translated_text: Thus all the daily and occasional rites have been described.

children.text: adhunā asyaiva āgamasya prāmāṇyam ucyate // AbhTs_21.2
children.translated_text: Now the authority (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) of this very <s>āgama</s> (scripture) is stated.

children.text: tatra saṃvinmātramaye viśvasmin saṃvidi ca vimarśātmikāyāṃ vimarśasya ca śabdanātmakatāyāṃ siddhāyāṃ sakalajaganniṣṭhavastunaḥ tadgatasya ca karmaphalasambandhavaicitryasya yat vimarśanaṃ tad eva śāstram iti parameśvarasvabhāvābhinna eva samastaḥ śāstrasaṃdarbho vastuta ekaphalaprāpakaḥ ekādhikāryuddeśenaiva tatra tu parameśvaraniyatiśaktimahimnaiva bhāge bhāge rūḍhiḥ lokānām iti // AbhTs_21.3
children.translated_text: Therein, since the entire universe consists of nothing but awareness (<s>saṃvit</s>), and awareness is of the nature of reflective consciousness (<s>vimarśa</s>), and reflective consciousness has been established as having the nature of articulation (<s>śabdana</s>) — the reflective awareness of the real nature of all things established in the entire universe, and of the diversity of the relation between action and its fruit residing therein, is itself scripture (<s>śāstra</s>). Thus the entire corpus of scripture is in reality non-different from the nature of the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), and in truth produces a single fruit. But by the majesty of the Supreme Lord's power of necessity (<s>niyati-śakti</s>), beings are established in [only] portions [of it]. [AbhTs 21.3]

children.text: kecit māyocitabhedaparāmarśātmani vedāgamādiśāstre rūḍhāḥ anye tathāvidha eva mokṣābhimānena sāṃkhyavaiṣṇavaśāstrādau pare tu viviktaśivasvabhāvāmarśanasāre śaivasiddhāntādau anye sarvamayaparameśvaratāmarśanasāre mataṃgādiśāstre kecit tu viralaviralāḥ samastāvacchedavandhyasvātantryānandaparamārthasaṃvinmayaparameśvarasvarūpāmarśanātmani śrītrikaśāstrakrame kecit tu pūrvapūrvatyāgakrameṇa laṅghanena vā ity evam ekaphalasiddhiḥ ekasmād eva āgamāt // AbhTs_21.4
children.translated_text: Some are established in the Veda-<s>Āgama</s> scriptures, whose reflective awareness involves differentiation appropriate to <s>Māyā</s>; others in similar [scriptures] with the pretension of liberation, such as the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, and other scriptures; others yet in [scriptures] whose essence is the reflective awareness of the distinct nature of <s>Śiva</s>, such as the <s>Śaiva Siddhānta</s>; others in [scriptures] whose essence is the reflective awareness of the Supreme Lord as pervading everything, such as the <s>Mataṅga</s> and other scriptures; but very rare are those [established] in the succession of the glorious <s>Trika</s> scripture, whose essence is the reflective awareness of the true nature of the Supreme Lord as consisting of awareness whose ultimate reality is the bliss of autonomy free from all limitation. Some [attain] the accomplishment of the one fruit from a single scripture, progressively renouncing the earlier [teachings] or by leaping over [them]. [AbhTs 21.4]

children.text: bhedavāde 'pi samastāgamānām ekeśvarakāryatve 'pi prāmāṇyaṃ tāvat avasthitam prāmāṇyanibandhanasya ekadeśasaṃvādasya avigītatāyā anidaṃtāpravṛtteś ca tulyatvāt parasparabādho viṣayabhedāt akiṃcitkaraḥ // AbhTs_21.5
children.translated_text: Even in the view of difference, the validity of all scriptures is established, since they are all the product of one Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>). For the foundation of validity — namely, agreement with a portion [of reality] — is undisputed, and the enterprise does not proceed through 'this-ness.' Mutual contradiction is ineffective because of the difference of subject matter. [AbhTs 21.5]

children.text: brahmahananatanniṣedhavat saṃskārabhedaḥ saṃskārātiśayaḥ tadabhāve kvacit anadhikṛtatvam iti samānam āśramabhedavat phalotkarṣāc ca utkarṣaḥ tatraiva upaniṣadbhāgavat bhinnakartṛkatve 'pi sarvasarvajñakṛtatvam atra saṃbhāvyate taduktatadatiriktayuktārthayogāt nityatve 'pi āgamānāṃ prasiddhiḥ tāvat avaśyopagamyā anvayavyatirekādhyakṣādīnāṃ tatprāmāṇyasya tanmūlatvāt satyaṃ rajataṃ paśyāmi iti hi sauvarṇikādiparaprasiddhyaiva prasiddhir eva āgamaḥ sā kācit dṛṣṭaphalā bubhukṣito bhuṅkte iti bālasya prasiddhita eva tatra tatra pravṛttiḥ nānvayavyatirekābhyāṃ tadā tayoḥ abhāvāt yauvanāvasthāyāṃ tadbhāvo 'pi akiṃcitkaraḥ prasiddhiṃ tu mūlīkṛtya so 'stu kasmaicit kāryāya kācit adṛṣṭavaidehyaprakṛtilayapuruṣakaivalyaphaladā kācit śivasamānatvaphaladā kācit aikyaparyavasāyinī sā ca pratyekam anekavidhā ity evaṃ bahutaraprasiddhipūrṇe jagati yo yādṛśo bhaviṣyan sa tādṛśīm eva prasiddhiṃ balād eva hṛdayaparyavasāyinīm abhimanyate // AbhTs_21.6
children.translated_text: Like [the seeming contradiction between] the killing of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and its prohibition — it is a difference of purificatory rite (<s>saṃskāra</s>); an excess of purificatory rite; in the absence thereof, non-qualification in some cases — this is the same as [the differences of] stages of life (<s>āśrama</s>). And there is hierarchy because of hierarchy of fruit; therein, like the <s>Upaniṣad</s> portion [within the Veda]. Even when there are different authors, the authorship by the all-knowing [Lord] of everything is conceivable here, because of the presence of both stated and additional reasoned meanings. Even regarding the eternality of scriptures, established tradition (<s>prasiddhi</s>) must necessarily be accepted, since the validity of co-presence-and-co-absence, direct perception, etc. is grounded in it. For indeed, 'I truly see silver' — validity rests precisely on the established tradition of the goldsmith and others. That established tradition is of various kinds: some have visible results — a hungry person eats, and a child's activity in that regard is based on established tradition alone, not on co-presence and co-absence, since those do not exist then; and even in youth, their presence is ineffective. But taking established tradition as the basis — let that be for some purpose. Some [traditions] bestow fruits of unseen merit, separation from <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), dissolution in <s>Puruṣa</s>, and <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation); some bestow the fruit of equality with <s>Śiva</s>; some culminate in oneness. And each of these is manifold. Thus, in the world full of diverse established traditions, whoever is destined to become whatever kind [of person], that one embraces precisely that established tradition which forcefully settles in the heart. [AbhTs 21.6]

children.text: iti riktasya jantoḥ atiriktā vācoyuktiḥ tāsāṃ kāṃcana prasiddhiṃ pramāṇīkurvatā abhyupagantavyam eva āgamaprāmāṇyam iti sa āgama āśrayaṇīyo yatra utkṛṣṭaṃ phalam ity alam anyena // AbhTs_21.7
children.translated_text: Thus, for the empty creature, there is excessive cleverness of speech. By one who would validate any particular established tradition, the validity of scripture (<s>āgama</s>) must necessarily be accepted. Therefore, one should resort to that scripture in which the fruit is supreme — enough of the rest. [AbhTs 21.7]

children.text: saṃvitprakāśaparamārthatayā yathaiva bhāty āmṛśaty api tatheti vivecayantaḥ // AbhTs_21.8
children.translated_text: Just as [reality] shines as having the ultimate nature of the light of awareness, so too it reflectively apprehends — those who discern thus, [AbhTs 21.8]

children.text: santaḥ samastamayacitpratibhāvimarśasāraṃ samāśrayata śāstram anuttarātma // AbhTs_21.9
children.translated_text: O virtuous ones, resort to the scripture whose essence is the unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>), the core of which is the reflective awareness of the flash of consciousness that pervades everything. [AbhTs 21.9]

children.text: jissa daḍhapasiddhighaḍie vavahāre soi asmi ṇīsaṃko // AbhTs_21.10
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] In the practical activity fashioned by firm established conviction, one is indeed without doubt — [AbhTs 21.10]

children.text: taha hohi jahuttiṇa pasiddhirūḍhie paramasivo // AbhTs_21.11
children.translated_text: So too, established in the firm conviction transcending [ordinary] birth, one becomes the supreme <s>Śiva</s>. [AbhTs 21.11]

children.text: nijadṛḍhaprasiddhighaṭite vyavahāre loka asti niḥśaṅkaḥ // AbhTs_21.12
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit:] In practical activity fashioned by one's own firm conviction, the world is indeed without doubt; [AbhTs 21.12]

children.text: tadā bhavati janottīrṇaprasiddhirūḍhaḥ paramaśivaḥ // AbhTs_21.13
children.translated_text: Then one becomes the supreme <s>Śiva</s>, established in the firm conviction that transcends [ordinary] birth. [AbhTs 21.13]

children.text: atha samastā iyam upāsā samunmiṣattādṛśadṛḍhavāsanārūḍhān adhikāriṇaḥ prati śrīmatkaulikaprakriyayā nirūpyate tatra uktaṃ yogasaṃcārādau ānandaṃ brahma taddehe tridhauṣṭyāntyavyavasthitam // AbhTs_22.1
children.translated_text: Now, this entire worship is explained through the glorious <s>Kaulika</s> (Kaula) procedure for qualified practitioners who have ascended to firm impressions of such nature as they arise. Therein, it is said in the <s>Yogasaṃcāra</s> and other [texts]: '<s>Ānanda</s> (bliss) is <s>Brahman</s>; in that body it is established in three [locations]: the lips, the end, and the final. [AbhTs 22.1]'

children.text: abrahmacāriṇas tasya tyāgād ānandavarjitāḥ // AbhTs_22.2
children.translated_text: 'Those who do not practice the conduct of <s>Brahman</s>/bliss (<s>brahmacarya</s>) are devoid of bliss through its abandonment. [AbhTs 22.2]'

children.text: ānandakṛtrimāhāravarjaṃ cakrasya yājakāḥ // AbhTs_22.3
children.translated_text: 'The worshippers of the <s>cakra</s> (circle), except for the nourishment made of <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) — [AbhTs 22.3]'

children.text: dvaye 'pi narake ghore tasmād enāṃ sthitiṃ bhajet // AbhTs_22.4
children.translated_text: 'In both [cases], one falls into terrible hell; therefore one should worship this state. [AbhTs 22.4]'

children.text: tad anayā sthityā kulayāgaḥ sa ca ṣoḍhā bāhye śaktau svadehe yāmale prāṇe saṃvidi ca iti // AbhTs_22.5
children.translated_text: By this state, the <s>Kula</s> worship (<s>kulayāga</s>) is sixfold: external, in the <s>Śakti</s> (consort), in one's own body, in the <s>yāmala</s> (paired), in the breath, and in awareness. [AbhTs 22.5]

children.text: tatra ca uttara uttara utkṛṣṭaḥ pūrvaḥ pūrvas tadrucyartham // AbhTs_22.6
children.translated_text: And therein, each successive [form] is superior; each preceding one serves to provide the taste [of the practice for that level]. [AbhTs 22.6]

children.text: siddhikāmasya dvitīyaturyapañcamāḥ sarvathā nirvartyāḥ ṣaṣṭhas tu mumukṣoḥ mukhyaḥ tasyāpi dvitīyādyā naimittike yathāsambhavam anuṣṭheyā eva vidhipūraṇārthaṃ ca // AbhTs_22.7
children.translated_text: For one who desires <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural powers), the second, fourth, and fifth must be accomplished in all cases. But the sixth is primary for one who desires liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>). Even for that one, the second and following [forms] should be performed at occasional [rites], as circumstances permit, and for the sake of completing the ritual requirements. [AbhTs 22.7]

children.text: tatra bāhyaṃ sthaṇḍilam ānandapūrṇaṃ vīrapātram aruṇaḥ paṭaḥ pūrvoktam api vā liṅgādi // AbhTs_22.8
children.translated_text: Therein, the external [support] is the altar (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>), the vessel filled with bliss (<s>ānandapūrṇa vīrapātra</s>), the red cloth, or as previously stated, the <s>liṅga</s> and the like. [AbhTs 22.8]
